rows.original: "So what did you do before you came here? How did you happen upon this orchard?" you ask. "Me? Well, um... it was so long ago..." Callie says, closing her eyes and rubbing her fingers on her temples. "I remember a village in the mountains. I can't recall if it had a name, the mountain range or my village, but neither were very big. I don't know that I'd seen an outsider at all before coming here." She opens her eyes and looks out one of the windows. "I vividly remember coming here. I was hunting sheep, since we needed wool for a harsh winter. It was... more trees than I'd seen in my whole life, and the apples were so pretty. I'd eaten so many before I even knew what was happening," she says, closing her eyes again as she remembers. "When I turned around, my familiar hunting paths were gone. There was only the fence, and an unbreachable wall of darkness." "That was it? And you were trapped?" "Yeah. I, uh, haven't been able to leave. It's not like I haven't thought about it, when others came, especially the first couple times. I just know, though, that it's impossible. I don't even feel worse when I get close to the fence. With the others, particularly the ones who eat too much, I can see it draining them as they try to get away. I don't get that. The fence is just a wall to me." "Was there anyone here before you?" "Dunno. Not as far as I saw. Not even any skulls. The lodge wasn't here either, built that myself." "You did a good job of it. It looks very homey," you say, looking around at the interior "Thank you, I tried. Hunted all the sheep and ox that make up the rugs and bedding, too. Most were charmed by the apples by the time I found them, but still," she says, rubbing the back of her neck. "Yeah, still. Even if you don't think the hunt is as impressive, the craftsmanship definitely is." "Thanks." You take a moment to look around at the carved wood and the oldest-looking pieces of furniture that adorn the lodge interior. "Is that trip all you remember? I don't mean to pry, if it's something that hurts to touch on, but is any of this in the style of your home?" "Yes, actually! It's really just names I've forgotten. I still remember my parents' faces, and others from the village, but names and places just kind of slip away. I think it's part of the compulsion, rather than any kind of memory overload. The same thing happens with new people. At least, after they've gone for good." "That sounds... slightly less terrifying than I would have thought," you say. "Ha, yeah... I think the curse stops me from feeling super strongly about it, to be honest. At least, once that forgetful period sets in. It does kinda terrify me, but I'm glad to have these moments where I can talk honestly about it. That probably pushes it back toward terrifying..." "Even if it does, I'm glad I can be here to help you remember for a while," you say, [callie.fucked |taking hold of one of her hands. |tapping your fingers on the table. ] She smiles, genuine and warm. "Me too. Anything else on your mind?"
rows.translation: 那么，在来到这里之前，你都做了些什么呢？又是如何做到的呢？ 你 你是怎么偶然发现这个果园的？”你问道。 “我吗？嗯，那个……已经是很久以前的事了……”卡莉闭上眼睛，用手部指揉着太阳穴说道，“我记得在山里有一个村庄。我想不起来它有没有名字，也不记得那是哪座山脉里的村庄，但反正那个村庄和那片山脉都不大。在我来到这里之前，我想我从来没见过外人。 她睁开眼睛，望向窗外。 “我清楚地记得自己当时是来这里猎羊的——因为那个严冬我们需要羊毛。这里的树木数量之多，是我这辈子见过的最多的一次，那些苹果也漂亮极了。我在不知不觉中吃了很多……”她回忆着，又闭上了眼睛。“当我转过身来时，那些我熟悉的猎羊小路已经不见了。只剩下那道围栏，以及一堵无形的、黑暗的墙。 就只是这样？你就被困在那里了？” “是的。我，呃，一直没能离开。其他人来的时候，尤其是刚开始的几次，我其实也想过要逃跑，但我知道那是不可能的。即使靠近那道栅栏，我也不会感到有什么不适。而对于那些吃得太多的家伙来说，他们试图逃跑的时候显然会消耗大量的体力，但我却完全没有这种感觉。对我来说，那道栅栏只不过是一堵墙而已。 在你来之前，这里还有其他人吗？” “不知道。就我所见，并没有其他人。甚至连骷髅都没有。这个小屋也是我亲手部建造的。” “你做得真不错，看起来非常温馨。”你环顾着屋内说道。 “谢谢，我尽力了。那些用来制作地毯和床铺的羊和牛，也都是我亲自捕猎的。当我找到它们的时候，大多数都已经被苹果吸引了，不过……”她说着，揉了揉后颈。 是的，确实如此。即使你认为这次狩猎并没有那么令人印象深刻，但这些工艺确实非常精湛。” “谢谢。” 你花了一些时间仔细观察小屋内部那些雕刻精美的木制品以及那些看起来最为古老的家具。 难道你只记得那次旅行吗？我并不是想打探你的隐私，如果这个话题会让你感到不适的话……不过，这些地方的名字有没有什么与你家乡的风格相似之处呢？” “是的，确实如此！其实只是那些名字我忘记了而已。我仍然记得父母的面容，还有村里其他人的样子，但那些名字和地点却渐渐从我的记忆中消失了。我想，这应该是一种心理上的强迫行为，而不是因为记忆负担过重。对于新认识的人，也会出现同样的情况——至少在他们彻底离开之后，我就会忘记他们的名字。 听起来……没我想象中那么可怕了，”你说。 “哈，是啊……说实话，我觉得这个诅咒让我无法对这件事产生过于强烈的情绪。至少，在那种健忘的状态开始之后是这样。虽然它还是会让我感到害怕，但我很高兴能有一些时刻可以坦诚地谈论这件事。这样，那种恐惧感似乎也会减轻一些…… 即使它真的发生了，我也很高兴能在这里帮助你暂时记住那些事情，”你说。 [callie.fucked |握住了她的手。 |用手指敲打桌子。 ] 她微笑着，那笑容真诚而温暖。 “我也是。你还有其他想说的吗？
rows.raw: ' "So what did you do before you came here? How did you happen upon this orchard?" you ask. "Me? Well, um... it was so long ago..." Callie says, closing her eyes and rubbing her fingers on her temples. "I remember a village in the mountains. I can't recall if it had a name, the mountain range or my village, but neither were very big. I don't know that I'd seen an outsider at all before coming here." She opens her eyes and looks out one of the windows. "I vividly remember coming here. I was hunting sheep, since we needed wool for a harsh winter. It was... more trees than I'd seen in my whole life, and the apples were so pretty. I'd eaten so many before I even knew what was happening," she says, closing her eyes again as she remembers. "When I turned around, my familiar hunting paths were gone. There was only the fence, and an unbreachable wall of darkness." "That was it? And you were trapped?" "Yeah. I, uh, haven't been able to leave. It's not like I haven't thought about it, when others came, especially the first couple times. I just know, though, that it's impossible. I don't even feel worse when I get close to the fence. With the others, particularly the ones who eat too much, I can see it draining them as they try to get away. I don't get that. The fence is just a wall to me." "Was there anyone here before you?" "Dunno. Not as far as I saw. Not even any skulls. The lodge wasn't here either, built that myself." "You did a good job of it. It looks very homey," you say, looking around at the interior "Thank you, I tried. Hunted all the sheep and ox that make up the rugs and bedding, too. Most were charmed by the apples by the time I found them, but still," she says, rubbing the back of her neck. "Yeah, still. Even if you don't think the hunt is as impressive, the craftsmanship definitely is." "Thanks." You take a moment to look around at the carved wood and the oldest-looking pieces of furniture that adorn the lodge interior. "Is that trip all you remember? I don't mean to pry, if it's something that hurts to touch on, but is any of this in the style of your home?" "Yes, actually! It's really just names I've forgotten. I still remember my parents' faces, and others from the village, but names and places just kind of slip away. I think it's part of the compulsion, rather than any kind of memory overload. The same thing happens with new people. At least, after they've gone for good." "That sounds... slightly less terrifying than I would have thought," you say. "Ha, yeah... I think the curse stops me from feeling super strongly about it, to be honest. At least, once that forgetful period sets in. It does kinda terrify me, but I'm glad to have these moments where I can talk honestly about it. That probably pushes it back toward terrifying..." "Even if it does, I'm glad I can be here to help you remember for a while," you say, [callie.fucked |taking hold of one of her hands. |tapping your fingers on the table. ] She smiles, genuine and warm. "Me too. Anything else on your mind?"'

rows.original: "What's the day-to-day like here? What do you do when you don't have guests? "Hmm, mostly making additions and renovations to the lodge," she says. "The apples might be magic, but the wood doesn't really share any of their magical properties, and applewood's still not the best for this kind of thing. There's no bugs like termites, but the wood still ages, and I often have to replace one or more parts. Sometimes I've even gotta replace whole walls. That's why some parts look newer than others." She indicates some of the different parts as she explains things. Some parts of the home do indeed look newer than others, and you can see how the corners are designed to support each wall and the ceiling separately. If one wall needed replacing, the others can support each other while it's being replaced. "Do you not run out of wood? Apart from that tree you were axing when we met I haven't seen a lot of stumps or lumber." "Well, I keep any extra logs behind the lodge, but also the grove just kinda grows as needed, I think? Rather than new trees, stumps just kind of grow back after a few days. It'll look like a new little seedling growing out from the stump at first, and then it'll be like a small tree, and then by the third or fourth day you can barely tell it was felled at all. I have no way to tell whether it's a new tree growing out of the old one or the same tree healing, though. "Useful, I suppose. What about the weather here? Is it always perfect like this?" "No, not quite. It tends to be rather hectic actually. Sometimes there are thunderstorms, or winter storms. The trees never die or lose their leaves from the cold, but it was really awful for me the first time when I didn't have any insulation. I didn't die either but I sure didn't get anything done." "And that happens all the time?" "Not that extreme all the time, but it's always different. Usually it tends to flop around between days like this and light rain. The trees are good protection from the rain when it's not heavy, too, so that makes it even easier." "I'd guess it makes keeping clean easier, too." "Yeah! Getting washed off in the rain after a rough day of work and then coming in to dry off and warm up with a fire is one of my favorite things." "Does the weather follow your mood then?" "N-..." she starts, pausing and thinking for a moment, subtly perplexed. "Nah, no way. It rains plenty of times when I'm happy. Or at least if it's influenced by me in any way, I don't have any idea how to detect or direct that influence." "If it were that subtle, I guess it'd be no different from a no," you [pc.mascFem |chuckle |giggle ]. "Hmm. Then what about food? I know you said you don't need to eat yourself, so how do you decide what to keep, and what do you do with the, uh, excess." "Well it mostly just goes to fertilizer. The roots here will suck up just about anything they can get their hands on, meat included. Not while you're alive or anything, but that's mostly what happens to entranced animals and even bugs. The people who die here, too. I buried some who were nice, but I'm pretty sure the same thing happens to them down there as up on the surface." "Ah. I guess there are worse fates than being fertilizer. What about stuff for fun?" "Hmm. I mostly keep myself occupied with exercise, but I do like rereading some of the books I've gotten from visitors over the years. Those I do remember. Not, like, word for word, but enough to know I've read every one at least a hundred times, even the ones I hated. Some of them I can't even read anymore since they're falling apart after being here so long, but I remember those ones too." "It sounds like a nice routine, at least." "Yeah. I've managed to not beat myself up about it," she says, smiling. "Anything else around here you want to hear about?"
rows.translation: 这里每天的生活是怎样的？在没有客人的时候，你们会做些什么呢？” “嗯，主要是对小屋进行一些添置和修缮工作，”她回答道。“苹果或许具有魔力，但木材本身并没有这种神奇的特性，而且苹果木其实并不适合用来做这些事情。虽然这里没有白蚁之类的害虫，但木材还是会老化，所以我经常需要更换一些部件，有时候甚至需要整面墙都重新搭建。这就是为什么有些部分看起来比其他部分更新一些的原因。 她在解释这些结构时指出了其中的一些不同部分。确实，房子的某些部分看起来比其他部分更新一些，而且你可以看到这些角落是如何被设计出来以分别支撑墙壁和天花板的。如果有一面墙需要更换，其他墙壁在更换那面墙的过程中仍然可以起到支撑作用。 你们的木材不是早就用轻型了吗？除了我们见面时你正在砍的那棵树，我根本没看到有什么树桩或原木。” “嗯，我把多余的原木都存放在小屋后面，而且那片树林也会根据需要自然生长，应该是这样的吧？ 与其说是新树苗，不如说树桩在几天后就会重新长出枝叶来。起初，会看起来像有一株新的小树苗从树桩上生长出来，然后它会逐渐长成一棵小树，而到了第三或第四天的时候，你几乎看不出来它曾经被砍倒过。 不过，我无从判断这是从老树上长出的新枝，还是同一棵树在自我修复。 还算有点用吧。这里的天气怎么样？总是这么完美无缺吗？” “不，并不是这样。实际上，这里的天气往往变化多端。有时候会遇到雷暴，或者冬季风暴。这里的树木永远不会因为寒冷而枯死或落叶，但当我第一次来到这里时，由于没有采取任何保暖措施，确实体验到了非常糟糕的天气条件。虽然我没有因此丧命，但确实什么事情都做不了。 这种事情经常发生吗？” “并不经常。 那个 天气总是变化无常，但每次都不一样。通常情况下，天气会在这样的晴天和小雨之间来回转变。当雨势不大时，树木也能为人们提供很好的遮雨保护，因此这让情况变得更加便利了。 我想这样也能让保持清洁变得更容易吧。” “没错！在辛苦工作一整天后，被雨水冲走身上的污垢，然后回到屋里休息、取暖，这真的是我最喜欢的事情之一。” “那么，天气也是会随着你的情绪而变化吗？不……”她开始说道，停顿了一下，似乎有些困惑。“不可能吧。当我开心的时候，经常会下雨。或者至少，如果这种天气变化真的受到了我的影响，我完全不知道该如何察觉或引导这种影响。如果真的有那么微妙的区别，我想那跟直接说‘不’也没什么两样吧。”你说道。 [pc.mascFem |轻声笑起来 |轻笑 ]嗯，那食物呢？我知道你说过自己不需要吃东西，那么你是怎么决定该保留哪些食物，又如何处理那些多余的食物的呢？” “嗯，那些多余的食物大多都被用来制作肥料了。这里的植物会吸收它们能获取到的任何东西，包括肉类呢。 不是说在你活着的时候就会发生这种事，但大多数被迷住的动物，甚至昆虫，都会遭遇这种命运。在这里死去的人也是如此。我埋葬过一些善良的人，但我很确定，他们在地下也会经历和在地面上一样的事情。啊，我想，比起被当成肥料，还有更糟糕的命运吧。那那些用来娱乐的东西呢？” “嗯，我主要是通过锻炼来打发时间，不过我确实很喜欢重读这些这些年来游客们送给我的书。 我确实记得那些书。不是说能一字不差地回忆起来，但至少足以确定我每本书都读过至少一百遍，包括那些我并不喜欢的书。有些书因为存放太久已经破旧不堪，我甚至再也无法阅读它们了，但我依然记得那些书的存在。至少听起来是个不错的习惯。” “是啊。我成功地没有因此而自责了，”她微笑着说，“这里还有其他你想了解的事情吗？

rows.original: "What about the people who've visited you before? Surely you have some cool stories, or scary ones. Might as well get the latter out of the way first, just so it's not what ends the stories." "Scary ones? I never had to kill anybody, if that's what you mean. There were a couple who were angry after they found out what happened too late, but none of them tried to attack me for it. A couple of them did die, though. The angry ones are usually the ones who most desperately try to leave, and that never works out. Most of the bones out there by the fence are from them." "Yeesh. I'm glad you haven't been attacked." "Oh, sorry, I didn't mean that. I have had to kill the occasional monster that slips through. Sometimes a drake thinks I look like a tastier treat than the apples, or some other beasty that resists the compulsion. It's the other reason I try to stay so fit. In addition to being a good workout, felling the trees really built up the chopping reflex. A drake's scales aren't that much stronger than the treebark here." "Wow. I [pc.isDK |bet you have some gnarly scars. |hope none of them hurt you too bad. ]" "[pc.isDK |Gotta disappoint you unfortunately. |Don't worry about it, really. ] I heal up really well. Even when I get scorched by drakefire my body heals up right. It's not like an instant magic thing, stuff still hurts mind you. I don't plan on hacking off any limbs to see if they grow back, either. Getting hurt still sucks, and I'd rather not do it at all if I can help it. I get enough nicks and bruises just carting around the chopped logs." "[callie.fucked |Well, If they ever last long enough for me to get here, I'll kiss them better." "I don't need to be injured for your kisses to make me feel better," she says with a giggle. |Sounds rough, when you put it that way." "I get used to it. It was rough at first but not really anymore. Now it's more stubbing and nicks than actual injuries. ]" "Good," you reply. "Hmm. Do you remember much about the non-angry visitors? Got any you consider interesting?" "Honestly I bet I could find something interesting about any of the good ones. The bad and boring ones kinda blend together, but the nice people all stick apart from their names. Lemme think," she says, tapping her chin and thinking for a bit. "[rand |One was a soapsmith, an elf from somewhere with a fiery name. She was hyper-fixated on the stuff, and it made me giggle listening to her talk about it. On top of that, she made sure I had several lifetimes supplies worth of the stuff. I don't know who's mortal lifetime she was supplying, but it feels like I still have several lifetimes worth. She taught me how to make a simpler version with animal fat, too. So I tend to do that first whenever beasts wander inside the boundary. I like to make use of every bit the trees don't, so it worked out wonderfully. That one stopped coming after she got too old. She was sadder than I was on her final visit, but she left with a smile on her face. She was always physically older than me, so she treated me like a proud grandma a lot at the end. |There was one aged general who wandered in while he was walking in his estate's gardens. He only came the once, but he was very excited to have something magical happen to him. He taught me some better ways to swing my axe when it was for fighting and not chopping wood. I don't really know how much of it I took to heart, but I feel like it's helped me deal with the more rambunctious monstery-types. |There was a poet who accidentally ate too many of the apples before I could stop him. He stayed the whole time. He never let it get him down, either, which is rare. The music he left is all long degraded at this point, but I still remember some of it," she says, humming a brief melody. "Some better than others. He never even tried to leave, and just spent the rest of his days helping me out. It was... rough to see him go. It never even got romantic, I just got used to seeing him every day." ] "It sounds like you care about them a lot. I hope I can be one of the memorable ones. And preferably not because of dying a terrible death..." you say, breaking her out of the reminiscent thoughts and making her giggle. "Yeah. I hope so too," she replies. "Anything else you want to talk about?"

rows.raw: ' "What about the people who've visited you before? Surely you have some cool stories, or scary ones. Might as well get the latter out of the way first, just so it's not what ends the stories." "Scary ones? I never had to kill anybody, if that's what you mean. There were a couple who were angry after they found out what happened too late, but none of them tried to attack me for it. A couple of them did die, though. The angry ones are usually the ones who most desperately try to leave, and that never works out. Most of the bones out there by the fence are from them." "Yeesh. I'm glad you haven't been attacked." "Oh, sorry, I didn't mean that. I have had to kill the occasional monster that slips through. Sometimes a drake thinks I look like a tastier treat than the apples, or some other beasty that resists the compulsion. It's the other reason I try to stay so fit. In addition to being a good workout, felling the trees really built up the chopping reflex. A drake's scales aren't that much stronger than the treebark here." "Wow. I [pc.isDK |bet you have some gnarly scars. |hope none of them hurt you too bad. ]" "[pc.isDK |Gotta disappoint you unfortunately. |Don't worry about it, really. ] I heal up really well. Even when I get scorched by drakefire my body heals up right. It's not like an instant magic thing, stuff still hurts mind you. I don't plan on hacking off any limbs to see if they grow back, either. Getting hurt still sucks, and I'd rather not do it at all if I can help it. I get enough nicks and bruises just carting around the chopped logs." "[callie.fucked |Well, If they ever last long enough for me to get here, I'll kiss them better." "I don't need to be injured for your kisses to make me feel better," she says with a giggle. |Sounds rough, when you put it that way." "I get used to it. It was rough at first but not really anymore. Now it's more stubbing and nicks than actual injuries. ]" "Good," you reply. "Hmm. Do you remember much about the non-angry visitors? Got any you consider interesting?" "Honestly I bet I could find something interesting about any of the good ones. The bad and boring ones kinda blend together, but the nice people all stick apart from their names. Lemme think," she says, tapping her chin and thinking for a bit. "[rand |One was a soapsmith, an elf from somewhere with a fiery name. She was hyper-fixated on the stuff, and it made me giggle listening to her talk about it. On top of that, she made sure I had several lifetimes supplies worth of the stuff. I don't know who's mortal lifetime she was supplying, but it feels like I still have several lifetimes worth. She taught me how to make a simpler version with animal fat, too. So I tend to do that first whenever beasts wander inside the boundary. I like to make use of every bit the trees don't, so it worked out wonderfully. That one stopped coming after she got too old. She was sadder than I was on her final visit, but she left with a smile on her face. She was always physically older than me, so she treated me like a proud grandma a lot at the end. |There was one aged general who wandered in while he was walking in his estate's gardens. He only came the once, but he was very excited to have something magical happen to him. He taught me some better ways to swing my axe when it was for fighting and not chopping wood. I don't really know how much of it I took to heart, but I feel like it's helped me deal with the more rambunctious monstery-types. |There was a poet who accidentally ate too many of the apples before I could stop him. He stayed the whole time. He never let it get him down, either, which is rare. The music he left is all long degraded at this point, but I still remember some of it," she says, humming a brief melody. "Some better than others. He never even tried to leave, and just spent the rest of his days helping me out. It was... rough to see him go. It never even got romantic, I just got used to seeing him every day." ] "It sounds like you care about them a lot. I hope I can be one of the memorable ones. rows.original:
"Would you like to hear about what's going on in the outside world?" you ask.
    
    "Yes!" she says, with a sudden explosion of enthusiasm. "Sorry, yes. Hearing about what's changed out there is one of my favorite things. It lets me feel less out of touch with the world."
    
    You take a seat at the counter and explain the current happenings of your struggle against Kasyrra. The enchanted centauress' eyes go wide as you explain about the monsters from another world, but she doesn't stay shocked for long. She's engrossed in the telling, asking you about specific points as you reach them. You tell her all about [var0
        |the siege of Khor'minos and its fallout
        |the retaking of the winter city and the chasing of its former-queen-turned-demon
        |your reclaiming of the local centaur village from the demon incursion
        |the magical explosion at the portal and your encounter with the cultists, along with your exploits since
    ]. The telling is peppered with the smaller feats of wonder you've accomplished, and even more smaller things that only have merit as addendums to the larger things. She hangs on every word with an abject excitement that draws more and more words out of your mouth.
    
    You tell her of [party.solo
        |the people you've met
        |the friends you've made
    ] and the places you've been, giving her as good a mental map of the Frost Marches as you can manage. With how long she's been here, it's possible someone from the northern world has been here before, but all the names and places don't bring forth any memories of such visits. She can't recall the names, but the places you describe aren't familiar either. Still, her eyes widen when you describe the amount of snow that falls in the Marches.
    
    "Wow. I thought the mountains of my homeland had a lot of snow..." she says when you've finished.
    
    You spend a few more minutes chatting about minor things, and answering questions she has about the Marches, and then the conversation slowly peters out. Did you want to chat about anything else?
rows.translation:
你想听听外面世界发生了什么吗？”你问道。

“想！”她突然充满热情地回答，“对不起，我真的很想听。了解外面发生了哪些变化，是我最喜欢做的事情之一。 这让我感觉自己并没有与这个世界脱节。”

你坐在柜台前，向店主讲述了你目前与卡希拉斗争的经过。当你提到那些来自另一个世界的怪物时，这位被施了魔法的半人马女店主的双眼瞪得大大的，但她并没有因此感到太过震惊。 她全神贯注地听你讲述，每当讲到某个具体细节时，她都会向你询问更多关于这些内容的信息。你便把她想了解的一切都告诉了她。 [var0
        |科尔米诺斯的围攻及其后果
        |夺回那座冬季之城，以及追捕那位曾经是女王如今却变成了恶魔的人……
        |你从恶魔的入侵中夺回了当地的半人马村庄
        |在传送门处发生的那场神奇爆炸，你与那些邪教徒的遭遇，以及自那以后你所取得的一切成就……
    ]你的讲述中穿插着那些你完成的种种令人惊叹的小事，还有一些更为微不足道的事情，但它们作为那些更重要事情的补充，也同样具有重要意义。她听得津津有味，那种热切的态度促使你不断继续讲述下去。

你向她讲述了这些事情…… [party.solo
        |你遇到的那些人
        |你结交的朋友们
    ] 你还告诉了她你曾经到过的一些地方，尽你所能为她描绘出一幅关于霜冻边境地区的详细 精神 map。考虑到她在这里已经待了这么长时间，很有可能之前也有来自北方世界的人来过这里，但那些地名和地点并没有让她想起任何关于那些访问的回忆。 她想不起来那些名字了，但你描述的地方她也不熟悉。不过，当你提到边境地区三月份会下多少雪时，她的眼睛还是亮了起来。

“哇，我原以为我家乡的山脉雪也很多呢。等你说完了，她说道。”

你们又聊了几分钟，谈论了一些琐事，同时也回答了她关于那些边境地区的一些问题，之后谈话就渐渐结束了。你还想聊些什么吗？

rows.original: "Can you explain how the apples work at all? I'm sure you've seen enough of them be eaten to have at least some idea." "That... really depends on what you're looking for when you ask that. I don't have the first clue what kind of magic is in them beyond the basics. They definitely taste just as good the enchantment suggests, at least for the first couple you eat. If you only eat one, or if they're diluted into something else, they taste pretty good, but after three or four, when the enchantment wears away, it starts to hurt to eat them." "Really? Even for you?" "Yeah. I still like the smell, but if I go to eat one nowadays it's the worst gut ache imaginable. I don't think it's quite as bad as for other people. The apples kinda changed me, but it didn't really alter that effect. Some of the visitors who got stuck here have described it as physically painful to eat another bite. I wouldn't suggest trying it out either way, except in a pie. Even then, only once a week or so." "Do you make pies like that?" "Yeah! Or at least I can. I especially like to bake one when there are visitors like you who don't get stuck but still want to try the apples. In my opinion it's much better than eating them raw. It's also the only way I can still eat them with the least possible amount of discomfort. And I mean it about the once a week thing. Even in a pie form, you don't want to be eating more than one or two in that period. It varies a little from person to person, but I've seen the number needed to get stuck here be as low as three." "Does the compulsion ever come back? Will I have to worry about it if I leave for too long?" "I don't think so. Once you know it's a thing it doesn't seem to work. The taste is still tempting, but that first smell that grips your mind goes away as soon as you get distracted. I'd probably have to put up more hardy defensive measures if it did." "Have you tried that?" "Mmm. Some smaller walls. Signs do nothing, and the fence is too wide to really block off that way. Plus I'm pretty sure the grove would just, like, move or something like that. I'd wake up one day to find my wall on the other side of the fence if it wasn't just gone entirely. I tend to listen to gut feelings like that. Besides, I've gotten into a pretty good pattern of knowing when people are showing up." "How can you tell?" "It's hard to explain. It's like the forest tries harder when it's got someone in its clutches, or when it's gearing up for someone to step over the boundary. I don't know how it knows when someone's on the other side, but it only ever grabs that person. It doesn't tend to switch while they're still alive, either. Just getting them here is enough for it, I guess. It also makes... let's just say I've gotten pretty good at sensing that change, and it's been quite a few people since anyone worth warning has eaten too many apples." "[pc.bg scholar |Fascinating. It's like you're [pc.isBimbo |magic too! |linked to the spell itself. ] |So you're[pc.isBimbo |, like, ] tapped into the magic of the place? ]" "I guess so. It doesn't feel like I influence it other than stopping people from hurting themselves. I've gotta do that myself, though." "Well, I for one am glad you've gotten so good at that part," you say with a smirk. "Yeah. It's a lot easier to feel like people are genuine in wanting to be here when it's actually a choice for them. Plus I like hearing about the outside." "We'll see if I can't find some things to show off." "I'd love that," she says. "Any other questions for me?"
rows.translation: 你能解释一下这些苹果到底是怎么起作用的吗？我敢肯定，你肯定见过很多人吃它们，所以应该至少有些了解吧。” “这个嘛……其实这完全取决于你提出这个问题的目的。除了一些基本原理之外，我根本不知道这些苹果里面究竟含有什么样的魔力。 至少在最初吃的那几颗之后，它们的味道确实如那种“魔法效果”所描述的那样美味。如果你只吃一颗，或者将它们与其他食物混合食用，味道也还算不错；但吃了三四颗之后，当那种“魔法效果”消退时，再继续吃下去就会觉得很难受了。" 真的吗？就连对你来说也是？” “是啊。我还是喜欢那种味道，但要是现在吃苹果，就会引发难以忍受的肠胃不适。我觉得这种反应对其他人来说可能更严重。那些被困在这里的访客们都说，再吃一口苹果就会感到身体疼痛。不管怎样，我都不建议大家尝试吃苹果，除非是放在派里。即便如此，也最好一周只吃一次吧。 你是用这种方法制作派的吗？” “是的！至少我是这么做的。特别是当有像你这样的客人来访时，他们既不想生吃苹果，又想尝尝派的味道，这时我就特别喜欢烤派。在我看来，这样吃比生吃苹果要好多了。 这也是我唯一能以最小程度的不适来食用它们的方法。我指的是每周吃一次这种情况。即使是将它们做成派的形式，你在那段时间里也不想吃超过一两个。这个数字因人而异，但我见过有些人只需要吃三个就就会出现这种情况。" 这种强迫感会再次出现吗？如果我离开太久，还会担心这个问题吗？” “我觉得不会。一旦你意识到这种存在，它似乎就不再起作用了。那种味道依然诱人，但那种一开始就抓住你注意力的气味，一旦你分了心，就会消失不见。如果真的会再次出现，那我可能就需要采取更严格的防御措施了。 你试过那个方法吗？” “嗯……那些小墙没什么用，标识牌根本不起作用，而围栏又太宽了，无法真正阻挡那个方向。另外，我敢肯定那些灌木丛会移动之类的……说不定有一天我醒来会发现，我的‘墙’已经不在那里了。 其他 如果它没有完全消失的话，我大概会站在某一方吧。我倾向于相信这样的直觉。另外，我已经养成了一种很好的习惯，能够判断出什么时候有人会到来。” “你怎么能判断出来的呢？” “这很难解释。 就好像当有人落入森林的怀抱中，或者当有人即将跨越那道界限时，森林会变得更加凶猛。我不知道它是如何知道有人正在另一边的，但它总是会抓住那个人。 在他们还活着的时候，这种情况也不会发生。我想，只要把他们带到这里就可以了。这也让我……这么说吧，我已经相当擅长察觉这种变化了，而且已经有很多人因为吃了太多苹果而需要被提醒了。" "[pc.bg scholar |太迷人了。就好像你真的置身其中一样。 [pc.isBimbo |魔法也一样！ |与这个法术本身紧密相关。 ] |所以你是……[pc.isBimbo |就像，比如说…… ] 感受到了这个地方的神奇之处吗？ ]我想也是吧。除了阻止别人伤害自己之外，我并没有感觉到自己对事情产生了什么影响。不过，这些事情我还是得亲自去做。” “嗯， 我 首先，我很高兴你在那方面变得这么出色了，”你笑着说。 “是啊。当人们真的是出于自己的意愿选择来到这里的时候，就会让人觉得他们是真的喜欢这里。而且，我也喜欢了解外面的世界。” “看看我能不能找到一些东西来让你看看吧。” “那我会非常高兴的，”她说。“还有其他问题要问我吗？

rows.original:
You ask Callie if she wouldn't mind baking some of the apples for you to try.

        "Sure! You only need a little bit, and a little bit helps dull the magic," she says, wandering out to pluck a few apples from the trees.
        
        She goes through the process of chopping them into small cubes, and mixing them with butter, sugar, and cinnamon to form a caramelly mix of filling. While she rolls a crust from a ball of dough, you chat more about life on the outside and your daily goings-on. It doesn't take more than fifteen minutes for things to settle and your pie to be ready for cooking, and you watch as she pours the apple mix into the crust and sets it on a rack in her woodstove.
        
        It takes another hour for the pie to actually bake, but you have delightful company to pass the time with. Chatting with her, it feels like no time passes at all. It's a nice day in the little forested demiplane, and your conversation partner is animated despite her lack of modern knowledge. She tells you more stories about beasts that happened upon the orchard, and whether she was able to pacify them or had to slay them.
        
        The time spent waiting feels like nothing at all in such good company, and you find yourself with a ready-to-eat pie at the end of your conversation. And a delicious pie it is, the perfect combo of sweet and tart held together in a delightful crust. You feel none of the magical pull from the apples you felt before, and the desire to take another slice is entirely natural. Callie takes a few slices of her own to nibble, and the two of you polish off the entire thing over the course of another hour.
        
        "Delicious," you say, rubbing your stomach.
        
        "Indeed. I'm glad sometimes that this is still an option, and that it works for avoiding the... yucky parts of the forest's magic. We'll have to wait a bit just in case, but don't be afraid to ask again.

你问卡莉是否愿意帮你烤一些苹果让你尝尝。

“当然可以！你只需要一点点，而且少量的苹果确实可以帮助减弱那种‘魔法’效果呢，”她说着，便走出去从树上摘了几个苹果。
        
        她将这些食材切成小方块，然后与黄油、糖和肉桂混合，制成一种焦糖味的馅料。而当她用面团擀成饼皮的时候，你们则继续聊着外面的生活以及彼此的日常琐事。 不到十五分钟的时间，一切就准备好了，你可以看到她将苹果混合物倒入饼皮中，然后将其放在木炉上的烤架上开始烘烤。
        
        虽然还需要再等一个小时才能真正烤好这个派，但你有了一位非常有趣的聊天伙伴来打发时间。和她聊天，时间仿佛根本不会流逝。在这个被森林环绕的小次元世界里，今天真是美好的一天；尽管她缺乏现代知识，但她的谈吐依然十分生动有趣。她向你讲述了许多在果园里遇到的野兽的故事，以及她是如何设法安抚它们，还是不得不将它们消灭的。
        
        在有这样好的陪伴下，等待的时间似乎根本不算什么。谈话结束后，你手中就会拿到一份现成的美味派。这确实是一份美味的派——甜中带酸，口感绝佳，而且饼皮也非常可口。与之前吃苹果时那种令人着迷的感觉不同，现在你再想吃一片，完全是出于自然的欲望。卡莉也拿了几片来品尝，于是你们俩又一起吃了一个小时才把整个派吃完。
        
        真好吃，”你边说边揉着肚子。

“确实。有时候我真的很庆幸还有这个选择，它能够帮助我们避开森林魔法中那些……令人不快的部分。我们还是需要再等一会儿，以防万一，但如果你还想吃的话，随时都可以再问哦。

rows.raw: "\n        You get the feeling eating these things without supervision is probably a very bad idea... Are you sure you want to eat them?"

rows.original:
Eh, surely you'll be fine. They're just apples, after all, and you know the effect they have. You'll just stop before there's a problem. After saying your goodbyes, you head back toward the fence, stopping just before you reach it and eyeing up one of the nearby trees. There are plenty of low-hanging apples, and you simply reach up to pluck one off the tree. It's firm and warm in your hand, and it certainly doesn't look malevolent.

            Without much further ado, you take a bite. Succulent sweetness greets your tongue, and you can't help but immediately take another bite. The golden fruit is easily the tastiest thing you've ever eaten, and you soon find yourself holding a completely picked-clean apple core. It was so good that you hardly even registered eating the rest of the apple. That won't do, so you pluck another apple off the tree and endeavor to eat this one more slowly.
            
            To that end, you take several bites at once and fill your mouth with crunchy sweetness. Wonderful sweetness caresses your brain just as much as your tongue, and you have to hold back a moan from the sheer ecstasy. This plan works, at least until you go to take another bite and find another apple core in your stomach. You grab another apple, feeling irritated at the lost time stealing your bites, and try to cram as much of it into your mouth as possible. Still, you are foiled after the first couple bites, and furrow your brow in irritation.
            When you go to bite the fourth apple, however, the sweetness that fills your mouth is cloying and sickening. You have to fight not to spit the sugary mass of chewed fruit out of your mouth, and merely looking at the rest of it in your hand makes you squeamish. There's a sudden inherent feeling in your gut that you've gone too far, and an accompanying sinking feeling that says you've gone too far. 
            
            It may not matter anymore, but you could damn the awfulness and keep eating.

rows.original:
You toss the apple aside, and spit out the remainder that was in your mouth. With a heavy heart, you take a few hesitant steps toward the fence. Sure enough, your outstretched hands hit the air above the wood like an imaginary wall. The empty plains beyond are plainly visible, but your body refuses to pass. You get the sense that to force the issue would be suicide, and despite the sinking feeling in your heart, you don't feel any need for that. 

                Instead, you suck up the remains of your hubris and head back to the lodge. Callie smiles as she sees you again, and then her smile falters as she notices the look on your face and assumedly notices the detritus of golden apple. You shrug, unsure of what, if anything, to say at this point. Finally, you settle on at least something.
                
                "Sorry. I guess I couldn't help myself," you say with a heavy sigh.
                
                "No. I should've realized it was such a temptation for you. If I'd known, I would have kept a better eye on you. You aren't... planning on doing anything drastic, are you?" she asks, averting her gaze as she says it.
                
                "No, no. Don't worry about that. I made a stupid decision I'll have to live with, but I do plan to live with it. If you wouldn't mind a more permanent [callie.fucked
                    |[pc.boyGirl]friend
                    |roommate
                ]," you say.
                
                "I definitely wouldn't mind. [callie.fucked
                    |I think I'll enjoy being with you more than the others who stayed.
                    |I enjoy the time I get to spend with people who eat too many, whether it's on accident or on purpose.
                ] Now come on, Let's make something to get that taste out of your mouth."
                
                You follow her, and help make some food to cleanse the cloying sweetness from your mouth. The magnitude of your decision doesn't hit you until a few days later. There's no going back. No more adventures, no saving the world, and not even the knowledge of what happens to the world outside. Maybe someone eventually saves the world of Savarra from the clutches of a demonic invasion, but you never find out.
                
                Having someone else to bounce thoughts off of does help to stop you from going insane, and you can't say life in the orchard is all boring. No other intelligent creatures come through while you're alive, but several animals and even a few monsters show up at random intervals. When you get too old to help out around the place, Callie keeps you warm and comfortable. Eventually, you pass in your sleep, content but never forgetting the adventures you could have had.

rows.original: Fuck that! You aren't about to go this far only to turn back when you know it's too late. You keep right on eating, trying to push the awful sweetness from your brain as you continue chewing and swallowing the crunchy apples. It helps to try and focus on the fruit itself while avoiding as much of the peel as you can. While not tasting much better, it ends up being far easier to just chew your way through the fruit. It's hard to tell how long you keep eating, till it feels like your stomach is fit to bursting with apple. As you continue to eat, however, it starts to feel different. Rather than absolute disgust, the sickening sensation you were fighting through fades to mild distaste. You also feel... different somehow. New sensations touch your mind in ways that are hard to comprehend. At the very least, you can inherently tell you wont be able to leave the orchard. Its magical influence is noticeably coursing through you, and the former discomfort is subsiding with each passing second. Swallowing down the last of the juices you haven't finished, you stand and make your way back to the lodge. Callie smiles when she sees you, and then worry creases her brow when she sees the detritus of so many apples. Then, inexplicably, she gets a curious look on her face. You can sense her presence now, and feel how she's the same as you. She feels just like any other part of the orchard to your new magical sense. Part of it, but different from the trees or the earth. "You ate the apples, but you're... different," she says, trotting closer. "[silly |Yeah, I'm just built different I guess. Ate my wheaties, |Yeah. Don't ask me how, though, I just kept eating them and eating them, ]" you reply. "There's no way it's that simple," she says with an exasperated chuckle. "People have tried that." "I don't know what to tell you." "Don't, you don't need to explain it for me to see that it's real. [callie.fucked |You're just determined not to leave me alone here, aren't you? |Did you feel that bad that I was stuck here? ]" she asks. "[callie.fucked |Someone else will save the world. I can't help that I met someone who probably wouldn't get another chance to have permanent company," you say, hugging her around the waist and kissing her toned tummy. |I dunno. I guess I did. You seemed so lonely, and I figure you could use a friend to pass the years," you say, patting her shoulder. ] The centauress tosses her arms around you in a tight hug, and doesn't let go for a long while. After that, you both cook some meat and chat about the future. The gravity of your decision doesn't strike you until a few days have passed. You probably won't find out what came of the struggle against Kasyrra, at the very least until it's been resolved for a long time. It feels a little scary, but you find the revelation to be surprisingly calming. It might be a little bit of magical compulsion keeping the stress away, but you feel like you can trust the fate of the world to your allies and the gods. You lose track of the days and then the years you spend with Callie, working around the orchard and adding additions to the lodge. It's much easier to stand the loneliness with someone there to talk to, and you never feel worried that you're going to break down mentally. Both of you are equally sure in your thoughts that you'll be alone together forever, which makes the first new arrival especially shocking. There's no good way to track how long it's been, but the first person to show up is an addled scholar who claims to have been wandering through piles of old books in an ancient belharran ruin. You ask about the war, but can't make heads or tales of his rambling explanation of what happened. Something about tieflings, whatever those are. After he leaves, you and Callie laugh and celebrate, happy to know you'll be seeing others. You live on, passing the years trapped in your magical orchard and greeting newcomers while making sure they're adequately warned about the dangers. The exact fate of the world is no longer your problem, but you're glad to know it, at the very least, wasn't the world's end.
rows.translation: 去他的！你总不能走到这一步，却在为时已晚的时候才放弃吧。继续吃吧，努力把那种难吃的甜味从脑海中赶走，继续咀嚼、咽下那些脆脆的苹果吧。 尽量专注于果肉本身，同时尽量少咬果皮。虽然这样吃并不会让果肉的味道变得更好，但确实会让你更容易咀嚼果肉。 很难判断自己会吃多久，直到感觉肚子都被苹果填得胀得不行为止。 然而，当你继续进食时，这种感觉开始发生变化。那种令人作呕的感觉不再那么强烈，从最初的极度厌恶逐渐转变为轻微的不适。同时，你也觉得……自己有些不一样了。 新内容 这些感官体验以一种难以理解的方式影响着你的思维。至少，你可以清楚地感觉到自己根本无法离开这个果园。它的魔力正在你体内流淌，那种最初的不适感也在每一秒钟里逐渐消退。 你喝光了那些还没喝完的果汁，站起身准备回到小屋。当卡莉看到你时，她露出了微笑，但看到那些被吃剩的苹果残渣后，她的眉头又皱了起来。随后，她的脸上浮现出一种难以解释的好奇神情。 你现在能够感受到她的存在，也能体会到她与你其实是相同的。在你的这种新的魔法感知能力中，她就像果园里的其他一切部分一样——是果园的一部分，却又与那些树木或大地有所不同。 “你吃了那些苹果，但你现在…………不一样，”她说着，快步走了过来。[silly |嗯，我想我就是天生与众不同吧。吃了我的麦片之后…… |是啊。不过别问我是怎么做到的，我只是不停地吃，一直吃个不停。 ]你回答吧。” “不可能那么简单，”她无奈地笑了笑说，“很多人都试过了。” “我不知道该跟你说什么。” “不用说，你不需要解释，我也知道这是真的。 [callie.fucked |你就是故意不让我在这里一个人待着，对吧？ |因为我被困在这里，你真的觉得我那么难受吗？ ]她问道。[callie.fucked |总会有人来拯救世界的。而我，只是遇到了一个可能再也不会有机会拥有长久陪伴的人罢了，”你一边说，一边搂住她的腰，亲了亲她那结实的小腹。 |我也不确定。不过我想我是这么做的吧。你看起来那么孤独，我觉得你需要一个朋友来陪伴你度过这些岁月。”你一边说，一边轻拍着她的肩膀。 ] 那个半人马女子紧紧地拥抱你，好久都没有松开。之后，你们一起煮了一些肉，还聊起了未来。直到几天后，你才真正意识到自己所做的决定意味着什么。 你很可能永远无法知道与卡希拉的这场斗争最终结果如何，至少在事情彻底解决之前是无法得知的。这种不确定性让人感到有些害怕，但当真相终于揭晓时，你却会发现它反而让人感到一种出乎意料的平静。或许是一种某种神奇的力量在帮助你缓解压力，但你知道，世界的命运其实掌握在你的盟友和众神手中。 与凯莉一起在果园里劳作，为小屋添置各种设施，日子就这样一天天、一年年地过去了。有她相伴，孤独感自然会减轻许多；你也再不会担心自己会精神崩溃。你们俩都坚信，自己将会永远在一起，因此当第一个新成员出现时，这个突如其来的变化确实令你们感到十分震惊。 虽然没有确切的方法可以计算出已经过去了多久，但第一个出现的人是一位精神有些错乱的学者。他声称自己一直在一座古老的贝尔哈兰废墟中，穿梭于堆积如山的旧书之中。你询问了他关于那场战争的情况，但却完全无法理解他那支离破碎、语无伦次的叙述——其中还提到了什么提夫林人之类的东西。在他离开后，你和卡莉相视而笑，为能遇到其他人而感到高兴。 你继续活着，年复一年地困在那个充满魔力的果园里，迎接新来的人，同时确保他们能够充分了解其中的危险。世界的最终命运已经不再与你有关，但至少你知道，那并不是世界的终结。

"[pc.isLactating |It can't be comfortable having your teats so overfull like that, and in a place you cant even reach. I get worried about the pressure building up and mine are easy-access. I could help out with that if you want, |[pc.dcb |How about you find me a bucket and a comfortable place to sit, and I'll help out with those obscenely full teats between your legs, |Would you like some help with milking? I can't help but notice how big your teats are, and I've seen some milkings before, |Wow! Your teats are swollen up so big they're dripping! I could help with that if you want, ] ]" you offer, as nonchalantly as you can manage. The dusky centaur stares, somehow managing to blush an even darker shade as she thinks about it. Before replying, she spins in place, trotting over to the drawers and searching for a moment before withdrawing a large pail. Additionally, she grabs a well-crafted wooden stool, sturdy enough for even a centaur to stand on, before returning to you. "It does get rather... inconvenient, not being able to reach them. If you wanted to try it out I won't say no," she says, holding the bucket out for you to take and placing the stool before your feet. You take a seat as she turns in place, shifting carefully to stand just before you with her hind legs parted slightly. From your seat you have a perfect view of her painfully swollen udders, and the occasional drip of cloudy golden liquid that falls from them. You're also given a face-to-face view of her equine slit, bared and glistening in the dim light of the cabin. Not even her long tail obstructs your view as she holds it out of the way to make your milking easier. With how tall she is she has no way of knowing you're staring, but she must know what kind of position she's put you in. Not wanting to make a complete fool of yourself, you fumble forward with your hands, gently wrapping your thumb and forefinger around the round nubs of her teats, grinning with surprise when a stream of rich bronze cider jets out into the bucket with a satisfying plink. Equally gratifying is the sigh of utter relief that comes from above you. You drop into a rhythm, resisting the urge to start whistling as Caliope visibly and audibly relaxes. Fruity aromas fill the air around you as the bucket begins to fill. After the first couple tugs the ebony centaur's nectar slows to a more even flow. At first you'd been worried about the size of the pail, but with the reduced rate you have plenty of space to fill. With that potential problem mitigated you still have something to worry about. As she relaxes, Caliope's exposed slit grows plump with arousal, and the occasional reflexive wink reveals a clit bigger than an electrum hawk. rows.original:
Mustering your will, you wrench your thoughts back to the task of milking. You continue to gently tug Caliope's perfectly squeezable teats till the flow slows to a trickle. The sensitive nubs are still far bigger than average, but no longer seem as painfully swollen. Roughly half a gallon of milk cider fills the bucket at your feet, smelling perfectly delicious. The dusky centaur grabs a handful of bottles from the table, filling a couple small bottles that she places on one of her shelves before handing you the larger bottle and the pail.

        "Gods that feel's so much better. You can keep that bottle, and what's left in the pail there. Maybe we can do this again the next time I fill up, and I can refill it," she offers with an eager smile. "Now, is there anything else you wanted?"

"[first CALIOPE_WINTERSTEM
        |Would you like to try some winterstem with me?" you ask. "Have you had it before?"
        
        "I'd love some! It's been actual ages, but yes! Only a handful of visitors have been both willing and able to get it,"
        |would you want to smoke together again? I brought more winterstem," you ask.
        
        "I'd love to! Last time was nice,"
    ] she says, trotting over as you pull out the stash you brought.
    
    You retrieve a pipe and prep it for smoking, packing the bowl as neatly as you can. lighting up the clump of plants inside, you wait for it all to take before inhaling a breath of relaxing smoke. Exhaling in a stream of wispy fog, you hand the pipe up to Callie. While she silently hypes herself up, you take a seat and put your chin in your hands.
    
    Callie inhales slowly and then exhales with a contented sigh. Despite the professed time since she last regularly smoked, she handles it with the grace of an expert. She takes another pull before handing the pipe back to you, in through the mouth and out through her nose. It's plain to see her reaction as you pass back and forth over a few minutes of smoking. Relaxation loosens her stance till her human end slumps down onto the counter with her head resting on one arm. A wide grin parts her lips, and she only continues down the path of utter relaxation.
    
    "This is nice. I missed this a lot. You can't grow anything like this here, especially not stuff this good."
    
    "I'm happy to help. It's somewhat common where I'm from, so I can bring it whenever you need some extra strength relaxing time."
    
    "Fuck yeah. This is the best," she says, taking another slow pull.
    
    You both alternate between who's smoking, till the plant you brought is burned through and smoked to nothing but pleasant-smelling ash. After that, you lounge around the lodge, giggling at small jokes and nibbling on meat jerky when you get hungry. The high lasts a good further couple hours after the last of the winterstem has been smoked, and it's an easy high to come down from on top of that. The orchard's apple-scent creeps back into your noses as it does, and you stretch as you stand and work the last of the relax-exhaustion out of your muscles. 
    
    Callie stretches in a similar fashion, bending forward and then backward before trotting back behind the counter. "Did you just come to relax me into oblivion, or was there anything else you needed?"
rows.translation:
"[first CALIOPE_WINTERSTEM
        |你想和我一起尝尝冬茎吗？”你问道，“你以前吃过吗？”

“我非常想尝！其实已经很久没有吃了，不过确实吃过！只有少数几位访客既有兴趣也有机会吃到它。
        |你想再一起抽烟吗？我带了更多的冬茎烟来，”你问道。

“我非常愿意！上次一起抽烟的时光真的很愉快。
    ] 她说着，一边快步走过来，一边你则拿出了带来的那些东西。

你取出一根烟斗，开始准备吸食，将烟斗里的烟叶装得格外整齐。点燃烟叶后，你等待着烟雾完全燃烧起来，然后深吸一口，让放松的烟雾进入肺部。呼出烟雾时，你将烟斗递给了卡莉。她默默地吸着烟，而你则坐下来，双手部托着下巴。
    
    卡莉缓缓吸了一口烟，然后满足地呼了出来。尽管她声称自己已经很久没有定期吸烟了，但她依然表现得像一位专家一样娴熟。她又吸了一口，之后才把烟斗递还给你——通过嘴巴吸进去，再通过鼻子呼出来。 当你们来回抽了几分钟的烟后，她的反应一目了然。随着放松情绪的蔓延，她的身体逐渐松弛下来，最终整个人瘫倒在柜台上，头靠在一只手部臂上。她的嘴角绽放出灿烂的笑容，整个人彻底陷入了彻底的放松状态。
    
    这太棒了。我真的很想念这种东西。在这里根本种不出这样的东西，尤其是这么好的。”

“我很乐意帮忙。在我家乡，这种东西还挺常见的，所以只要你们需要一些放松的时光，我随时都可以提供。”

“太好了，这真是太棒了！”她一边说，一边又慢慢品尝起来。
    
    你们轮流吸烟，直到你们带来的那株植物被完全烧尽，只剩下散发着怡人香气的灰烬。之后，你们就在小屋里闲逛，互相讲些笑话，饿了就啃点肉干。 在最后一根冬茎被点燃燃烧之后，这种兴奋感还能持续好几个小时，而且这种兴奋感也很容易消退。随着时间的流逝，果园里苹果的香气又会重新弥漫在你的鼻尖，你会伸伸懒腰，站起身来，让肌肉中的紧张与疲惫彻底消退。 
    
    卡莉也以类似的方式做了伸展运动，先向前弯腰，再向后仰，然后快步走回柜台后面。“你是专门来让我放松到忘乎所以的地步的，还是还有其他事情需要你处理？

rows.original:
"I've got something good here. I'd like to share it with you if you're ok with that," you say, pulling out the portion of Razorcup Nectar from your pack and splitting it into two half-shots.
    
    "[var0
        |I-I mean if you're sure. You're handling that stuff like it's liquid gold, and I can tell you right now the value might be lost on me,
        |Is that the same ultra-valuable stuff? I still don't know if I'm the most worthy taker, but I'm willing if you want to,
    ]" she says, scooting her glass closer.
    
    "I'm sure. I won't regret it."
    
    She nods, lifting the glass as you lift yours. You hold your hand out, and she clinks her cup against yours before the both of you drink down the sweet nectar in one swift gulp. The clear liquid heightens your senses almost immediately, and you see the dusky centauress' eyebrows raise as a shiver runs up her shoulders. Looking around the lodge and then turning back to focus on you.
    
    "Whoa. That's fantastic. You look even [callie.fucked
        |[pc.mascFem
            |more handsome
            |prettier
        ]
        |more the dashing hero
    ] like this. This is powerful stuff," she says.
    
    "Yeah, it is. I don't know how much it'll really help you around here, though. Maybe you'll get an extra productive day for logging," you reply with a smile. "If any unruly beasts leak through the boundary, you'll be darn ready for them, too."
    
    "[var0
        |Day? How long does this stuff last?" she asks, eyes wide once again.
        |I remember. Last time I caught a couple rabbits, even. Reminded me of the long past."
    ]
    
    "[var0
        |About twenty four hours give or take a couple minutes. It's potent stuff," you explain with a laugh.
        |I'm glad you get use out of it. May this time be no less helpful," you say with a smile.
    ]
    
    "I'll make as much use of this boon you've shared as I can. Did you want to do anything else while you're here?"

rows.original:
"I have some wine from a local city of minotaurs, if you'd like to try some. I can't try it with you cause it has a transformative effect on me, but it's good wine."
    
    "I'd love to! I've got a glass around here somewhere."
    
    She fishes around beneath the table and pulls out a wine glass, waiting for you to uncork and pour the serving of bovum sherry from your pack. Once it's settled, she picks up the glass and swishes it around a few times before taking a sip. While she tastes the wine, you explain Khor'minos and a little bit of the history you know. Her eyes remain closed as she savors the flavor, but you can tell she's listening, and she gives you a smile after she finally swallows.
    
    "That's wonderful. Those minotaurs know what they're doing. It's been ages since I really tried wines, but this stuff is legit," she says, taking another sip.
    
    You explain more of Khor'minos, everything you've learned about it so far, and some indirect tales you've heard while she finishes the glass. You keep on till the tales are done, regaling her while she cleans the glass and places it back beneath the counter. When everythings done, she's still smiling, waiting patiently till the last story finishes.
    
    "Did you have anything else for this trip? Or just the story and the wonderful wine?"
rows.translation:
我有一些来自弥诺陶洛斯所在城市的葡萄酒，如果你想尝尝的话。可惜我不能和你一起品尝，因为这种酒会对我产生某种特殊的效果，但它的味道确实很不错。”

“我非常愿意！我应该在这里的某个地方有一杯吧。她在桌子下面翻找着，最终拿出一只酒杯，等着你打开瓶盖，然后从你的包里取出那瓶博文雪利酒倒进去。等酒液静止下来后，她拿起酒杯晃了几下，然后喝了一口。 当她品尝葡萄酒时，你开始向她解释关于科尔米诺斯的事情，以及你所了解的那些历史背景。她闭着眼睛细细品味酒香，但你能看出她在认真听你讲述。等她终于咽下酒液后，她朝你露出了微笑。
    
    太棒了。那些弥诺陶洛斯确实知道自己在做什么。我已经很久没有真正品尝过葡萄酒了，但这种酒确实非常不错，”她边说边又喝了一口。

在她喝完酒的过程中，你向她详细介绍了关于科尔米诺斯的一切，包括你目前所了解的信息，还有一些你间接听来的故事。 你一直讲着故事，直到所有的故事都讲完。在她清洗玻璃杯并将它们放回柜台下方的过程中，你一直在给她讲故事。当一切结束后，她依然面带微笑，耐心地等待着最后一个故事结束。

“这次旅行你还有其他安排吗？ 还是只想要故事和美酒而已？

Again the now-familiar sound of centaur hooves thundering upon the cracked earth begins to roar in your [pc.ears],[party.som| your [pc.weapon] coming out to guard yourself| [party.compNames] getting closer to you in preparation| your party huddling together for protection] as the horde approaches over a hill.

        The din of myriad hooves trampling the earth drowns out everything but your thoughts as a cloud of dust appears, tall, muscular forms emerging from it as shadowy figures until at last, the forefront of the horde can be seen clearly. Another horrifically demon-touched packleader, every bit as ugly as the last, leads the pack in a nonstop charge through the valley.
        
        Upon spotting you, the grotesquely demonic example of a centaur breaks off from the stampeding group with two accompanying marauders, yelling and whooping in their ruined language. Wheeling around from the group, they charge you down with impunity and engage!
rows.translation:
那熟悉的半人马蹄声再次在裂开的土地上轰鸣，那种声音再度在你耳边回荡起来…… [pc.ears],[party.som| 你的 [pc.weapon] 站出来保护自己| [party.compNames] 为了更好地与你交流，我正在做相应的准备。| 你们的队伍挤在一起以寻求保护] 当那支庞大的队伍翻过山丘时，无数马蹄踩在地面上发出的嘈杂声淹没了周围的一切，只留下了你的思绪。随后，一片尘土升腾而起，高大的、肌肉结实的身影从尘土中逐渐显现出来，那些朦胧的轮廓最终变成了清晰可辨的队伍前卫。 又有一个被恶魔侵蚀得面目可憎的兽群首领，和上一个一样丑陋，它带领着兽群不停地冲过山谷。

当它发现你的存在时，这个长得丑陋不堪、完全被恶魔控制的半人马立刻从奔腾的兽群中分离出来，带着两个跟班的掠夺者，用它们那残缺的语言大声呼喊着、尖叫着朝你冲了过来。 他们从队伍中冲出来，毫无顾忌地向你冲过来，然后开始战斗！

当你穿梭于那些杂草丛生的荒野之中时，突然开始听到一阵微弱的……嗡嗡声？你四处张望，试图找出这个奇怪声音的来源，同时紧紧握住手中的武器。 [pc.weapon] 随着那种陌生的声音变得越来越响亮，似乎从你周围的所有方向传来，你不由得后退了几步，同时继续观察周围环境，寻找任何可能的威胁。

突然间，整个世界开始旋转起来。你无助地尖叫着，身体失去平衡，摔倒在地，而你的脚被一根粗大的树根缠住了。 你发出一声闷哼，仰面躺了下来，睁大眼睛望着树梢。

就在那里！一片洁白的云朵般柔软的绒毛正从高处盘旋着落在你周围，它被一对亮粉色的翅膀托举着，那翅膀如此精致透明，看起来它们更适合属于一只蝴蝶，而不是这样的生物。……不管那是什么。它的体型与人类相当，速度也非常快，在俯冲攻击你的前一刻，它的动作太快了，让你根本来不及仔细观察。你赶紧翻滚躲开，同时将身体…… [pc.legs] 当你从那生物的身边跳开时，迅速站起身来，准备行动。 [pc.weapon] 当这只生物盘旋着飞回原地，在离你几步远的地方停下来，悬停在地面之上时，它自己也完成了一个翻滚动作。

现在，你的攻击者终于停了下来，你终于可以好好看看她了。 多么迷人的身影啊！一位身形曲线优美的女子出现在你面前，乍一看她与人类无异，唯有身后那双柔软的粉色翅膀在轻轻振动。她的四肢以及脖颈部位覆盖着一层厚厚的白色绒毛，质地如同羊毛般柔软。 然而，在那片洁白之中，她的身体有一半是裸露的：一条皮制马裤紧紧贴合着她修长的双腿，而那些由硬化皮革制成的半护腿也为她的腿部提供了保护；此外，她腰带上悬挂着一串串闪闪发光的硬币和宝石，这些装饰物在她的双腿间晃动。
    
    相反，她的丰满胸部和腹部完全暴露在外，F罩杯的胸部骄傲地展现在人们面前，而倒立的乳头在寒风中显得格外坚硬。当她站立时，这些胸部会呈现出一种迷人的摆动姿态，偶尔还能看到一条细银链将一枚闪闪发光的粉色护身符悬挂在她那丰满的双峰之间。 她那火红色的双眼与你的目光紧紧对视，你竭尽全力地将视线从她那诱人的身姿上移开，看向她手中那把对准你的巨型双刃剑。

“你、你到底想……”你刚开口，却见这个形如飞蛾的女孩危险地挥动了她的剑。
    
    别把这件事弄得这么复杂， [pc.mascFem|英俊的|亲爱的]就是这个，”她说着，指的是你腰带上挂着的钱袋。“站起来，把东西交出来！你总得把你的贵重物品交出来，不过怎么交……那就看你的了！”

你……你真的要被抢劫了吗？搞什么鬼！那你打算怎么办：给她一些钱，和她打架，还是试着协商另一种支付方式呢？
rows.raw:
"
    As you make your way through the overgrown wilderlands, you start to hear a faint... buzzing? You look around for the source of the strange noise, clutching your [pc.weapon] tight as the alien sound grows louder and louder, coming from seemingly all around you. You back up, still scanning your surroundings for a threat.

    Suddenly, the world is spinning. You give a helpless cry as you tumble to the ground, foot caught on a thick root. With a grunt, you flop onto your backside, staring wide-eyed into the treetops.
    
    And there it is! A swirling mass of white, as fluffy as a cloud, is circling you from on high, carried aloft on a set of brilliant pink wings, so delicate and translucent they look like they'd be more at home on a butterfly than... whatever that is. It's human sized, and fast, buzzing around too quickly for you to get a good look at in the moments before it dive-bombs you. You twist and roll, tucking your [pc.legs] up as you tumble out of the creature's way. You jump up, readying your [pc.weapon] as the creature banks and flies back around, executing a roll of its own before coming to a stop a few paces from you, hovering just above the ground.
    
    Now that your assailant's finally stopped, you can finally get a good look at her. And what a her it is! A curvy woman flutters before you, human at first glance save the delicate pink wings beating behind her. Her limbs and the collar of her neck are covered in a downy white fuzz as thick as wool, and by the looks of it just as soft. Beyond the whiteness, though, she's half bare: a pair of leather breeches cling tightly to her long legs, armored with hardened leather half-greaves, and crossing chains of shiny coins and gemstones hang from her belt to dangle between her legs.
    
    Conversely, her large breasts and belly are uncovered, F-cup tits proudly on display and inverted nipples stiff in the cold breeze. They sway hypnotically as she hovers, occasionally giving a glimpse of a glittering pink amulet held aloft by a slim silver chain tucked between her hefty mounds. Her fiery red eyes lock with yours, and with all your willpower you drag your gaze from the buxom body on display to the imposing two-handed sword she's leveled at you.
    
    "Wh-what do you-" you start to say, but are cut off as the moth-like girl flicks her sword dangerously.
    
    "Don't make this hard, [pc.mascFem|handsome|sweetheart]," she says, indicating the coin pouch hanging on your belt. "Stand and deliver! You're going to hand your valuables over, but how much fun it is... that's up to you!"
    
    Are... are you seriously getting mugged? For fuck's sake! Well, what are you going to do: give her some coin, fight her, or try and bargain for a... different kind of payment?"

rows.original: Time to teach this fluffy slut who's boss!
rows.translation: 是时候让这个毛茸茸的贱人知道谁才是老板了！
rows.raw: "Time to teach this fluffy slut who's boss!"

rows.original: No need for violence... just take my money! Give her 100 coins.
rows.translation: 不需要使用暴力……只要把我的钱拿走就行了！给她100枚硬币吧。
rows.raw: "No need for violence... just take my money! Give her 100 coins."

rows.original: You're not willing to give her your money, but by the way she's eyeing you, you bet she's got other things on her mind, too.
rows.translation: 你不愿意把钱给她，但看她看你的眼神，我敢打赌，她心里肯定也在想着别的东西。
rows.raw: "You're not willing to give her your money, but by the way she's eyeing you, you bet she's got other things on her mind, too."

rows.original:
As you wander the valley, you begin to hear a faint humming sound coming from not far away. Curious, you follow the sound over the gentle rise of a nearby hill and into a small copse of trees nearer to the lake's shore. Peeking through the dense underbrush, you see the buxom purple-winged moth-girl who's been trying to rob you since you arrived in the valley. She's sitting on a tree stump in the middle of a small clearing, surrounded by a few open knapsacks filled with coins, jewels, and... books, of all things!
    
    Legs crossed and eyes ever so slightly squinted, the girl's currently deep into one of the leather-bound volumes she's squirreled away, gingerly turning one of the ancient-looking pages. This must be her camp, you guess: silk scarves and heavy cloaks alike are strung up from low-hanging tree branches, and a clumsily-made weapon rack near her holds a brace of bronze sabers as well as the gold-hilted claymore she's been wielding, a weapon utterly unlike any you've seen elsewhere in the Marches. She hasn't noticed you yet, and lost in the pages as she is, you don't think she will unless you announce yourself.
    
    What do you do?
rows.translation:
当你漫步在山谷中时，突然听到不远处传来一阵微弱的嗡嗡声。出于好奇，你顺着声音的方向，穿过附近小山丘的缓坡，来到湖边的一片小树林中。透过茂密的灌木丛，你看到了那个身材丰满、拥有紫色翅膀的蛾女——自从你来到这个山谷以来，她一直在试图抢走你的东西。 她坐在一片小空地中央的树桩上，周围放着几个敞开的背包，里面装满了硬币、珠宝，还有……居然是书籍！

女孩双腿交叉坐着，眼睛微微眯起，正专心致志地阅读那本皮封的书，她小心翼翼地翻动着那些看起来很古老的页面。 这肯定就是她的营地：丝质围巾和厚重的斗篷都被挂在低垂的树枝上，她身边那个粗糙制作的武器架上放着一把把青铜短剑，还有那把她一直在使用的金柄长剑——这种武器在边境地区绝对是独一无二的。 她还没有注意到你，而且她现在正全神贯注地读着书，你觉得除非你主动示意，否则她是不会注意到你的。

你该怎么办呢？

rows.original: What's the worst that can happen? You push through the bush and into the moth-girl's camp. [pc.bg hunter thief barbarian |Before you get two steps, you find out exactly why she's so confidently absorbed in her tomes — her camp's surrounded by tripwires and snares. Clever girl! But you're just a little more experienced in these things than she is, a benefit of your rough and tumble upbringing; you deftly weave between her traps and step into the clearing. She only notices you when you deign to clear your throat. |You get about two steps past the underbrush before your [pc.foot] steps straight into a snare. With a yelp of surprise, you tumble face-first into the dirt as the sound of jingling metal echoes through the camp. ] With a shriek of her own, the moth-girl nearly tumbles over herself and scrambles back toward her weapon rack, grabbing her silvery blade. She only stops when you put up your hands and tell her that you mean no harm. You just wanted to talk. She freezes, looking nervously over her shoulder to look at you. Slowly, she lowers her sword. "Oh! Goddess, you scared me, [pc.mf |handsome |sweetheart ]!" she sighs, picking her fallen book up from the ground before reaching for a white scarf hanging overhead and waggling it at you. "Flag of truce?" You nod, eliciting a relieved sigh from her. "Good. I enjoy a good fight and fuck as much as the next wildling, but... it's been longer than I care to admit since I last traded words with someone. And... frankly it's getting so dangerous around here that I'm thinking of giving it up." She twirls her blade between her fingers before sliding it into a scabbard at her hip and swinging her legs back over the stump she'd been sitting at. "The name's Lusina, by the way," the moth says, extending a hand. "Lusina en Errion." "[pc.name]," you say. [pc.bg noblescion scholar |"Errion? Isn't that the ruling family of a city-state back south a ways?" Lusina grimaces, eyes darting away from you. "Was... and that was a long time ago. |"En Errion sounds like a noble's name." Lusina forces a chuckle, but her eyes dart away from you. "Maybe it was, once. But that was a long time ago. ] My name doesn't mean much all the way out here in any case. And how about you? That little thorpe on the valley's edge doesn't churn out a [pc.class] like you very often." That it doesn't. You give her the highlights leading up to your arrival here in the valley, though when you start talking about the night you and Cait charged up that blizzard-wracked mountainside, the thief's eyes go wide. "That cult... I've seen 'em before, here in the valley. They've been grabbing people crossing the river, dragging them gods-know-where. Centaur camp, maybe? The lot of 'em seem to be in bed together, anyway." [flags.CQ_CLEAR|She won't have to worry about that any more.|Is that right? Just another reason to head that way and deal with the corrupted centaurs, you suppose.] "Ah, well, good to know somebody's stepping up around here," she says, flashing you a more genuine grin this time. "I was starting to think I'd have to pack up and head for greener pastures. I haven't been scraping by all these years just to get jumped in the night by a buncha evil rape-ponies." You blink at her. "Years? You've been a bandit here for years?" She fidgets, feelers drooping. "Well, not here specifically, but... yeah. I've been on my own a while. As long as I can remember... more than long enough to grow into a woman out here in the wilds." Lusina sighs, bringing her knees up to her chest. A wave of sadness washes over her face, but before you can press the issue, she vigorously shakes her head and claps you on the shoulder, hard enough to make you rock forward. "You didn't come here to get a sob story, though. I'm doin' alright, especially if there's a brave hero out there fighting whatever's making the centaurs and other folk go mad with lust." "In fact," she purrs, [flags.CQ_CLEAR |"Now that you've dealt with the big evil ponies, maybe I ought to take the cue and give up this highwayman act. Now that I've seen what real brigandry is like, I want no part in it. |"If you finish off those evil centaurs, maybe things'll calm down enough for me to be able to start fresh, find something less... harmful... to do with myself. ] Maybe I'll head to the marefolk village, see if they've got space for another topless harrier in the ranks! Come and look me up some time, and I'll show you my gratitude proper-like. For right now, though, I've got something that might help you on your quest. I tend to fly solo, but if you've got friends to cover you, this'll be sure to keep you safe." She hops to her feet and delves a hand into one of the packs hanging up on a branch, and from a band inside it withdraws a simple silver ring adorned with a black gem. "Catch!" You grab it out of the air, and gasp as a faint mist begins to swirl around it, crawling up your arm before dissipating in the breeze. "The witch I got it from says it helps you hide in plain sight... but only if you don't wear much in the way of armor. Something tells me you'll need it more than I do. Now go on and save the world — I'll be [flags.CQ_CLEAR |at the village, if they'll take me, |fine till you've cleared things up at least. Then... then I'll head to the village and see what their old warhorse has to say. Maybe she'll take me in ] thanks to you. No more purse-snatching from me!" As you stand and ready to leave, Lusina wings past you for one last theft — a kiss off your lips before she sends you on your way with a slap on the ass.
rows.translation: 最坏的情况会是什么呢？你穿过灌木丛，进入那个蛾女所在的营地。 [pc.bg hunter thief barbarian |你才走了两步，就立刻明白了她为何能如此专注地研究那些典籍——她的营地周围布满了陷阱和埋伏。真是个聪明的女孩！不过在这些事情上，你确实比她更有经验，这要归功于你那坎坷的成长经历；你熟练地避开了她设置的陷阱，终于走到了空地上。直到你清了清嗓子，她才注意到你的存在。 |你才刚走过灌木丛两步，就…… [pc.foot] 你径直踏入了陷阱。随着一声惊叫，你面朝下摔在了地上，而叮当作响的金属声在营地里回荡。 ] 随着一声自己的尖叫，那个蛾女差点摔倒在地，她慌忙爬回武器架旁，抓起了那把银色的剑。直到你举起手部，告诉她你没有恶意，只是想和她谈谈，她才停了下来。她紧张地回头看着你，慢慢地放下了剑。 “哦！女神啊，你吓死我了…… [pc.mf |英俊的 |亲爱的 ]唉，”她叹了口气，从地上捡起掉落的书，然后伸手部去拿挂在头顶上的白色围巾，摇晃着向你示意：“这是停战信号吗？” 你点了点头，她这才松了一口气：“好。我和其他野人一样，既喜欢激烈的战斗，也喜欢美好的性爱……但是……说实话，我已经很久没有和别人说过话了。而且……这里的环境变得越来越危险，我真的在考虑放弃这个地方了。” 她把刀在手部指间转了几圈，然后将其插回腰间的刀鞘中，接着跨回原本坐着的树桩上。 顺便说一下，我的名字叫卢西娜，”蛾子伸出手部说道，“卢西娜·恩·埃里恩。[pc.name]你是这么说的。 [pc.bg noblescion scholar |埃里恩？那不是南方某个城邦的统治家族吗？” 卢西娜皱起了眉头，目光迅速从你身上移开：“是的……但那已经是很久以前的事了。 |恩·埃里恩听起来像是个贵族的名字。” 卢西娜勉强挤出了笑声，但她的目光立刻从你身上移开了。“也许曾经是吧。不过那已经是很久以前的事了。 ] 反正，在这个地方，我的名字也没什么特别的意义。那你呢？那个位于山谷边缘的小村庄，也没产生什么了不起的人或事吧…… [pc.class] 你经常这样对她说话。” [flags.CQ_CLEAR|她再也不用为此担心了。|是吗？这么说来，又多了一个理由要去那里解决那些被腐蚀的半人马了。] 啊，好吧，很高兴看到有人愿意站出来帮忙，”她说道，这次露出了更加真诚的笑容。“我本来还以为自己得收拾东西，去寻找其他机会了呢。这些年来我辛苦挣扎，可不是为了在夜里被一群邪恶的家伙袭击。” 你愣住了，问道：“多年？你在这里当强盗已经…… 多年她坐立不安，双手部无精打采地搭在膝上。“嗯，不是具体指这里，但是……是的。我已经独自生活了一段时间了。从我记事起就是这样……这个时间长得足以让我在荒野中长大成人。 卢西娜叹了口气，将双膝抱在胸前。一阵悲伤涌上她的面庞，但在你还没来得及追问时，她猛地摇了摇头，然后用力拍了拍你的肩膀，力度之大让你不由得向前倾了一下。 不过，你来这里并不是为了听我的悲叹。我过得还不错，尤其是当有位勇敢的英雄正在与那些让半人马和其他生物陷入疯狂的敌人作斗争的时候。” “事实上，”她轻声说道， [flags.CQ_CLEAR |既然你已经解决了那些邪恶的家伙，或许我也该效仿你的做法，放弃这种强盗行径了。既然我已经见识到了真正的强盗行为是什么样的，我就再也不想参与其中了。 |如果你能把那些邪恶的半人马消灭掉，或许情况就会平静下来，我就能重新开始，找一些不那么……有害……的事情来做。 ] 也许我会去马人村落看看，看看他们是否还能再接纳一个赤膊的猎手部加入他们的行列！有空的时候来找我吧，我会好好感谢你的。 不过，现在我有一些东西可能会对你的任务有所帮助。 我通常喜欢独自行动，但如果有朋友在旁边保护你，那就一定能确保你的安全了。 她站起身来，从挂在树枝上的背包中拿出一个包，从里面的带子中取出一枚简单的银戒指，戒指上镶嵌着一颗黑色的宝石。 抓住它！” 你从空中接住了它，顿时倒吸一口凉气——因为有一股淡淡的雾气开始在它周围旋转，顺着你的手部臂向上蔓延，最终在微风中消散了。“给我这个东西的女巫说，它能帮助你在众人眼前隐藏自己。..但前提是你不要穿戴太多的护甲。我有种预感，你比我更需要它们。现在去拯救世界吧——我会在后面支持的。 [flags.CQ_CLEAR |在那个村庄里，如果他们愿意接纳我的话…… |至少在你把事情弄清楚之前，一切都还好。然后……然后我就去村子，看看他们的那位老前辈有什么要说的。也许她会收留我。 ] 多亏了你，我再也不会遭遇抢包事件了！” 当你站起身准备离开时，卢西娜突然从你身边飞过，又来了一次“偷窃”——在她轻拍你的屁股让你继续上路之前，她在你的嘴唇上留下了一记吻。

"Oh! Goddess, you scared me, [pc.mf |handsome |sweetheart ]!" she sighs, picking her fallen book up from the ground before reaching for a white scarf hanging overhead and waggling it at you. "Flag of truce?" You nod, eliciting a relieved sigh from her. "Good. I enjoy a good fight and fuck as much as the next wildling, but... it's been longer than I care to admit since I last traded words with someone. And... frankly it's getting so dangerous around here that I'm thinking of giving it up." She twirls her blade between her fingers before sliding it into a scabbard at her hip and swinging her legs back over the stump she'd been sitting at. "The name's Lusina, by the way," the moth says, extending a hand. "Lusina en Errion." "[pc.name]," you say. [pc.bg noblescion scholar |"Errion? Isn't that the ruling family of a city-state back south a ways?" Lusina grimaces, eyes darting away from you. "Was... and that was a long time ago. |"En Errion sounds like a noble's name." Lusina forces a chuckle, but her eyes dart away from you. "Maybe it was, once. But that was a long time ago. ] My name doesn't mean much all the way out here in any case. And how about you? That little thorpe on the valley's edge doesn't churn out a [pc.class] like you very often." That it doesn't. You give her the highlights leading up to your arrival here in the valley, though when you start talking about the night you and Cait charged up that blizzard-wracked mountainside, the thief's eyes go wide. "That cult... I've seen 'em before, here in the valley. They've been grabbing people crossing the river, dragging them gods-know-where. Centaur camp, maybe? The lot of 'em seem to be in bed together, anyway." [flags.CQ_CLEAR|She won't have to worry about that any more.|Is that right? Just another reason to head that way and deal with the corrupted centaurs, you suppose.] "Ah, well, good to know somebody's stepping up around here," she says, flashing you a more genuine grin this time. "I was starting to think I'd have to pack up and head for greener pastures. I haven't been scraping by all these years just to get jumped in the night by a buncha evil rape-ponies." You blink at her. "Years? You've been a bandit here for years?" She fidgets, feelers drooping. "Well, not here specifically, but... yeah. I've been on my own a while. As long as I can remember... more than long enough to grow into a woman out here in the wilds." Lusina sighs, bringing her knees up to her chest. A wave of sadness washes over her face, but before you can press the issue, she vigorously shakes her head and claps you on the shoulder, hard enough to make you rock forward. "You didn't come here to get a sob story, though. I'm doin' alright, especially if there's a brave hero out there fighting whatever's making the centaurs and other folk go mad with lust." "In fact," she purrs, [flags.CQ_CLEAR |"Now that you've dealt with the big evil ponies, maybe I ought to take the cue and give up this highwayman act. Now that I've seen what real brigandry is like, I want no part in it. |"If you finish off those evil centaurs, maybe things'll calm down enough for me to be able to start fresh, find something less... harmful... to do with myself. ] Maybe I'll head to the marefolk village, see if they've got space for another topless harrier in the ranks! Come and look me up some time, and I'll show you my gratitude proper-like. For right now, though, I've got something that might help you on your quest. I tend to fly solo, but if you've got friends to cover you, this'll be sure to keep you safe." She hops to her feet and delves a hand into one of the packs hanging up on a branch, and from a band inside it withdraws a simple silver ring adorned with a black gem. "Catch!" You grab it out of the air, and gasp as a faint mist begins to swirl around it, crawling up your arm before dissipating in the breeze. "The witch I got it from says it helps you hide in plain sight... but only if you don't wear much in the way of armor. Something tells me you'll need it more than I do. Now go on and save the world — I'll be [flags.CQ_CLEAR |at the village, if they'll take me, |fine till you've cleared things up at least. Then... then I'll head to the village and see what their old warhorse has to say. Maybe she'll take me in ] thanks to you. No more purse-snatching from me!" As you stand and ready to leave, Lusina wings past you for one last theft — a kiss off your lips before she sends you on your way with a slap on the ass."

rows.original: Go over and try to have a chat with the brigand. Maybe approaching her here will give you a chance to make friends rather than stay as foes.
rows.translation: 过去试着和那个强盗聊聊天吧。也许在这里接近她，会让你有机会和她成为朋友，而不是继续敌对下去。
rows.raw: "Go over and try to have a chat with the brigand. Maybe approaching her here will give you a chance to make friends rather than stay as foes."

rows.original: You withdraw from the little clearing, heading back to the main path. No reason to trigger another fight with the flighty filcher, is there?
rows.translation: 你离开了那个小空地，重新回到了主路上。没有必要再和那个爱惹麻烦的家伙发生冲突，对吧？
rows.raw: "\n        You withdraw from the little clearing, heading back to the main path. No reason to trigger another fight with the flighty filcher, is there?"

rows.original: No reason to bother her. She'll probably just try to assault you, anyway.
rows.translation: 没必要去打扰她。反正她很可能还是会试图攻击你。
rows.raw: "No reason to bother her. She'll probably just try to assault you, anyway."

rows.original:
As you wander the valley, a familiar faint humming sound reaches your ears. Once again, [party.combatNames] ready your weapons — and once again, the busty, purple-winged moth girl descends from the trees to alight right in front of you. This time, though, her sword is still securely in its scabbard, she's wearing a sheepish grin, and even if her breasts are as bare as ever, she's waving a little white scarf in one hand.

    "Hey there!" she chirps. "Um, truce?"
    
    You put away your [pc.weapon]. "[pc.dcb|Hah. Fucking finally, right?|Nice to see you coming around.|Hee hee — I'll shake on it if you will!]"
    
    "Yeah." She proffers her hand, and you take it [pc.isDK|firmly|warmly]. "Life's too short, you know?"
    
    "[pc.isBimbo|Yeah! So are you just coming to say hi?|It is. So, is this just a social call?]"
    
    "I mean, kind of," she laughs. "My camp's not too far away, and I heard you roaming about — figured I'd fly over and say hi. Wanna visit real quick? Rest some weary legs and all that?"
    
    "[pc.isBimbo|That sounds great! Buuuut it wouldn't be right to do that without names first. What's your name, cutie?|Might as well, Miss...?]"
    
    "Lusina! Lusina en Errion. What about you?"
    
    You grin. "[pc.isBimbo
    |I'm [pc.name]! It's so awesome to meet you for realsies this time, Luseeeena!"
    
    "Gods, you're adorable," Lusina giggles. "All right: follow me, [pc.name]."
    |[pc.name], [pc.title]. Lead on, Lusina."
    ]
rows.translation:
当你漫步在山谷中时，一阵熟悉的、微弱的嗡嗡声传入了你的耳中。又一次， [party.combatNames] 准备好你的武器吧——又一次，那个拥有丰满身材、紫色翅膀的蛾女从树上飞下来，落在了你的面前。不过这一次，她的剑仍然牢牢地插在剑鞘里，她脸上带着一丝害羞的笑容，虽然她的胸部依旧裸露着，但她的一只手却挥舞着一条白色的围巾。

“嘿，你好！”她欢快地说道，“嗯，我们可以停战一会儿吗？”

你把武器收了起来…… [pc.weapon]. "[pc.dcb|哈，他妈的，终于等到了，对吧？|很高兴见到你再次光临。|嘻嘻——如果你愿意的话，我们就这么定吧！]嗯。”她伸出了手，你便握住了它。 [pc.isDK|坚定地|热情地]人生苦短，你知道吗？[pc.isBimbo|是啊！那你来主要是为了打个招呼吗？|确实是这样。那么，这仅仅是一次社交聚会而已吗？]嗯，算是吧，”她笑着说，“我的营地离这里不是很远，听说你一直在附近闲逛，所以就想着过来打个招呼。想顺便拜访一下吗？让你那些疲惫的双腿也休息一下吧。”[pc.isBimbo|那听起来太棒了！但是，如果不先知道你的名字，这样做就有点不太合适了。你叫什么名字呢，小可爱？|那就这么办吧，小姐……？]卢西娜！在埃里恩的卢西娜。你呢？”

你露出了微笑。[pc.isBimbo
    |我是 [pc.name]这次能真正见到你，真是太棒了，Luseeeena！”

“天啊，你真是太可爱了，”卢西娜笑着说，“好吧，跟我来吧。 [pc.name]."
    |[pc.name], [pc.title]继续说吧，卢西娜。
    ]
