rows.raw: " [zo.exertionRange 0 1 2 3 ||You relay the motions and you repeat the events that Zo had just demonstrated in your mind over and over as you take your place where she stood. It’s not about the breathing exercises, or the rubbing in your arms, or whatever – there’s a good chance that all that extra movement is just fluff. It’s about something else – something that’s within you, something that you can draw upon, if only you knew how to grasp it. Zo hasn’t mastered it herself, but she’s gotten to the point where she can at least call upon her inner strength, at least after a bit of focus. Still, you go through the motions anyway: Zo had done them before her spectacle of a demonstration, and besides, the repetitive actions help put your mind at ease. When you get to the part where you thrust your hands forward, none of what made Zo’s example so thrilling to see was present: no gusts of wind; no outward pushing force; nothing. Zo, ever the patient teacher, smiles and nods, waving her hand palm-up towards you, imploring you to try again. It’s frustrating to you that she can’t give you any verbal guidance or understanding – but, then again, you can only imagine how frustrating it is for her to not speak ever. You shut your eyes and begin the sequence again. You think of what happened when Zo completed this step of the training, and you think on what she was trying to tell you when she pointed at your chest during your last lesson. Her actions resulted in a force, an exertion upon the world around herself; like she was pushing on everything, in every direction, using only... herself. Not her arms, or her legs, or any part of her physical body. Thinking about literally pushing something with your arms and legs gets you started on a train of thought, though. Why is it that, if you were to physically exert yourself for a period of time, you’d feel tired afterward? There’s some kind of finite resource within yourself that’s being expended when you perform any action like that that’s replenished with things like eating and sleeping. What is this resource? Is that what you’re trying to draw upon? You ruminate on how you can draw upon that finite well of energy the same way Zo had as your fingers begin sprawling down your arms. It’s not enough to just tense your muscles and pretend. You think back to when Zo showed you the world through her eyes, and you saw the world’s energies as flowing, shimmering auras that every living creature, large or small, fauna or flora, emanated. If you’re to accomplish what she had, you need to grasp onto and draw upon that: you need to sacrifice a part of yourself so that you can influence the world around you, whether it’s something as small as striking a dummy standing a few yards away, or something grander. Unbeknownst to you, with your eyes closed, the area around yourself begins to shift. The winds pick up, circling around your form, ruffling your [pc.clothes], shifting the blades of grass around your [pc.feet], and flowing through Zo’s hair. She smiles wryly and cocks her head to one side – no matter how well you do today, she’s proud of your progress and is eager to see how far you go. You’re close to a breakthrough, you can feel it! Your hands make a wide circle around your body, and as they do, you feel yourself change: a pit within your stomach suddenly forms and grows, like a hole that’s feeding on its surroundings and growing larger as the seconds tick by. But, simultaneously, you feel a certain strength begin to rise within yourself: the vacuum that spawned within you was brought by your inner strength being moved, rather than missing or consumed, and all that strength has to go somewhere. When you finally open your eyes, you’ve moved into the striking position that Zo had just before she launched her own energy forward: your hands at your side, pressed together at the base of your palms, with your fingers crooked at the knuckles. Your stance is wide, with your back leg giving you balance and your front leg giving you stability. And it’s only now that you realize that things are rather windy around you. Your strength has pooled into your hands, and you can feel what can only be yourself in an incorporeal-yet-energetic form crackling between your fingertips. The energy is so fierce and potent that you feel like you could punch straight through a block of steel – but that’s not your goal (and you’d probably break every bone in your hand if you tried). Your eyes are locked onto the training dummy just down the path – that is your target. You launch both of your hands forward with the same ferocity that Zo had earlier, attempting to ‘throw’ the building force between your hands at it. The strength between your fingers dissipates; the billowing wind around yourself stops abruptly; and the yawning chasm in your stomach suddenly lurches, consuming more of your self in one bite, before stopping entirely. Yet, you don’t accomplish any more than Zo. In fact, you’ve probably accomplished less: Zo could at least make you shuffle off your balance. She doesn’t even shift in place from your display. And the training dummy, as ever, remains unimpressed. Still, from the way Zo’s smile is spreading on her face, you had made leaps and bounds in your training in this topic. And you have the pit in your stomach to prove it: you pant from the exertion and you rub at your belly, feeling as though... not like you had been punched in the stomach, but rather, something about you is missing. Like it had cost you something to do what you just had. If you could refine this technique and focus it into a point, it could have a more pronounced, more powerful application – but it’d come at a cost. When Zo puts her hand on your shoulder and soothingly rubs it, you know you both have the same idea: that’s enough for one day. |Zo’s movements were smooth, calm, and surely: it wasn’t a matter of confidence in her skill, exactly, but rather, it was more like she was about to state a common, inalienable fact: as sure as the sun will rise tomorrow or that water is wet, she was going to stand in the doorway to her home and she was going to be able to perform this technique with all the poise and practice of a honed master. And now, it’s your turn to follow her example. You may not be at Zo’s level – she’s lived most of her life living this kind of lifestyle and learning these kinds of techniques, but you’ve nonetheless achieved enough mastery of this skill to be able to perform a facsimile of it in the short time you’ve had. You understand the sort of mindset she had when she stood in the spot you’re standing and moved her body the way she was: the question now isn’t whether you can, it’s how well you can. The motions you go through is more of a focus than a catalyst: they’re unnecessary, and you could probably jump straight to the end, where you draw upon your inner energies to fire them forward at your target. But performing them helps you gather yourself, and performing all the steps, from beginning to end, helps remind you the process of gathering yourself to launch as a weapon at your target. It’s good for practice, either way. Referring to it as a ‘process’ makes it feel more mechanical than it is in truth: your body is not some kind of machine that requires each part work in perfect synchronicity, lest the whole thing fall apart. Pulling your energy from within yourself is as automatic a process as breathing, blinking, or walking... although the resulting, yawning pit in your stomach that starts as a pinprick before turning into a hole is still a struggle to get used to. By the time your hands are at your side, and your eyes are open and focused on the training dummy – looking a bit rattled and worn after Zo’s demonstration – the wind has circled around you like a cocoon, blowing in a constant, smooth, clockwise motion around you. It rustles the grass at your feet; it courses through your [pc.clothes] and through your hair; and the force you’re exerting from yourself, like Zo before you, makes her derelict cabin groan as its wood is pushed out of place. It feels just as automatic when you move your hands from your side to outstretched in front of you, your palms facing outward and together at their bases, your fingers crooked at the knuckles. The wind circling you is sucked inward, compressing on your body before focusing into your hands; the force that had been building between your palms is expelled from you with all the ferocity that your body can muster; and, like Zo before you, the grass between you and the training dummy curves outward, your energy arcing through the air and carving a line in the grass as it travels. The force strikes the dummy true: it rattles on its flimsy legs, pushed backward from the sudden onset of force, its hay vest flaking to little more than the odd straw still stubbornly clinging to its skeleton made of less than eight sticks held together with string and smaller sticks. [var0|New Ability: Exertion: Draw upon your inner energies to immediately strike a single target, doing damage equal to the amount of effort you put into it.] You could have put more force into it if you wanted. Like you knew Zo was capable of, you could have obliterated the training dummy by putting more of yourself into the thrust of your energy. But... the strength in your hands is equally matched by the vacancy consuming your torso, starting at your gut and radiating outwards. It costs you something for every iota you put into the strike – you aren’t sure what, exactly, it is, but you know that you need it, and performing this technique is just as dangerous to you as it is to your target. You’ve proven your capability; you don’t need to act recklessly just to one-up Zo. [zo.fucked |Zo steps in behind you, wrapping her arms around you and meeting at your front, just above your [pc.stomach]. She rubs at it soothingly, one hand on top of the other, knowing exactly how it feels. It may not be the kind of ache that goes away from some massaging, but the sentiment is there, and when you lean into her and her touch, she leans back into you, letting you use her for stability. You tell her that she’s the best teacher a student can ask for, and you ask if you’ve done well as her student. She, in her non-verbal response, rests her chin on your shoulder – you can feel her tail wagging rapidly behind herself from the way her hips are grinding against yours, subconsciously or not. You ask her if today’s lessons are over. She nuzzles against you a bit. You ask her if you two deserve a reward – say, a mutual belly rub and massage. And maybe a happy ending to congratulate each other. She takes a deep, shuddering breath through her nose, and she starts kissing at your neck as the fingers of her left hand begin to drop into the waistband of your [pc.lowerGarments]. That’s about all the acquiescence you need. |Zo steps in behind you, wrapping her arms around you and meeting at your stomach, hugging you from behind. While you understand what the training is and what it does, you can hardly put it into words; it might be a bit much for a baby. Still, you asked her for some training, doing whatever it was that she was trying to do to get the flowers to cooperate for her. As you recall, the ‘training’ involved her cupping one of them just beneath the bulb at the top of the stem, and focusing intently on it. Beyond the literal motions and imagery, though, you wouldn’t know where to begin. Sensing your apprehension and confusion, Zo turns her head to you to get your attention. She has a warm smile spread beneath her silver mask; the kind of smile that a person makes when they’re with company they enjoy. It’s the kind of smile you can’t help but reciprocate. She starts by cupping her hands beneath her breasts, her palms facing upward. As she inhales through her nose, she lifts her hands, raising them past the swell of her breasts until her lungs are full; then, she turns her hands outward, both palms facing the flower bed as she exhales through her mouth. You can understand the gist of what it is she’s trying to explain: the practice involves dredging up your inner essence and putting it into the flowers. It’s an easy enough concept to grasp, but... the practice of accomplishing it is going to be a bit trickier. How do you even begin? It would somehow involve the auras that you witnessed when you saw the world through Zo’s eyes back when you first met, but how do you grasp or manipulate your own in order to directly influence another’s for the better? Even though you don’t know where to begin, there’s nothing else to do but to start. You mimic her actions exactly: you cup your hands around your navel and raise them both as you inhale through your nose; then, once your lungs are full, you turn your palms towards the flowers and exhale through your mouth. Naturally, you accomplish very little. Zo doesn’t fare much better than yourself: she’s right back to gently cupping the closest flower beneath its bulb and focusing intently on it. The motion of exhaling onto the flowers clearly wasn’t literal, and she was trying to get a message across without using words, since she can’t. It seems she’s just as lost on how to accomplish the training as you are. That said, as her focus intensifies, the flowers of the bed begin to lean towards her, their stems bending so that the bulbs could get closer, as if she was the sun. None of them are even close to blossoming: each flower’s bulb remains stubbornly shut, hiding their vibrant hues and charming smells. Although maybe that’s for the best. You can only imagine how much pollen you’d have to deal with if every flower were to bloom at once, each of them within arm’s reach of you. The fact that they’re responding to Zo means that she’s on to something – something that you need to emulate if you want to achieve the same results as her. Any start would be better than none. You cup the closest flower by its bulb, and you apply all that you’ve learned in this particular school of training: you need to reach out to this flower’s personal aura with your own, somehow, and you need to influence and accelerate its growth, somehow. Clear as mud. You shut your eyes and focus on what you remember seeing from Zo’s eyes. You remember seeing your own aura emanating from your limbs and across your body; the way it shimmered and rippled on its own around yourself, interlacing with Zo’s without interacting with her own in any meaningful way. You just need to change that: to get your personal energy, your internal ‘self,’ to interact with the flower’s in some meaningful way. Or, perhaps ‘interact’ is too base a term. Maybe it’d be better as ‘communicating’ with the flower: you use your aura to reach out and communicate with one of the world’s most simple creatures and ask, or perhaps bargain, for it to open. [var3|It reminds you somewhat of your training in Zo’s potato patch, where you learned to influence the very earth to move as you wanted, but this is different: it’s one thing to, say, ask a person to step aside, and it’s another to ask them to lift something heavy. They’re similar thoughts and intentions, but in practice, it’s very, very different.|Or... maybe ‘interact’ is too complex a term? Is it simpler than that? It’s just a plant, after all: it’s not like it’s going to respond if you asked it how it’s feeling or whatever. Perhaps reaching out to its aura with your own is a much simpler, much more base and primeval task than you’re making it out to be. Before you met Zo, you wouldn’t have entertained any of these thoughts or possibilities as anything other than fantasy, but here you are, debating on the best tactics on how to reason with a plant. You saw how the world worked through her own eyes, and that memory is the only thing keeping you grounded in how whimsy this whole scenario is.] By the time Zo’s ready to call the training for the day, you’ve meditated on how to interact with the flowers of her garden and how to get them to bloom, and all you’ve learned is how to not accomplish your task. But, that just means you know what doesn’t work. You’ll figure out what does eventually. |You had been thinking on your last session with Zo at the flower garden on and off since it ended. You know what you need to achieve, and you have a vague idea on how to achieve it, but you don’t know how to... get to the part where you achieve it, for lack of better phrasing. It’s a four step process, and you have every step mapped out except step two. Getting to that part is something you’d like to achieve with today’s lesson, ideally. Zo, for her part, is quick to jump straight into the training herself: she doesn’t bother going through the motions of breathing deeply and making the motions with her hands, and instead, goes right to the part where she cups the flower’s bud and begins to focus on it. Although her demeanor has noticeably changed: before, she would stare intently at the flower and she’d focus on it so much that she’d nearly start to shake at how tense and eager she was to get the damn thing to bloom. Now, she’s much calmer and composed: she went straight into this lesson with... perhaps not a plan, exactly, but, a change in attitude and a clearer mind. Maybe that’s what you were missing. Previously, you had spent so much time thinking on how you could accomplish your goal that you neglected to actually try and do it. You still don’t even know where to start, but even going into the training with the gumption to start, regardless of whether or not you can, might be better than just thinking on it. You follow Zo’s example, gingerly gripping the nearest flower by its stem and pulling it towards you. You cup your hands beneath its bulb, and you close your eyes and you relax your body: you may not be able to see the world like Zo can without her help, but you at least remember how the world looked when you did, and you can visualize it well enough. You try and picture your aura as an extension of yourself: a limb that you could reach out and grasp things with, and that the flower’s own aura is an extension of itself, waiting to latch onto yours. It’s easy to visualize, but there’s a missing ingredient: something vital to the recipe that makes the whole thing more than a daydream. It’s a thing that you can do, you know that, and the concept of trying to ‘reach out’ to the flower feels like you’re on the right track, but.... You open your eyes and turn to Zo, to see how well she’s doing and whether she’s made any progress. Like before, the flowers in the bed are all curved at their stems, trying to guide their bulbs towards her; but, more than that, the flower in her hand, as proof of her growing expertise on the subject, begins to bloom. Each petal unfurls simultaneously at a slower pace than you’d expect from a natural bloom, but, nonetheless, it opens to Zo until you see the dark-brown center of its style and the long, thin feelers of its stamen. When she releases the flower, it bounds on the strength of its stem, standing upright – but it, like every flower around it, subtly leans toward her, looking for more. Maybe she’s doing something similar: she’s emanating her energies for the flowers to seek out themselves, and once she has one within her aura’s reach, she can work from there to get the flower to bloom. Maybe you’ve had it backwards this whole time: you shouldn’t have been trying to seek out the flowers yourself – you should have given the flowers a reason to seek out you. It’s not like a typical lack of energy, where you’re tired after a hard day’s work: it’s more like... you’re removing something that belongs to yourself. Where you once had something within you that you needed to function – something invisible, nameless, and incorporeal, but necessary all the same, like oxygen – you feel weaker and hollow as that something evaporates from your body the longer you keep up this particular form of meditation. Yet... you feel motion in your palms. When you open your eyes, the petals of the bud in your hand have slowly begun to unfurl. It’s even slower than Zo’s, and, in fact, once you dumbly focus on the flower, it stops blooming entirely and rests in your hand in a half-open state. But it started. And some of the flowers around you – not all of them, but some of them – have started to lean towards you. They’ve noticed your energy, and they’ve started seeking you out of their own volition, just as they had done with Zo. You release the flower, letting it bound on its stem as it rights itself. The chasm yawning inside you has stopped for now, and even now, you feel the gap inside you slowly refilling over time. It’s going to take a little bit, but you’ll be back to feeling whole before tomorrow begins. Zo puts her hand on your shoulder and smiles warmly at you. You’ve made great progress today, and it’s clear from the way she’s looking at you that she’s proud of your accomplishment. It’s time to end today’s training on a high note. |The progress you had made the last time you practiced this particular school of training was really promising: you successfully managed to get the flower to... not bloom, that’s too generous a word. You got its petals to unfurl in your hand. But it’s better than no progress! If you hadn’t achieved anything, the flower would have remained shut and closed the entire time it stayed in your hands. Zo is apparently just as eager to get started: she kneels in front of the flower bed, her hands resting on her knees, and she closes her eyes, going right into her meditative state. She doesn’t waste any time: almost as soon as her eyes shut, her braided hair begins to lift into the air behind her skull, levitating by the bulbous ends. And, shortly after they do, half the flowers in the bed closest to her lean towards her, guided by the personal energies she’s emitting, and, one by one, starting with the closest and ended with the farthest, they begin to bloom: before, the flower bed was just a plain, almost ugly set of green, featureless stalks with fat tips swaying in the wind; now, you’re treated to a veritable banquet of colors and scents as the petals stretch open for her. She made it look so effortless: all she did was sit on her knees and focus, and suddenly, all the flowers reacted to her like they hadn’t seen the sun in all their lives. With just a little bit of focus on her inner energies, she had managed to reach out to each and every flower in her half of the bed, and they bloomed, just like that. Last time, you came to the conclusion that you couldn’t try to reach out to the flowers via their own auras with your own, and that, in order to achieve any results, you needed to give them a reason to seek you. Given Zo’s results, and how quickly she managed to make it work, it’s easy to think that you only have half the answers; that maybe you had the right idea before, but the wrong execution. Or maybe you were missing something altogether. Still, there’s not much else to do but to get to it. This is the training you wanted from her today. You kneel in front of your half of the flower bed, just as she had. You think to cup the nearest flower bulb in your hands, but Zo just demonstrated that she didn’t need to, so you shouldn’t need to, either. You shut your eyes, and you start the way you had learned how to find what you sought: by making you and your energies desirable to the flowers; to make them want to find you. Like before, the way you put out your energies, radiating them into the air, is quickly exhausting you: you still don’t understand what, precisely, it’s costing you to do this. Your body feels as though you’re running a marathon, but without the heavy breathing and panting you need to supplant the exhaustion; your muscles ache and your body feels heavy as you continue the technique, and the longer you go, the more you yearn for a pillow to rest your head on. But it works, just like it had before: you don’t have the flower in your hand for you to physically feel as it blooms, but you can just tell, through whatever extrasensory gift your aura is giving you, that the flowers in your half of the bed have noticed your emanating aura, and they are responding to it, seeking you out for their nourishment. You try and focus on the sensation of the flowers and their own auras pulling on you, seeking you out now that you’ve made yourself visible to them. Now that you know where they are, and now that you’ve managed to ‘hook’ into them, you don’t need to expend so much energy making yourself visible – you picture a torch, or maybe a lighthouse, and how it lights up everything around it, but if you were to put something to one side of the light, it would focus the light in the opposite direction, making it more powerful.[silly | Actually, that’s not a bad idea for a lighthouse design. Maybe you should look into that. ] With your eyes closed, you don’t have a sense of direction when it comes to the auras of the flowers; you don’t see them as ‘in front of you,’ nor as ‘behind’ or ‘beside’ you. But you can feel each one individually in the void, now that they’ve connected with you: and you have the spatial awareness to not send your energy in any other direction except straight to them. While the technique is still exhausting to perform, the difference one little change like that makes is astounding. It’s the difference between a light jog and a full sprint. When you open your eyes, you’re greeted with the sight of... most of the flowers in the bed blooming in your direction. Some of them remain stubbornly closed, and it’s not the farthest ones: some of the un-bloomed flowers are within your arm’s reach. ‘Distance’ may not be such a large factor as ‘visibility,’ for as strenuous a term as that is when your eyes are closed and you’re focused on the dark void. But you’ve done it. You’ve mastered this technique – maybe not to the degree that Zo has, but about as well as you could ever hope to have it, unless you intend to devote your life to the practice like she has. rows.translation: 你询问佐关于她在照料花朵时所遵循的训练计划。 [var2 |根据你对她看待世界的方式的了解，以及她认为每一株植物和生物都拥有属于自己的能量光环这一观点，可以推测，她所做的任何事情肯定都与操控这些花朵的能量有关——也许是为了让它们提前开花吧？你虽然不是植物学家，但既然现在这些花还没有开放，那就说明现在肯定不是它们的开花季节，而她正在试图加速这个过程。 |你知道，她是通过运用自身的能量来加速这一自然过程，从而促使花朵绽放的——有些人可能会认为这种做法违背了自然规律，但事实上，这种技术在现实世界中有着许多实际应用。当你第一次见到她的时候，她就曾用这种方法治愈了自己在战斗中受到的严重伤势；治愈自己与治愈他人虽然有所不同，但并没有理由认为这种方法是不可行的。 [var0 |优化 |学习 ] 这种技术。 ] [flags.ZO_BAB_RANDO |佐点了点头，弯下腰，用手抓住瓦伊的腋下，将他抱在怀里，然后转身往回走去。 [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|房子|简陋的小屋]这次你打算进行的训练并不危险——而且考虑到它的性质，让Vai参加反而可能有益——但毕竟，他仍然只是个婴儿，几乎还不清楚自己身处何处、正在做什么。虽然你明白这种训练的具体内容及其作用，但却很难用语言来描述它；对一个婴儿来说，这种训练或许有些过于艰巨了。 当她从……中重新出现时…… [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|家|简陋的小屋] 在没有瓦伊的情况下——大概是因为她当时正在把瓦伊放在婴儿床里——她抓住你的手部腕，拉着你跟在她身后，然后带你去了她果园南侧的那片花田。这片花田其实并不大：它的面积大概只占她整个果园总面积的一半而已。 [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|小屋|破败的小屋]但是，它的每一寸地方都开满了尚未绽放的花朵，你根本无法分辨这些花到底是什么品种的（其实，你本来也就无从分辨吧）。 如果 他们就是这样的。 |佐点了点头，轻轻抓住你的手部腕，拉着你走在她身后，引领你前往她果园南侧的那片花田。这片花田其实并不大：它的面积大概只占她整个果园总面积的一半而已。 [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3||破败不堪 |佐将你带到花坛边，双膝跪地，然后拉着你也跪在她身旁。这一幕简直充满浪漫气息：你和佐一起准备照料这个花园，共度时光。你甚至可以稍微靠近她一些，把头靠在她的肩上，这样她就能明白你其实更想跳过这次训练——而如果她同意的话，你也不会感到惊讶。 不过，你还是请求她进行一些训练，让她尝试那些能让花朵配合她行动的方法。你应该还记得，那种“训练”就是让她把杯子放在花朵茎部顶端的球茎下方，然后全神贯注地盯着它。不过，除了这些具体的动作和场景之外，你真的不知道该从哪里入手才好。 感受到你的忧虑与困惑，佐转过头来吸引你的注意。她的银色面具下露出温暖的笑容——那种只有在与自己喜欢的人在一起时才会出现的笑容。这种笑容会让人不由自主地回以微笑。 她首先将双手放在胸前，手掌朝上。当她通过鼻子吸气时，将双手抬起，让它们高于胸部的位置，直到肺部充满空气；然后，在通过嘴巴呼气时，将双手向外展开，手掌朝向花坛的方向。 想要找到 你。 和之前一样，你将能量释放到空气中，这种方式会让你迅速感到疲惫：你仍然没有明白这一点。 什么？ 确切地说，这样做确实会让你付出代价。你的身体会感觉就像在参加马拉松一样，但却没有那种因剧烈呼吸和喘息来缓解疲劳的感觉；你的肌肉会疼痛，身体也会变得重型，而当你继续坚持这种练习时，这种不适感会越来越强烈，你甚至会越来越渴望能有一个枕头来依靠。 不过，这种方法确实有效，就像以前一样：虽然你手部中并没有那朵花，因此无法真正感受到它绽放的情景，但你仍然可以…… 告诉吧。 无论你的气场赋予你何种超感官能力，那些位于你床铺这一侧的花朵肯定已经察觉到了你散发出的气场，并且正在对此作出反应，它们正在寻找你，以获取养分。 你努力集中注意力，去感受那些花朵以及它们自身气场对你产生的牵引力——既然你已经让自己变得对它们可见了，它们自然就会来找你。 现在你知道它们的位置了，也成功与它们建立了联系，因此你不再需要耗费那么多精力来让自己显眼了。你可以想象一支火炬，或者一座灯塔，它如何照亮周围的一切；但如果你将某个物体放在轻型源的一侧，轻型线就会被引导到相反的方向，从而变得更为强烈。[silly | 其实，这个想法用来设计灯塔倒也不错。你不妨考虑一下。 ] 当你闭上眼睛时，就无法根据花朵散发的气场来判断方向了；你既感觉不到它们就在“自己面前”，也意识不到它们是在“身后”或“身旁”。然而，现在这些气场已经与你产生了联系，你能够在虚空中逐一感受到它们的存在——于是，你就拥有了相应的空间感知能力。 不是 把你的精力投入到其他方面去吧。 除了……之外 直接告诉他们。 虽然这种技巧在执行过程中仍然会让人感到疲惫，但像这样小小的一个改变所带来的效果却是惊人的。这就好比在慢跑和全速冲刺之间的区别。 当你睁开眼睛时，映入眼帘的将是…… 大多数 花坛里那些朝向你方向绽放的花朵中，有些依然固执地紧闭着，而且那些花朵并不在远处：有些尚未开放的花朵其实就在你伸手部可及的范围之内。当你的双眼紧闭，专注于那片暗影的空虚时，“距离”或许并不是那么重要的因素，而“可见性”才才是真正的关键。 但是你确实做到了。你已经将这项技术掌握得炉火纯青——也许没有Zo那么精通，但已经达到了你所能期望的最好水平，除非你打算像她那样将一生都奉献给这项练习。 [zo.fucked |佐摇摇晃晃地朝你走来，逐渐缩短你们之间的距离，但她既没有转头去看那些花朵，也没有站起来。当你们坐到彼此肩并肩的位置时，她把脸颊贴在你的肩膀上，另一只手臂则绕到你的背后，手指勾住了你裤子的腰带。 [pc.lowerGarment]. |佐慢慢地朝你挪了挪身体，靠近了你一点，想要亲眼看看你们俩为把这个花坛打造成现在的样子所付出的一切努力所带来的成果。 ] 你们俩都为这件事付出了很多努力，而她只是想和大家一起享受这段时轻型而已。 [zo.fucked |恋人 |最受喜爱的学生 ] 毕竟，再过一段时间他们就会进入淡季了。 ]
rows.raw: " You ask Zo about the training regimen she does when she tends to her flowers. [var2 |Given what you know about how she perceives the world and how every living creature and plant has its own energy aura, whatever she’s trying to do, it must involve manipulating the energy of the flowers – maybe, to make them bloom prematurely? You aren’t a botanist, but they must not be in season if they aren’t blooming now, and she’s trying to jumpstart the process. |You know that she’s coaxing the flower into blooming by using her personal energies to accelerate the natural process – some might consider it an affront to the natural order, but the reality is that a technique like that has a multitude of real-world, in-the-field applications. She once healed a slashing wound she had taken in combat when you first met her; healing oneself is different from healing another, but there’s no reason why you can’t [var0 |refine |learn ] this technique. ] [flags.ZO_BAB_RANDO |Zo nods and bends over to pick up Vai by his armpits, cradling him in her arms as she heads back into the [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|house|shack]. The training that you had in mind this time isn’t a dangerous one – and it might actually be beneficial to include Vai, given its nature – but, all the same, he’s still just a baby, hardly even aware of where he is or what he’s doing. While you understand what the training is and what it does, you can hardly put it into words; it might be a bit much for a baby. When she re-emerges from her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|home|shack] without Vai, presumably putting him in his crib, she grabs you by the wrist, pulling you behind herself as she guides you to her flower patch at the south side of her grove. The patch itself isn’t especially large: it takes up maybe half the total surface area of her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|cabin|dilapidated hut]. But every inch of it is covered in flowers that aren’t blooming, and you can’t tell what kind of flowers they are (not that you could even if they were). |Zo nods and gently grabs you by the wrist, pulling you behind herself as she guides you to her flower patch at the south side of her grove. The patch itself isn’t especially large: it takes up maybe half the total surface area of her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3||dilapidated ]hut. But every inch of it is covered in flowers that aren’t blooming, and you can’t tell what kind of flowers they are (not that you could even if they were). ] [zo.guidanceRange 0 1 2 3 |Zo brings you to the flower bed’s edge and kneels, dropping to her knees in front of it and pulling you down to join her by the wrist. It’s almost a romantic scene: you and Zo, about to tend to a flower garden to pass the time together. You could probably shuffle a bit closer to her and lay your head on her shoulder to signal to her that you’d rather skip the training, and you wouldn’t be surprised if she agreed. Still, you asked her for some training, doing whatever it was that she was trying to do to get the flowers to cooperate for her. As you recall, the ‘training’ involved her cupping one of them just beneath the bulb at the top of the stem, and focusing intently on it. Beyond the literal motions and imagery, though, you wouldn’t know where to begin. Sensing your apprehension and confusion, Zo turns her head to you to get your attention. She has a warm smile spread beneath her silver mask; the kind of smile that a person makes when they’re with company they enjoy. It’s the kind of smile you can’t help but reciprocate. She starts by cupping her hands beneath her breasts, her palms facing upward. As she inhales through her nose, she lifts her hands, raising them past the swell of her breasts until her lungs are full; then, she turns her hands outward, both palms facing the flower bed as she exhales through her mouth. You can understand the gist of what it is she’s trying to explain: the practice involves dredging up your inner essence and putting it into the flowers. It’s an easy enough concept to grasp, but... the practice of accomplishing it is going to be a bit trickier. How do you even begin? It would somehow involve the auras that you witnessed when you saw the world through Zo’s eyes back when you first met, but how do you grasp or manipulate your own in order to directly influence another’s for the better? Even though you don’t know where to begin, there’s nothing else to do but to start. You mimic her actions exactly: you cup your hands around your navel and raise them both as you inhale through your nose; then, once your lungs are full, you turn your palms towards the flowers and exhale through your mouth. Naturally, you accomplish very little. Zo doesn’t fare much better than yourself: she’s right back to gently cupping the closest flower beneath its bulb and focusing intently on it. The motion of exhaling onto the flowers clearly wasn’t literal, and she was trying to get a message across without using words, since she can’t. It seems she’s just as lost on how to accomplish the training as you are. That said, as her focus intensifies, the flowers of the bed begin to lean towards her, their stems bending so that the bulbs could get closer, as if she was the sun. None of them are even close to blossoming: each flower’s bulb remains stubbornly shut, hiding their vibrant hues and charming smells. Although maybe that’s for the best. You can only imagine how much pollen you’d have to deal with if every flower were to bloom at once, each of them within arm’s reach of you. The fact that they’re responding to Zo means that she’s on to something – something that you need to emulate if you want to achieve the same results as her. Any start would be better than none. You cup the closest flower by its bulb, and you apply all that you’ve learned in this particular school of training: you need to reach out to this flower’s personal aura with your own, somehow, and you need to influence and accelerate its growth, somehow. Clear as mud. You shut your eyes and focus on what you remember seeing from Zo’s eyes. You remember seeing your own aura emanating from your limbs and across your body; the way it shimmered and rippled on its own around yourself, interlacing with Zo’s without interacting with her own in any meaningful way. You just need to change that: to get your personal energy, your internal ‘self,’ to interact with the flower’s in some meaningful way. Or, perhaps ‘interact’ is too base a term. Maybe it’d be better as ‘communicating’ with the flower: you use your aura to reach out and communicate with one of the world’s most simple creatures and ask, or perhaps bargain, for it to open. [var3|It reminds you somewhat of your training in Zo’s potato patch, where you learned to influence the very earth to move as you wanted, but this is different: it’s one thing to, say, ask a person to step aside, and it’s another to ask them to lift something heavy. They’re similar thoughts and intentions, but in practice, it’s very, very different.|Or... maybe ‘interact’ is too complex a term? Is it simpler than that? It’s just a plant, after all: it’s not like it’s going to respond if you asked it how it’s feeling or whatever. Perhaps reaching out to its aura with your own is a much simpler, much more base and primeval task than you’re making it out to be. Before you met Zo, you wouldn’t have entertained any of these thoughts or possibilities as anything other than fantasy, but here you are, debating on the best tactics on how to reason with a plant. You saw how the world worked through her own eyes, and that memory is the only thing keeping you grounded in how whimsy this whole scenario is.] By the time Zo’s ready to call the training for the day, you’ve meditated on how to interact with the flowers of her garden and how to get them to bloom, and all you’ve learned is how to not accomplish your task. But, that just means you know what doesn’t work. You’ll figure out what does eventually. |You had been thinking on your last session with Zo at the flower garden on and off since it ended. You know what you need to achieve, and you have a vague idea on how to achieve it, but you don’t know how to... get to the part where you achieve it, for lack of better phrasing. It’s a four step process, and you have every step mapped out except step two. Getting to that part is something you’d like to achieve with today’s lesson, ideally. Zo, for her part, is quick to jump straight into the training herself: she doesn’t bother going through the motions of breathing deeply and making the motions with her hands, and instead, goes right to the part where she cups the flower’s bud and begins to focus on it. Although her demeanor has noticeably changed: before, she would stare intently at the flower and she’d focus on it so much that she’d nearly start to shake at how tense and eager she was to get the damn thing to bloom. Now, she’s much calmer and composed: she went straight into this lesson with... perhaps not a plan, exactly, but, a change in attitude and a clearer mind. Maybe that’s what you were missing. Previously, you had spent so much time thinking on how you could accomplish your goal that you neglected to actually try and do it. You still don’t even know where to start, but even going into the training with the gumption to start, regardless of whether or not you can, might be better than just thinking on it. You follow Zo’s example, gingerly gripping the nearest flower by its stem and pulling it towards you. You cup your hands beneath its bulb, and you close your eyes and you relax your body: you may not be able to see the world like Zo can without her help, but you at least remember how the world looked when you did, and you can visualize it well enough. You try and picture your aura as an extension of yourself: a limb that you could reach out and grasp things with, and that the flower’s own aura is an extension of itself, waiting to latch onto yours. It’s easy to visualize, but there’s a missing ingredient: something vital to the recipe that makes the whole thing more than a daydream. It’s a thing that you can do, you know that, and the concept of trying to ‘reach out’ to the flower feels like you’re on the right track, but.... You open your eyes and turn to Zo, to see how well she’s doing and whether she’s made any progress. Like before, the flowers in the bed are all curved at their stems, trying to guide their bulbs towards her; but, more than that, the flower in her hand, as proof of her growing expertise on the subject, begins to bloom. Each petal unfurls simultaneously at a slower pace than you’d expect from a natural bloom, but, nonetheless, it opens to Zo until you see the dark-brown center of its style and the long, thin feelers of its stamen. When she releases the flower, it bounds on the strength of its stem, standing upright – but it, like every flower around it, subtly leans toward her, looking for more. The way the flowers all seek Zo out reminds you again of the sun, and how plants tend to grow in the direction the sunlight is most readily available to them for their sustenance. Maybe she’s doing something similar: she’s emanating her energies for the flowers to seek out themselves, and once she has one within her aura’s reach, she can work from there to get the flower to bloom. Maybe you’ve had it backwards this whole time: you shouldn’t have been trying to seek out the flowers yourself – you should have given the flowers a reason to seek out you. Rather than try and search for something in the world that Zo can see and you can’t, you instead try to visualize your aura as expanding, reaching out in all directions: your personal energies radiate into the open air around you, broadcasting to the flowers in the bed that you are a source of energy that they can utilize for themselves. The longer that it goes, the faster a sensation of exhaustion creeps up on you. It’s not like a typical lack of energy, where you’re tired after a hard day’s work: it’s more like... you’re removing something that belongs to yourself. Where you once had something within you that you needed to function – something invisible, nameless, and incorporeal, but necessary all the same, like oxygen – you feel weaker and hollow as that something evaporates from your body the longer you keep up this particular form of meditation. Yet... you feel motion in your palms. When you open your eyes, the petals of the bud in your hand have slowly begun to unfurl. It’s even slower than Zo’s, and, in fact, once you dumbly focus on the flower, it stops blooming entirely and rests in your hand in a half-open state. But it started. And some of the flowers around you – not all of them, but some of them – have started to lean towards you. They’ve noticed your energy, and they’ve started seeking you out of their own volition, just as they had done with Zo. You release the flower, letting it bound on its stem as it rights itself. The chasm yawning inside you has stopped for now, and even now, you feel the gap inside you slowly refilling over time. It’s going to take a little bit, but you’ll be back to feeling whole before tomorrow begins. Zo puts her hand on your shoulder and smiles warmly at you. You’ve made great progress today, and it’s clear from the way she’s looking at you that she’s proud of your accomplishment. It’s time to end today’s training on a high note. |The progress you had made the last time you practiced this particular school of training was really promising: you successfully managed to get the flower to... not bloom, that’s too generous a word. You got its petals to unfurl in your hand. But it’s better than no progress! If you hadn’t achieved anything, the flower would have remained shut and closed the entire time it stayed in your hands. Zo is apparently just as eager to get started: she kneels in front of the flower bed, her hands resting on her knees, and she closes her eyes, going right into her meditative state. She doesn’t waste any time: almost as soon as her eyes shut, her braided hair begins to lift into the air behind her skull, levitating by the bulbous ends. And, shortly after they do, half the flowers in the bed closest to her lean towards her, guided by the personal energies she’s emitting, and, one by one, starting with the closest and ended with the farthest, they begin to bloom: before, the flower bed was just a plain, almost ugly set of green, featureless stalks with fat tips swaying in the wind; now, you’re treated to a veritable banquet of colors and scents as the petals stretch open for her. She made it look so effortless: all she did was sit on her knees and focus, and suddenly, all the flowers reacted to her like they hadn’t seen the sun in all their lives. With just a little bit of focus on her inner energies, she had managed to reach out to each and every flower in her half of the bed, and they bloomed, just like that. Last time, you came to the conclusion that you couldn’t try to reach out to the flowers via their own auras with your own, and that, in order to achieve any results, you needed to give them a reason to seek you. Given Zo’s results, and how quickly she managed to make it work, it’s easy to think that you only have half the answers; that maybe you had the right idea before, but the wrong execution. Or maybe you were missing something altogether. Still, there’s not much else to do but to get to it. This is the training you wanted from her today. You kneel in front of your half of the flower bed, just as she had. You think to cup the nearest flower bulb in your hands, but Zo just demonstrated that she didn’t need to, so you shouldn’t need to, either. You shut your eyes, and you start the way you had learned how to find what you sought: by making you and your energies desirable to the flowers; to make them want to find you. Like before, the way you put out your energies, radiating them into the air, is quickly exhausting you: you still don’t understand what, precisely, it’s costing you to do this. Your body feels as though you’re running a marathon, but without the heavy breathing and panting you need to supplant the exhaustion; your muscles ache and your body feels heavy as you continue the technique, and the longer you go, the more you yearn for a pillow to rest your head on. But it works, just like it had before: you don’t have the flower in your hand for you to physically feel as it blooms, but you can just tell, through whatever extrasensory gift your aura is giving you, that the flowers in your half of the bed have noticed your emanating aura, and they are responding to it, seeking you out for their nourishment. You try and focus on the sensation of the flowers and their own auras pulling on you, seeking you out now that you’ve made yourself visible to them. Now that you know where they are, and now that you’ve managed to ‘hook’ into them, you don’t need to expend so much energy making yourself visible – you picture a torch, or maybe a lighthouse, and how it lights up everything around it, but if you were to put something to one side of the light, it would focus the light in the opposite direction, making it more powerful.[silly | Actually, that’s not a bad idea for a lighthouse design. Maybe you should look into that. ] With your eyes closed, you don’t have a sense of direction when it comes to the auras of the flowers; you don’t see them as ‘in front of you,’ nor as ‘behind’ or ‘beside’ you. But you can feel each one individually in the void, now that they’ve connected with you: and you have the spatial awareness to not send your energy in any other direction except straight to them. While the technique is still exhausting to perform, the difference one little change like that makes is astounding. It’s the difference between a light jog and a full sprint. When you open your eyes, you’re greeted with the sight of... most of the flowers in the bed blooming in your direction. Some of them remain stubbornly closed, and it’s not the farthest ones: some of the un-bloomed flowers are within your arm’s reach. ‘Distance’ may not be such a large factor as ‘visibility,’ for as strenuous a term as that is when your eyes are closed and you’re focused on the dark void. But you’ve done it. You’ve mastered this technique – maybe not to the degree that Zo has, but about as well as you could ever hope to have it, unless you intend to devote your life to the practice like she has. rows.original: You enter Zo’s grove, her little pocket of paradise on the north side of the valley. It’s a path you’ve taken enough times by now that you memorize the layout perfectly, from the little crests and bumps in the walkway from a nearby tree’s root bulging up underneath, to the minor twists and curves in the walkway. When you enter the grove proper, Zo herself isn’t difficult to find: she’s in the back of the area, on the grassy, unoccupied section that you and she have done dozens of training sessions on by now. Her legs are crossed and her hands are together, pressed against each other at the bottoms of her palms and her fingers pointed in opposite directions. It’s not an unfamiliar pose – and the fact that she’s floating a few feet off the ground isn’t even that alarming a sight for you. Zo is capable of a lot of things you would never have guessed were possible until now. This time is slightly different, though: a number of rocks and pebbles, each of varying sizes and shapes, are floating in a wide circle around Zo in crisscrossing orbits. The braids of her hair are standing on their ends, lifting up above her skull and pointing into the sky, held perfectly still on nothing. Her clothes do not hang off her arms or legs, but they don’t lift upward like her hair does: they’re kept perfectly still on her body, covering her without touching her. But what’s most drawing to her and her state is her eyes: gone are her usual emerald-green irises, and they haven’t been replaced by the shimmering silver you sometimes see when she uses her mystic powers on something. Instead, her eyes are replaced entirely with a muted silver: there is no iris and there is no pupil. Light shines through her eyes, illuminating the silver on her mask and sprawling into the grass in front of her. You approach her and call her name, but she doesn’t respond. You walk through the outer rings of the orbiting rocks, knocking them out of position, only for them to float right back into place once you’re through. You say her name again, but she doesn’t acknowledge your presence – she doesn’t even blink. You aren’t positive she’s breathing. You try to put your hands on her body, to shake her out of whatever trance she’s in (not that she wouldn’t be able to ignore it, given her inner tranquility, something that you helped her master), but your fingers don’t make it to her clothes or her fur; they stop a few inches away, held back by an unseen force that wraps around her like a bubble. Nothing you do can get her to react to your very existence. She ignores you every time you shout in her ear; throwing things at her, like clumps of dirt or the rocks from the orbits around her, stop inches from her body. You can’t even get her outfit dirty. Desperate, you try and throw a punch at her, but your fist sinks into the force surrounding her, absorbing the strike like you had just punched some snow. There is one more method that you can try, but you aren’t certain if it would be any more effective than anything else. You’ve learned how to master your personal energy and things like how you can use it to influence the world around yourself, or how to guide the energy of something else to move in a way that you want. Going up against Zo would be like [pc.isDK |pissing into the ocean |trying to find a needle in a haystack, and you’re a needle yourself ], but... well, if her training has taught you anything, it’s that damn near anything is possible with some lateral thinking.
rows.translation: 你走进了佐的小树林——那片位于山谷北侧的世外桃源。这条小路你已经走过太多次了，以至于早已将它的布局熟记于心：从附近一棵树的树根在小路上凸出的小土包，到小路中那些细微的转弯之处，无一不了如指掌。 当你走进那片树林时，找到佐本人并不困难：她就在树林的后面，那片长满草、没有人居住的地方。你们之前已经在那里进行过几十次训练了。她双腿交叉坐着，双手部交叠放在掌心处，手部指朝相反的方向伸着。 这个姿势对你来说并不陌生，而她悬浮在离地面几英尺的高度这一事实，也并不会让你感到太过惊慌。佐能够做出许多你此前根本无法想象的事情来。 不过，这一次有些不同：许多大小形状各异的岩石和鹅卵石在佐周围划着交叉的轨道，呈一个宽阔的圆形漂浮着。她的头发完全竖了起来，高高耸立在头骨上方，指向天空，却仿佛被什么东西牢牢固定在那里，一动不动。她的衣服也没有悬挂在手部臂或腿上，也没有像头发那样向上飘起，而是紧紧贴在她的身体上，将她完全包裹起来，却丝毫没有碰到她的皮肤。 但最吸引她以及令她处于这种状态的，其实是她的双眼：她那惯常的翠绿色虹膜已经消失了，取而代之的也不是她在使用神秘力量时偶尔会显现出的那种闪烁银轻型。她的双眼完全被一种暗淡的银色所取代——既没有虹膜，也没有瞳孔。轻型线穿过她的双眼，照亮了她面具上的银色装饰，同时也洒在了她足部前的草地上。 你走近她，叫她的名字，但她没有回应。你穿过那些绕轨道运行的岩石的外围，将它们撞得偏离了原来的位置，但当你走过去后，它们又会自动回到原来的位置。你再次叫她的名字，但她依然没有注意到你的存在——她甚至没有眨一下眼。 你不确定她是否还在呼吸。你试图把手部放在她的身上，试图把她从那种恍惚状态中唤醒过来（不过，考虑到她内心的平静——这种平静正是你帮助她培养出来的——她其实完全可以无视外界的干扰），但你的手部指却无法触碰到她的衣服或毛发；它们在距离她的身体几英寸的地方就被某种无形的力量挡住了，这种力量仿佛一层气泡一样将她包裹了起来。 无论你做什么，都无法让她对你这个存在的存在产生任何反应。每次你在她耳边大喊，她都会选择无视你；即使你朝她扔泥块或周围轨道上飞来的石头，那些东西也会在离她身体几英寸的地方停下来，根本无法弄脏她的衣服。绝望之下，你试图朝她挥出一拳，但你的拳头却仿佛陷入了包围她的某种力量之中，那力量将你的攻击完全吸收了，就像你刚刚打在了一团雪上一样。 有 是 还有另一种方法你可以尝试，不过你并不确定这种方法是否会比其他方法更有效。你已经学会了如何掌控自己的能量，也知道了如何利用这种能量来影响周围的世界，或者如何引导其他事物的能量朝你期望的方向发展。但与Zo对抗的话……那就另当别论了。 [pc.isDK |在海洋里撒尿——白费力气 |这简直就像在干草堆里找针一样，简直毫无希望。 你是 自己动手做吧。 ]但是……嗯，如果她的训练真的教会了你什么的话，那就是：只要运用一些创新的思维方式，几乎什么事情都是有可能做到的。

rows.original: You sit in front of Zo, taking the same sitting pose as her, and you close your eyes. You try to focus on your personal energies, and, drawing on your lessons with her in front of the flower garden, you think to try and ‘cast out’ your aura, so that you’re as visible to her as you can be. Almost immediately, you ‘find’ her own aura. It’s massive; the force and the energies that she’s putting out immediately dwarfs your own. If you were the sun to the flowers during that one training session, then you are the flower to Zo. As soon as your energies meet in the void, they hook into each other, just as you had done to the flowers, but you feel like yours are being dragged and pulled by hers. You aren’t certain what it is you should be doing at this point. Zo’s radiance is overpowering: anything you try to do to get noticed in the wake of her aura would be little more than a whisper in the wind; you’d have all the impact of a leaf fluttering the ground. But, above all else, you and Zo are connected now: you never considered attempting to apply your training with the flowers as the flowers, but it’s not like you have any other option. Zo is unresponsive to anything else you do. It’s an exhausting technique for you to perform, and you feel the strength leaving your limbs and your chest the longer it keeps up, but you try and put out more of yourself into the void anyway. You can’t hope to match Zo, but you can at least try and make yourself visible to her. Curiously, every ‘pulse’ of energy that you send to her is found by her overpowering, emanating aura, and is then consumed and dissipated; she neither acknowledges it, nor grows or feeds upon it. It’s as if you had discarded a piece of yourself into the empty nothingness of the void between you two. It’s dangerous to keep going down this path, but it’s not like you can try anything else. You do it again, putting more of yourself into the void, trying your hardest to be seen against the totality of Zo’s presence; you’re attempting to be as obvious as a single flake of snow against the shining sun, and you can feel the very essence of yourself evaporating from your body as you do it, but if it has even the slightest chance of getting Zo out of whatever trance she’s gotten herself into, no cost is too great. As you reach your limits with this attempt, you feel a response: a tug on the line that connects your aura to Zo’s. You aren’t sure what to make of it; it isn’t like the flowers ever pulled on you back. The ‘hook’ between you two fidgets and yanks again – it’s like a fish on the end of a fishing line, gently nibbling before it bites, except... instead of you trying to pull the fish out of the water, the fish is trying to use your line to pull itself out of the water. Suddenly, the immensity of Zo’s aura – the absoluteness that represented her and how it blotted out even the darkness of the void around you – inverts into itself, and your eyes are unconsciously snapped open. The orbits of rocks surrounding you two rain onto the dirt and the grass around you, and, falling to the earth with a loud ‘thump,’ is Zo; she hits the ground hard on her ass, her silver mask flinging away from her face as she tumbles, and she falls into you, landing face-first into your [pc.chest]. She clings to you hard, her fingers digging into your [pc.upperGarment], and when she opens her eyes again, the blank, dull, muted silver is replaced with the same, familiar emerald-green irises from before.
rows.translation: 你坐在佐面前，采取与她相同的坐姿，然后闭上眼睛。你努力集中自己的精神力量，回想起在花园里与她一起练习时的经验，尝试将自己的气场“释放”出来，这样她就能尽可能清楚地看到你。 几乎立刻，你就“感知”到了她自己的气场。它…… 庞大的她所释放出的力量与能量，瞬间就远远超过了你自身所拥有的。如果说在那次训练中你就像是花朵们赖以生存的太阳，那么对于佐来说，你便是那朵花朵。当你的能量在虚空中相遇时，它们会彼此交织、相互连接，就如同你当初对那些花朵所做的那样——只不过这一次，你能够真切地感受到这一过程。 你的 被牵着走 她的此刻，你其实并不确定自己应该做些什么。佐的光芒太过耀眼了——在她那强大的气场之下，你无论尝试做什么来吸引别人的注意，都只不过是微风中的轻声细语，根本没有任何影响力，就像一片树叶轻轻拂过地面而已。但最重要的是，你现在与佐已经建立了某种联系：你根本没考虑过要运用自己所学的知识来处理这些花朵。 如同 那些花朵……不过你也没有其他选择。无论你做什么，Zo都毫无反应。 对你来说，这种做法实在令人精疲力竭。随着时间的推移，你会感到自己的四肢和胸部逐渐失去了力量，但即便如此，你还是努力向那个虚无中投入自己的一切。你实在没有其他办法了…… 匹配 佐，但你至少可以试着让她注意到你的存在。 奇怪的是，你向她发出的每一丝能量，都会被她那强大的气场所察觉，然后被吸收并消散掉；她既不会对此作出任何反应，也不会因此而成长或获得力量。 就好像你将自己的一部分抛入了你们两人之间的那片虚无之中。 继续沿着这条路走下去很危险，但你也没有其他选择。你又一次这样做，将自己更多的部分投入那片虚无之中，竭尽全力让自己在Zo的存在感面前显得显眼一些；你试图让自己像一片雪花在灿烂的阳光下那样容易被看到。在这个过程中，你能感觉到自己的本质正在逐渐从身体里消散，但只要这样做能有一丝机会让Zo从她现在的状态中清醒过来，任何代价都是值得的。 当你在这次尝试中达到自己的极限时，你感受到了一种反应：那根连接你的气场与佐的线被轻轻拉了一下。你不确定该如何理解这种感觉；因为那些花朵之前从未这样拉过你。你们之间的这种“联系”再次微微晃动、拉扯着——就像鱼线末端的鱼在轻轻试探，然后才决定是否咬钩一样。而不是你试图把鱼从水里拉出来，而是鱼在试图利用你的鱼线把自己拉出来。 它自己 突然间，佐那强大而绝对的气场——那种代表着她自身的力量，甚至能够掩盖周围虚无中的黑暗——发生了逆转，你的双眼不由自主地睁开了。 你们周围那些岩石的轨道将它们抛向你们周围的泥土和草地上，其中一块岩石“砰”的一声坠落到地上，那就是佐；她重重地摔在地上，银色的面具从她脸上飞了出去，她整个人摔在了你身上，脸先着地，落在了你的怀里…… [pc.chest]她紧紧地抱住你，手指深深地嵌入你的身体里。 [pc.upperGarment]当她再次睁开眼睛时，那片空洞、暗淡、毫无生气的银色已经消失了，取而代之的，依然是那熟悉的翠绿色虹膜。

rows.original: When her eyes meet yours, she clings to you tighter, and she buries her face into your chest again, clearly in the need of some comfort; whatever she had just gone through, it was a harrowing experience that she wasn’t ready for, and she needs you, above all else, to give her something to anchor herself to. You wrap your arms around her, hugging her at the shoulders, and you wring your fingers through her fur, clutching her closer to you; she shivers and shakily exhales, thankful to whoever she believes in that you’re there with her. You reflect on what it was that you two had just gone through. She had entered some kind of state of being where the outside world had no bearing on herself; protected, or perhaps caged, from everything. She didn’t respond when you made loud noises, and you can’t tell if it’s because she had mastered the ability to tune out the universe, or because she literally wasn’t present to respond. You’ve been in the presence of her personal aura multiple times, now, but it never felt as intense as it did just now. What had she done differently to attain these different states of being? Where she was simultaneously missing, but omnipresent? Nowhere, but everywhere? It’s a while before Zo stops shaking in your embrace, and when she does, you gather up the courage to ask her what just happened. It’s a question you feel a little silly and insensitive for asking, given she’s mute, but knowing her, she’d be able to at least give you a hint. Zo takes her time before responding to the question. Almost laboriously, she tears herself from you and sits up, resting on her knees to face you directly. She frowns, her lips curling down but her eyebrows arching up; the kind of expression that a parent makes when they need to make the difficult decision about teaching a child a life lesson. After another moment, she puts her hands on your face, her fingers taking very specific positions on your cheeks, forehead, around your eyes, and down your neck. You remember this from before, back when you two had first met and she showed you the realities of the universe through her own eyes. Whatever she’s about to do must be similar. You aren’t certain if you want to see whatever it was that she saw, but it’s too late to back out now. Once all of her digits are in place and resting against your skull, she closes her eyes and focuses, and when she reopens them, they’re that same, familiar, shimmering silver – the kind where you can still see her pupils. Your own vision doesn’t change, unlike last time. In fact, you don’t feel much of anything. Actually... that’s not true. It’s not that you don’t feel anything. It’s that you feel nothing. You don’t feel your tongue in your mouth; you don’t feel your eyes drying up the longer you keep them open; you don’t feel the wind blowing and rustling from between you two, even though you can clearly see it against her hair; after a few moments of this, you realize that you don’t feel the need to breathe (even though you do, just in case). Although you’re clearly sitting in a grassy field with Zo, you don’t feel as though you’re there – you don’t feel as though you exist. Like your body has died, and you’re just waiting for your mind to follow along after it. The experience only lasts a few moments before Zo pulls her hands away; as soon as the first digit slides out of place, the sensation leaves – or, more appropriately, every other sensation returns – and your body and your mind are brought back into alignment with each other. You don’t bother asking her if that was what she was experiencing; she wouldn’t have put you through a sensation like that for no reason. You imagine that she was holding back for your sake: her experience was total, and included her mind as well. You were conscious and aware the whole time, which... you aren’t certain if those words would describe Zo’s state of being nearly as well. Before you say or do anything else, Zo reaches forward with her left hand, placing it onto your chest, just above your heart, and her right hand goes to her breast, resting with her palm flatly above her own. The gesture alone would be enough to get the message across, especially with the warm smile that turns her eyes into crescents, but you also feel something else: a surge of her energy, looking to reach out to you like you had to her. A way to remind you that you and her share something special, something that connects you two in a tangible-yet-incorporeal way, going beyond what friends or lovers are capable of, and that, if you ever needed her like she needed you, she’d be there for you. You two enjoy each other’s company for a while longer. It’s not often that you two do that, where you just sit there and bask in the presence of one-another: you’re usually training or having sex when you’re with her. There’s something to be said about doing nothing with someone. It’s almost a shame that you need to leave. If only you and Zo could stay together a bit longer....
rows.translation: 当她的目光与你的相遇时，她会更加紧紧地依偎在你身边，再次将脸埋进你的胸膛，显然她需要一些安慰；无论她刚刚经历了什么，那一定是一次令她痛苦不堪的经历，而她现在迫切需要你，让你给她一些力量，让她能够重新找到依靠。 你将手部臂环绕在她身上，搂住她的肩膀，手部指穿过她的毛发，将她紧紧抱在怀里；她微微颤抖着，颤抖着呼出气息，心中充满感激——无论她信仰什么，她都庆幸有你陪伴在她身边。 你仔细回想你们刚刚经历的一切。她仿佛进入了一种某种状态，在这种状态下，外部世界对她来说已经毫无影响；她仿佛被保护了起来，或者更确切地说，被关在了一个与外界隔绝的笼子里。当你发出很大的声响时，她并没有做出任何反应，你也不清楚这是因为她已经掌握了屏蔽外界一切干扰的能力，还是因为她真的没有听到那些声音。 当前 你需要做出回应。你已经多次感受到她的个人气场了，现在，你…… 永远不会 那种强烈的感觉，和刚才一样。她究竟做了什么不同的事情，才会产生这种截然不同的状态呢？为什么她有时似乎不在那里，却又仿佛无处不在？既不在任何地方，却又存在于每一个角落？ 过了好一会儿，佐才在你的怀里停止了颤抖。当她终于平静下来时，你鼓起勇气问她刚才发生了什么。考虑到她是哑巴，你觉得自己提出这个问题有点傻，也显得有些不体贴，但你知道，她至少会给你一些提示的。 佐花花了一些时间才回答这个问题。她似乎费了很大的劲才从你身边抽身出来，坐直身体，双膝着地，以便能够直接面对你。她皱起了眉头，嘴唇微微下垂，但眉毛却高高扬起——这种表情，就像是一位父母在必须做出那个艰难的决定、教导孩子人生道理时所表现出来的那样。 又过了一会儿，她将双手部放在你的脸上，她的手部指在你的脸颊、额头、眼周以及脖颈处摆出了特定的位置。你记得以前有过这样的情景——当初你们初次见面时，她就是通过自己的双眼向你展示了这个世界的真实面貌。现在她要做的，应该也是类似的事情吧。你不确定自己是否想看到她所看到的那些东西，但现在已经来不及退缩了。 当她的所有手部指都放置到位，紧贴着你的头骨时，她闭上了眼睛，集中注意力。当她再次睁开眼睛时，那些手部指依然是那熟悉的、闪烁着银光的样子——那种你仍然能够看到她瞳孔的颜色。与上次不同，你的视线并没有发生任何变化。事实上，你几乎感觉不到任何东西。 其实……并不是这样的。并不是说你没有那种感觉。 任何东西。 问题就在于你的这种感受。 没什么。 你感觉不到自己的舌头在嘴里；你也不会觉得眼睛在睁得越久就会越干；尽管你能清楚地看到风从你们两人之间吹过，拂动她的头发，但你却感觉不到风的存在；过了几分钟之后，你突然意识到自己甚至觉得没有必要呼吸（虽然其实还是需要呼吸的，只是出于习惯罢了）。虽然你明明是和Zo一起坐在一片长满草的田野里，但你却完全没有那种身处其中的真实感觉——你完全感觉不到…… 存在就好像你的身体已经死亡，而你只是在等待大脑也随之停止运作。 这种感觉只持续了短短的几秒钟，随后佐就把手部抽了回去；只要有一个手部指的位置发生了改变，那种感觉就会立刻消失——或者更准确地说，其他所有的感觉都会随之消失。 返回结果 – 这时，你的身体与心灵再次达到了和谐统一的状态。 你没有去问她是否确实经历了这样的感受；她肯定不会无缘无故地让你体验那种感觉。你认为，她是出于对你的考虑而忍住了自己的感受：她的体验其实…… 总共， 你的意识也完全清醒着，你始终保持着清醒与觉察……不过，你不确定这些词语是否也能同样准确地描述佐的状态。 在你再说出或做出任何举动之前，佐用左手部伸过来，将她的手部放在你的胸膛上，正好位于你的心脏上方；而她的右手部则放在自己的胸前，手部掌平放在那里。 仅仅这个手部势就足以传达出这个意思，尤其是当她露出那种让眼睛都变成月牙形的温暖微笑时，但你还会感受到另一种东西：她身上散发出的那种能量，仿佛她在试图与你建立联系，就像你也需要与她建立联系一样。 这是一种方式，用来提醒你：你和她之间存在着某种特别的东西，某种以无形却又真实的方式将你们联系在一起的东西，这种联系超越了普通朋友或恋人之间所能拥有的关系；同时，这也意味着：如果你有任何需要她的时刻，她也会在你身边，一如她需要你那样。 你们俩再一起享受这段时光吧。这样的时刻其实并不常见——你们通常要么在训练，要么在做爱。能够和某人一起什么都不做，这种感觉也挺不错的。 你真的要离开，真是太遗憾了。要是你和Zo能再多待在一起一段时间该多好……
rows.raw: " When her eyes meet yours, she clings to you tighter, and she buries her face into your chest again, clearly in the need of some comfort; whatever she had just gone through, it was a harrowing experience that she wasn’t ready for, and she needs you, above all else, to give her something to anchor herself to. You wrap your arms around her, hugging her at the shoulders, and you wring your fingers through her fur, clutching her closer to you; she shivers and shakily exhales, thankful to whoever she believes in that you’re there with her. You reflect on what it was that you two had just gone through. She had entered some kind of state of being where the outside world had no bearing on herself; protected, or perhaps caged, from everything. She didn’t respond when you made loud noises, and you can’t tell if it’s because she had mastered the ability to tune out the universe, or because she literally wasn’t present to respond. You’ve been in the presence of her personal aura multiple times, now, but it never felt as intense as it did just now. What had she done differently to attain these different states of being? Where she was simultaneously missing, but omnipresent? Nowhere, but everywhere? It’s a while before Zo stops shaking in your embrace, and when she does, you gather up the courage to ask her what just happened. It’s a question you feel a little silly and insensitive for asking, given she’s mute, but knowing her, she’d be able to at least give you a hint. Zo takes her time before responding to the question. Almost laboriously, she tears herself from you and sits up, resting on her knees to face you directly. She frowns, her lips curling down but her eyebrows arching up; the kind of expression that a parent makes when they need to make the difficult decision about teaching a child a life lesson. After another moment, she puts her hands on your face, her fingers taking very specific positions on your cheeks, forehead, around your eyes, and down your neck. You remember this from before, back when you two had first met and she showed you the realities of the universe through her own eyes. Whatever she’s about to do must be similar. You aren’t certain if you want to see whatever it was that she saw, but it’s too late to back out now. Once all of her digits are in place and resting against your skull, she closes her eyes and focuses, and when she reopens them, they’re that same, familiar, shimmering silver – the kind where you can still see her pupils. Your own vision doesn’t change, unlike last time. In fact, you don’t feel much of anything. Actually... that’s not true. It’s not that you don’t feel anything. It’s that you feel nothing. You don’t feel your tongue in your mouth; you don’t feel your eyes drying up the longer you keep them open; you don’t feel the wind blowing and rustling from between you two, even though you can clearly see it against her hair; after a few moments of this, you realize that you don’t feel the need to breathe (even though you do, just in case). Although you’re clearly sitting in a grassy field with Zo, you don’t feel as though you’re there – you don’t feel as though you exist. Like your body has died, and you’re just waiting for your mind to follow along after it. The experience only lasts a few moments before Zo pulls her hands away; as soon as the first digit slides out of place, the sensation leaves – or, more appropriately, every other sensation returns – and your body and your mind are brought back into alignment with each other. You don’t bother asking her if that was what she was experiencing; she wouldn’t have put you through a sensation like that for no reason. You imagine that she was holding back for your sake: her experience was total, and included her mind as well. You were conscious and aware the whole time, which... you aren’t certain if those words would describe Zo’s state of being nearly as well. Before you say or do anything else, Zo reaches forward with her left hand, placing it onto your chest, just above your heart, and her right hand goes to her breast, resting with her palm flatly above her own. The gesture alone would be enough to get the message across, especially with the warm smile that turns her eyes into crescents, but you also feel something else: a surge of her energy, looking to reach out to you like you had to her. A way to remind you that you and her share something special, something that connects you two in a tangible-yet-incorporeal way, going beyond what friends or lovers are capable of, and that, if you ever needed her like she needed you, she’d be there for you. You two enjoy each other’s company for a while longer. It’s not often that you two do that, where you just sit there and bask in the presence of one-another: you’re usually training or having sex when you’re with her. There’s something to be said about doing nothing with someone. It’s almost a shame that you need to leave. If only you and Zo could stay together a bit longer.... "

rows.original: When you enter Zo’s grove, the woman herself is easy to spot: she’s going through her usual training routines in the grassy field, making various poses that test her body’s rigidity and balance, swapping between them regularly. As soon as she spots you at the entrance to her grove, she stops immediately, excited to see you again. Before you have the chance to say hello, she extends one finger upward at you as she hurries into her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|home|derelict shack]. She comes back out just a few seconds later, carrying something wrapped in a towel in both of her hands. Her smile is as bright as the sun and wide enough to touch her triangular ears when she presents it to you. Taking the guess that she isn’t offering you the towel itself, you unfold it in her hands to see what’s inside. There, lying across both her hands, is a mask made of silver. You glance up at her, seeing that she’s wearing her own – this is a second mask, and, judging by the expression on her face and how she lifts her hands higher to you when you unravel it, it’s a gift for you. You turn it over in your hands, inspecting the craftsmanship, before you slide it onto your face[pc.hasHelmet|, removing your [pc.helmet] to make room]. It’s a perfect fit; you don’t know where Zo got your measurements, or if she just guessed, and she nailed it exactly. You ask her if she forged the mask herself; she shakes her head no, and points to the northwest of the grove, towards Hawkethorne. Sometime between now and when you last visited her, she must have had the opportunity to go into town and commission the local blacksmith. But a mask this fine must have taken longer than a day to make; she must have had this gift in mind for a while. You ask her how she managed to pay for it. In response, she taps at her own silver mask, but provides no further hints. She must have a stockpile of silver hidden somewhere – even a few nuggets of the stuff would have been enough to compensate any blacksmith for their work. The mask must have been made from her stash, too. It’s a beautiful mask, and it’s been meticulously crafted to your specifications to fit onto your face precisely, just like her own. When you wear it, it covers the top of your nose (leaving your nostrils clear); your cheeks; your forehead; and it covers everything across both of your temples, leaving holes for your eyes. Your vision isn’t impeded when you wear it, and although it was cool to the touch when you handled it, it warms to your body temperature as soon as you put it on. And, when you put it on, you suddenly feel a newfound focus; a surge of... potential, that you didn’t have before. When you remove the mask, all that focus, all that energy, dissipates almost immediately. It’s like night and day. Zo rocks on her heels, waiting for your appraisal of her present. You don’t have many words to say, other than ‘thank you;’ instead of words, you step into her, wrapping your arms around her and hugging her to your chest. She’s all too happy to return the gesture, resting her chin on your shoulder as her own arms squeeze you against her. It’s a wonderful gift.
rows.translation: 当你走进佐的树林时，那个女人很容易就被发现：她正在草地上进行日常的训练，做出各种动作来测试自己身体的柔韧性和平衡能力，这些动作会不断地变换。一旦她在树林入口处看到你，就会立刻停下来，因为见到你她非常兴奋。在你还有机会打招呼之前，她就会伸出一根手部指朝你示意，然后快步走进树林里去。 [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|家|废弃的小屋]几秒钟后，她又走了出来，双手部捧着用毛巾包着的东西。当她把那个东西递给你时，她的笑容如同阳光般灿烂，笑容之大几乎能碰到她那三角形的耳朵。 你猜她并不是要把毛巾本身送给你的，于是你在她面前将毛巾展开，想看看里面有什么。 果然，她的双手部上放着一块银制的面具。你抬头看她，发现她自己也戴着另一块面具——这块是第二块面具，而从她脸上的表情，以及当你将毛巾展开时她把双手部举得更高这一举动来看，这块面具显然是送给你的礼物。 你将它拿在手部中仔细端详，欣赏其精湛的工艺，然后将其戴在脸上。[pc.hasHelmet|，移除你的…… [pc.helmet] 腾出空间]这简直太完美了——你根本不知道Zo是怎么得到你的尺寸数据的，也不知道她是不是只是随便猜的，但她竟然做得一点都不差。你问她这个面具是不是她自己制作的，她摇摇头说不是，然后指出了树林的西北方向，朝着鹰棘镇的方向。从你上次见到她到现在这段时间里，她肯定有机会去镇上，委托当地的铁匠制作这个面具。不过，这样一个精美的面具肯定需要花费一整天的时间才能制作完成；看来她早就打算送你这个礼物了。 你问她是怎么凑到钱来支付这笔费用的。她只是轻轻敲了敲自己戴的银色面具，没有再透露任何信息。她肯定在某个地方藏了一大批银子——哪怕只有几块银子，也足以支付任何铁匠的工作费用了。那面面具肯定也是用她藏的银子制成的。 这是一副精美的面具，它是根据你的要求精心制作的，能够完美地贴合你的脸型，就像她自己戴的那副一样。当你戴上它时，它的顶部会覆盖你的鼻子（同时让你的鼻孔保持通畅），脸颊、额头都会被完全遮住，而两侧太阳穴处则留有眼睛的位置。戴上它后，你的视线不会受到任何影响。虽然初次触摸时它感觉有些凉爽，但一旦戴在脸上，就会迅速升温，变得与你的体温相同。 而当你戴上它的时候，会突然感受到一种全新的专注力；一种……的力量涌上心头。 潜力， 那种你之前从未拥有过的感觉。当你摘下面具时，所有那些专注、那些能量，几乎会立刻消散殆尽，简直就像天壤之别。 佐站在那里，踮着脚尖，等待着你对她现在的表现的评价。你实在找不到太多话可说，只能说出“谢谢”两个字；但 instead of 用言语表达，你走上前去，搂住她，将她紧紧抱在怀里。她也非常高兴地回应了这个拥抱，把下巴靠在你的肩膀上，用自己的手部臂也将你紧紧搂住。这真是一份美妙的礼物。

rows.original: Zo is [dayNight |in her grove |in her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|home|shack] ], just as you had expected her to be during this time of day, but, [dayNight |where you’d normally see her practicing some kind of martial art or doing some kind of training |where you’d normally see her doing some chore, like cleaning or mending her clothing or cooking some food for her dinner ], she’s abnormally listless and floaty – it’s like her mind is absent, which is unusual for someone that preaches stability and fortitude like she does. Her teeth keep nibbling into her bottom lip, and her eyes are half-lidded and frantic, focusing on nothing. When you ask her if she has something on her mind, she reacts strangely: almost like you had startled her, but, at the same time, like she had expected, or at least hoped, that you would be there. Her eyes shift between your two again and again beneath her mask, and her tongue snakes out to lick her lips more than once. She, as usual, doesn’t answer, and you think better than to ask her a different question. It takes her another moment to respond as she considers her options; from the look on her face, she wants something – and the more lecherous part of your mind is having an easy time reading her body language and jumping to conclusions on what, exactly, she wants – but she’s having a difficult time ‘phrasing’ it, as it were. She sighs throatily, her breath coming out in rough ‘gargles,’ as she gets frustrated with her indecisiveness and her inability to speak her mind. So, instead, she faces you directly, her eyes narrowed underneath her silver mask, and she points to herself before she puts her left hand on top of her left breast, right above her heart; then, she points to you with her other, putting her hand on top of your chest, right above your own. She values you as more than a student and a friend, and this is the best way she can get that across. But she continues: she points to you; then, she [pc.mascFem |makes a circle with her left index finger and her thumb, and she drives her right index finger into the circle, thrusting it several times |makes two V’s with her left and right index and middle fingers, and then drives them together, plugging the openings of the Vs together and bumping them into each other several times ]. She’s looking to value you as a whole lot more than a friend, it seems. It’s a highly vulgar gesture, and it catches you off-guard that someone as monistic as Zo would even think to communicate this way, much less convey her wants to you in the way she has. You don’t bother asking her for confirmation; what she wants from you is crystal clear. [pc.isMale |[pc.hasCock | |There’s just one problem, though: you explain to Zo that you... aren’t equipped to give her what it is she wants. You know you look like a man, but you’re packing something decidedly feminine instead. She tilts her head to one side at first, then nods, making two V’s with her left and right index and middle fingers before driving them together, plugging the openings of the Vs together and bumping them into each other several times. It seems she doesn’t care how she gets it, as long as she does. ] |[pc.hasCock |There’s just one caveat, though: you explain to Zo that you’re... differently equipped than how she might be expecting. You know you look like a woman, but you’re packing something a bit more masculine to work with.[pc.cockRange 0 13 | | Frankly, you’re surprised she hadn’t noticed; your ‘immensity’ tends to give you a bulge that’s hard to disguise. ] She tilts her head to one side at first, then nods, making a circle with her left index finger and her thumb before she drives her right index finger into the circle, thrusting it several times. It seems it doesn’t matter how she gets it, as long as she does. ] ]You ask her what brought about this kind of... forwardness. Given how her training normally emphasizes things like stability and clarity, you’d think her needing to get off wouldn’t even be a concern, much less something she needs so badly that she’d proposition you on the spot. In response, she points to herself; then, she puts her hands together by their palms, her fingers standing straight up; then, she points to her own crotch; and finally, she puts her hands together by their palms again, but with her fingers crooked to one side. She smiles and exhales sharply through her nose in her awkward way of laughing; she’s so horny that her need to get laid is knocking off her inner-balance. Frankly, you can’t exactly blame her; there have been times in your life where you’ve been so overwhelmingly horny that you couldn’t think of anything else either. And having a partner is always better at clearing that up than doing it on your own. Still, it isn’t like she’s grabbing you by the wrist and dragging you into her [flags.ZO_UPGRADE 3|house|shack] so she can fuck you dry[pc.dcb |, as much as you’d be okay with that |.
