[zo.vaiExists |You’re not about to let your baby and your baby mommy live in such squalor like this. |You get that she’s a monk and doesn’t need extra to survive, but she’s taking it too far and you feel gross and poor by proximity. ] |To be deft: she doesn’t live in a place that’s safe or comfortable [zo.vaiExists |for a baby. As much as you trust her to be a good mom, there’s only so far she can go with a house like... that. |for anyone at all. She’s an adult and she can take care of herself, and she’s a monk that prefers to live off what she has over getting more, but... come on. Look at this place. ] ] Zo’s mouth twists diagonally as she turns towards the shack in her grove. It’s maybe fifteen paces wide and ten paces deep; the wooden walls have holes in them, having been worn down from time and the elements, not to mention all the bugs and termites having eaten the walls hallow; the roof is poorly thatched and falling apart; the floor is half-rotten and beaten up from years of having things scraped overtop it; and the whole thing is leaning to one side slightly. And it had to withstand the might of your combined exertions during that one form of training, back when you both didn’t have the same sort of control over yourselves as you do now. She knows it’s a [pc.isDK |shitty |derelict ] place to live in, and she knows you’re right. Her living arrangements work for her – she lives a very monastic lifestyle and needs very little to not only survive, but live a happy life in her little grove. And from the look in her eyes, she has some sentimental value to her shack: there’s clearly a reason she likes it the way it is, even though she could live in Hawkethorne, less than an hour’s walk to the north. Or, at the very least, she could have had the shack fixed by now. [zo.vaiExists |But it’s not a place for a child. She might have some contingency for if the whole thing comes down on her while she’s sleeping or whatever, but that’s not a risk she can take as a parent. |But that doesn’t change the fact that it’s a death trap. She sleeps in there – if a storm hits when she’s trying to sleep, the whole thing could come down on her. And she might have a contingency for that, but she’s playing with fire, and she knows it. ] You aren’t a carpenter, and from the look of her house, neither is she. [wayfort.renovated |But you know a guy that knows some guys in Hawkethorne that can get it fixed up for a small fee |While you don’t know of any carpenters or a carpentry business in Hawkethorne, you at least know where to start looking ]. She doesn’t need to worry about the money; all she needs to do is give you her permission. She tilts her head and rests her chin on her hand as she regards you. The answer is already a given, but it comes down to what it is that she [zo.vaiExists |and [zo.isPregnant |the baby |Vai ] ]will need for it to be a safe, comfortable environment. Given her lifestyle, she might be uncomfortable with anything more than the bare [silly |necessities |minimums ], and she might balk at any sort of opulence – for example, given her current arrangement, a door that locks. rows.translation: 你告诉佐，你想和她谈谈她目前的……居住安排。 [pc.isDK |它们太糟糕了。 [zo.vaiExists |你总不能让你的宝宝和宝宝的妈妈生活在这样的肮脏环境中吧。 |你明白她其实是个僧人，生存并不需要这些额外的东西，但她做得太过分了，靠近她你会觉得既恶心又难受。 ] |要身手敏捷，就必须生活在一个既安全又舒适的环境中。 [zo.vaiExists |对于一个婴儿来说，尽管你非常信任她能成为一个好妈妈，但对于这样的房子来说，她的能力也是有限的…… 那个。 |对于任何人来说，她都是一个成年人了，她完全有能力照顾自己。而且她是一个选择过简生活、宁愿满足于现有的一切也不愿去追求更多的人……但是，拜托，看看这个地方吧。 ] ] 佐转过身，朝着她树林里的那间小屋走去。那小屋大概有十五步宽、十步深，木墙上布满了洞孔——这些洞都是随着时间的流逝以及自然环境的侵蚀而形成的，更不用说那些虫子和白蚁对木墙的破坏了；屋顶的茅草敷得很不牢固，已经开始脱落；地板也有一半已经腐烂了，由于多年来人们不断在上面摩擦，地板表面变得凹凸不平；而整个小屋还微微向一侧倾斜着。 而且，在那种训练方式中，它必须能够承受你们两人共同施加的力量——那时候，你们还无法像现在这样很好地控制自己的行为。 她知道这是…… [pc.isDK |糟糕透了 |被遗弃的 ] 她有地方住，而且她也知道你是对的。她的居住方式对她来说很合适——她过着非常简朴的生活，只需要很少的东西就能生存下去，甚至能在她那个小角落里过上幸福的生活。从她的眼神中可以看出，她对那间小屋有着特殊的感情：显然，她之所以喜欢它现在的样子，是有着原因的，尽管她完全可以搬到离那里不到一小时路程的鹰棘镇去住。或者，至少她现在也可以把那间小屋修缮一下。 [zo.vaiExists |但这确实不是一个适合孩子待的地方。或许她能想出一些应对办法，比如在孩子睡觉时发生意外之类的情况，但作为父母，她无法承担这样的风险。 |但事实依然是，那地方简直就是个死亡陷阱。她就在那里睡觉——如果她在睡觉的时候遇到暴风雨，整个结构都可能会倒塌下来压在她身上。她或许已经考虑到了这种可能性，但她仍在冒险，而且她自己也清楚这一点。 ] 你又不是木匠，而从她房子的状况来看，她显然也不是。 [wayfort.renovated |但是你认识一个人吧，这个人在鹰棘镇认识一些人，只要支付一小笔费用，他们就能把这个问题解决掉。 |虽然你不知道鹰棘镇有什么木匠或木工店，但至少你知道该从哪里开始寻找。 ]她不需要担心钱的问题；她所要做的就是给你她的许可而已。 她歪着头，用手托着下巴，注视着你。答案其实早已显而易见，但关键在于她究竟会做出什么样的选择…… [zo.vaiExists |以及 [zo.isPregnant |宝宝 |走吧。 ] ]会 需要 为了营造一个安全、舒适的环境，考虑到她的生活方式，任何超出最基本要求的设施都可能会让她感到不适。 [silly |生活必需品 |最低要求 ]而且，她可能会对任何形式的奢华感到反感——比如说，以她目前的处境来看，一扇能上锁的门对她来说可能就是一种奢华。 [pc.isDK |就我个人而言，你并不真正理解这一点。你尝试过按照她的方式去生活，以便从中吸取教训，虽然你证明了自己有能力这样做，但当有住房子的选择时，你却并不会选择去住帐篷。 |说实话，这种生活方式简直让人羡慕：只使用自己真正需要的东西，依靠大自然来维持生活。不过，虽然你已经证明了自己至少能够理解她的生活方式——毕竟你已经完成了她的训练任务——但你自己并不认为这种生活方式是自己愿意永远过下去的。 ] 你向她保证，她不会得到一座豪华的大房子。她得到的将会是那间老房子——同样的布局，同样的基本设施，都是她已经习惯了的：有遮风挡雨的屋顶、两扇玻璃窗，还有一个火坑。你的打算就是修缮她的屋顶和墙壁，重新安装窗户，这样就能给她一间看起来像样的小屋了。 [zo.vaiExists |以及 [zo.isPregnant |宝宝 |走吧。 ] ]一个可以居住的地方。最豪华的配置也不过是一扇能正常关闭和锁上的门罢了。 她转向你，目光紧锁，嘴唇微微抿着，似乎在认真思考……过了一会儿，她笑了，脸颊的肌肉让她脸上的“面具”暂时掀开了。她的左手伸过来，握住了你的手，手指紧紧地缠绕在一起。 你可以把这理解为“同意”，也就是说，她允许你重新设计她的房子了。 [wayfort.renovated |你知道，只需要和那位调酒师谈谈就行了。 |现在，你只需要找一些木匠就可以了。显然，这是必要的。 有人 在鹰棘镇，没人比加思更懂如何建造房屋了。或许你可以去问问他？酒馆老板通常都是获取当地新闻和信息的首选对象…… ]
rows.raw: " You tell Zo that you wanted to speak with her about her current... living arrangements. [pc.isDK |They suck. [zo.vaiExists |You’re not about to let your baby and your baby mommy live in such squalor like this. |You get that she’s a monk and doesn’t need extra to survive, but she’s taking it too far and you feel gross and poor by proximity. ] |To be deft: she doesn’t live in a place that’s safe or comfortable [zo.vaiExists |for a baby. As much as you trust her to be a good mom, there’s only so far she can go with a house like... that. |for anyone at all. She’s an adult and she can take care of herself, and she’s a monk that prefers to live off what she has over getting more, but... come on. Look at this place. ] ] Zo’s mouth twists diagonally as she turns towards the shack in her grove. It’s maybe fifteen paces wide and ten paces deep; the wooden walls have holes in them, having been worn down from time and the elements, not to mention all the bugs and termites having eaten the walls hallow; the roof is poorly thatched and falling apart; the floor is half-rotten and beaten up from years of having things scraped overtop it; and the whole thing is leaning to one side slightly. And it had to withstand the might of your combined exertions during that one form of training, back when you both didn’t have the same sort of control over yourselves as you do now. She knows it’s a [pc.isDK |shitty |derelict ] place to live in, and she knows you’re right. Her living arrangements work for her – she lives a very monastic lifestyle and needs very little to not only survive, but live a happy life in her little grove. And from the look in her eyes, she has some sentimental value to her shack: there’s clearly a reason she likes it the way it is, even though she could live in Hawkethorne, less than an hour’s walk to the north. Or, at the very least, she could have had the shack fixed by now. [zo.vaiExists |But it’s not a place for a child. She might have some contingency for if the whole thing comes down on her while she’s sleeping or whatever, but that’s not a risk she can take as a parent. |But that doesn’t change the fact that it’s a death trap. She sleeps in there – if a storm hits when she’s trying to sleep, the whole thing could come down on her. And she might have a contingency for that, but she’s playing with fire, and she knows it. ] You aren’t a carpenter, and from the look of her house, neither is she. [wayfort.renovated |But you know a guy that knows some guys in Hawkethorne that can get it fixed up for a small fee |While you don’t know of any carpenters or a carpentry business in Hawkethorne, you at least know where to start looking ]. She doesn’t need to worry about the money; all she needs to do is give you her permission. She tilts her head and rests her chin on her hand as she regards you. The answer is already a given, but it comes down to what it is that she [zo.vaiExists |and [zo.isPregnant |the baby |Vai ] ]will need for it to be a safe, comfortable environment. Given her lifestyle, she might be uncomfortable with anything more than the bare [silly |necessities |minimums ], and she might balk at any sort of opulence – for example, given her current arrangement, a door that locks. [pc.isDK |Personally, you don’t get it. You’ve tried living things her way in order to learn her lessons, and while you’ve proven that you’re capable of it, you’re not about to choose to live in a tent when the option to live in a house is right there. |It’s a borderline enviable way of living, honestly: using only what you need, living how you can off the land. But, although you’ve proven that you’re capable of at least understanding her lifestyle, given that you’ve completed her training, it’s not a life that you think you’d want forever. ] You assure her that she’s not going to get a big, fancy house. What she’ll be getting is the same shack, with the same layout, and the same minimums that she’s used to: a roof over her head; two glass windows; and a fire pit. What you’re looking to do is fix up her roof and walls and redo the windows, so that it’s a presentable little hut for her [zo.vaiExists |and [zo.isPregnant |the baby |Vai ] ]to live in. The fanciest it’ll get is a door that closes and locks properly. She turns to you, her eyes narrowed in thought and her lips pursed as she considers it... and then, after a moment, she smiles, her cheeks lifting the mask on her face. Her left hand reaches out and seeks yours, her fingers wrapping and intertwining around your own and squeezing. You’ll take that as a ‘yes,’ and you have her permission to redo her house. [wayfort.renovated |And you know just the bartender to speak to. |Now, you just need to find some carpenters. Clearly someone in Hawkethorne knows how to build a house. Maybe you could ask Garth? The tavernkeeper is usually the first person to go to for local news and information.... ]"

rows.original: [wayfort.renovated |You tell Garth that you’re starting up another carpenter job and you need him to get in contact with his people again. "Sure," he answers quickly and simply, not pausing his ardent cleaning of his beer mugs. "The last job went without a hitch and you paid them well enough. They had no complaints. I’m assuming it’s for the same place as last time? An expansion or something?" This one’s actually a repair job, and it’s for something considerably smaller: a single-room, one-story shack, maybe as large as the bar you’re sitting in right now, out in a grove just a few minute’s ride into Harvest Valley. It needs a new roof; some redone windows; a redone floor; and its old door has fallen off its hinges. It’d be very simple, especially compared to the previous job you wanted. "Sounds like the place is for the worms already," he responds, lifting an eyebrow. "What is this, a toolshed or something? Why not just build a new one?" It’s more of a... cottage, you suppose. And it’s not just for you: it’s for someone you know[zo.vaiExists |. Someone you’re expecting to start a family with |. Someone you respect very much. You... don’t know if she’s more to you than that, yet ]. Garth breathes a sigh through his nose as he gives his rag one last pass over the glass mug before setting it down and picking up another recently-cleaned-but-still-wet one. "And they’re sentimental about it, I take it," he asks rhetorically. "I get it. At least I won’t be hitting the boys with a project to fix up an entire fortress this time around. It’ll cost you less, too." |You tell Garth that you’re in need of hiring a carpenter, and you figured he was the person to ask about what sort of services you can find in Hawkethorne about it. You imagine there are skilled tradesmen in the village, but they don’t exactly advertise their business. "There’s no need if you’re the only business in town," he laughs. "I don’t need to advertise my rooms or my booze, either." He puts down the glass beer mug that he’s been drying and picks up a recently-washed-but-still-wet one to start on. "Yeah, I know a group. A bunch’a regulars that don’t work the normal hours, but come in every day they’re on a project. If you give me the details, I can pass on that you’re hiring." It’s nothing special – it’d be smaller than any building in Hawkethorne. A shack, out in the Harvest Valley, that’s a bit past its ‘service date.’ It needs repairs: a new roof; new walls; new floor; the whole bag. It’s only got the ground floor and it’s only one room. "What is it, like, a toolshed for that pupper farm or something?" It’s more of a... cottage, you suppose. And it’s not just for you: it’s for someone you know[zo.vaiExists |. Someone you’re expecting to start a family with |. Someone you respect very much. You... don’t know if she’s more to you than that, yet ]. Garth breathes a sigh through his nose; his cleaning stops for a moment as he regards the mug in his hands. "And they’re sentimental about it, I take it," he asks rhetorically. "I get it. Repairing an old house can be trickier than just building a new one, mind, but if it’s really as small as you’re saying it is, it still ought to be an easy in-and-out job that only ought to take a few days." Garth cups his hand underneath the bottom rim of the mug and leans forward, moving the mug behind his back as he regards you over the countertop. "That said," he says, "work ain’t cheap." ]
rows.translation: [wayfort.renovated |你告诉加斯，你又要开始一项木工工作了，需要他再联系一下他的那些人。 “当然可以，”他迅速而简洁地回答道，一边继续认真地清洗他的啤酒杯。“上一次的工作进行得很顺利，而且你给他们的报酬也足够丰厚，他们没有任何怨言。我猜这次也是同一个地方吧？是进行扩建之类的工程吗？” 其实这次的工作是维修性质的，而且涉及的对象也是某个特定的东西…… 相当多 更小一些的那种：一间单间、一层的小屋，面积大概就跟你现在坐的这个酒吧差不多大，位于丰收谷附近的一片树林里，开车只需要几分钟就能到达。这小屋需要重新铺设屋顶，更换窗户，重新铺设地板，而且它的旧门也已经从门框上脱落了。 这工作其实很简单，尤其是和你之前想做的那份工作相比。” “听起来这个地方早就该被扔掉了吧，”他挑了挑眉毛回答，“这算什么地方？是工具间还是别的什么？为什么不干脆建一个新的呢？你可以把它看作是一间小屋吧。而且这间小屋不只是为你准备的，而是为你认识的人准备的。[zo.vaiExists |那个你期望与之共同组建家庭的人 |一个你非常尊敬的人。你……还不知道她对你的意义是否超过了这个程度。 ]加思通过鼻子叹了口气，他用抹布最后擦了擦那个玻璃杯，然后把它放下来，拿起另一个刚洗过但还湿漉漉的杯子。“他们应该是对这个杯子怀有感情吧，”他反问道，“我理解。至少这次我不会让那些孩子们去修理整座堡垒了。这样你们的花费也会少一些。 |你告诉加斯，你需要雇一名木匠，于是你认为他才是最适合咨询在鹰棘镇能找到哪些相关服务的人。你认为村里应该也有技术娴熟的工匠，但他们并不太主动宣传自己的业务。 如果你是镇上唯一的商家，那就没这个必要了，”他笑着说，“我也没必要去宣传自己的房间或酒水。”他放下那个刚刚擦干的啤酒杯，拿起另一个刚洗过但还湿漉漉的杯子，继续喝起酒来。 是的，我认识一个团队。那是一群固定成员，他们并不在常规工作时间工作，但只要有项目在进行，他们就会每天来上班。如果你把详细信息告诉我的话，我可以转达你们正在招聘人员这一消息。” 其实也没什么特别的——那个团队的规模甚至比鹰棘镇的任何一栋建筑都要小。 在丰收谷外有一间小屋，它的使用年限已经差不多到了尽头。这间小屋需要修缮：重新铺设屋顶、重建墙壁、更换地板，总之需要全面翻新。它只有一层楼，而且只有一个房间。 “这间小屋是用来存放那些狗狗的工具吗，还是有什么别的用途？你可以把它看作是一间小屋吧。而且它不仅仅是为你准备的，而是为你认识的人准备的。[zo.vaiExists |那个你期望与之共同组建家庭的人 |一个你非常尊敬的人。你……还不知道她对你的意义是否超越了单纯的尊敬而已。 ]加思通过鼻子叹了口气；他停下手部中的清洁工作，凝视着手部中的那个杯子，问道：“我想，他们对这个房子应该怀有很深的感情吧？”他继续说道，“我理解。修复一座老房子确实比建造一座新房子要复杂一些，但是如果真像你说的那么小，那么这项工作应该也不会太复杂，只需要几天时间就能完成吧。加思将手部放在杯子的下装边缘下方，身体前倾，然后将杯子移到背后，透过柜台看着你说道：“话虽如此，工作可不是便宜的事。 ]

rows.original:
You lift your coin pouch and place it on the counter; its leather sinks into itself as the coins clank and jingle from the impact against the wood. You presume that this ought to cover such a small job. And there’s even some extra in there for his commission – for helping you with your ‘help wanted advertising.’

        He pinches the neck of the pouch between his thumb and index finger and gives the bag a heft. His eyebrows arch – it’s heavier than he expected. "Sure, this’ll be good," he says as he stands upright, tossing the coin pouch somewhere hidden underneath the countertop. "I expect they’ll get started tomorrow."
rows.translation: 你拿出钱袋放在柜台上；皮革在硬币撞击木头发出的叮当声中微微凹陷。你认为这笔钱应该足够支付这么小的费用了，甚至还多出一些，可以用来支付他的佣金——毕竟他帮你发布了那则“招聘帮助”的广告。他用拇指和食指捏住钱袋的袋口，轻轻一提，发现它的重量比他预想的要重。他的眉毛微微一挑，“嗯，这个应该不错。”说着，他站直身体，把那个装硬币的钱袋扔到了柜台下面的某个隐蔽地方。 我预计他们明天就会开始行动了。

        He pinches the neck of the pouch between his thumb and index finger and gives the bag a heft. His eyebrows arch – it’s heavier than he expected. "Sure, this’ll be good," he says as he stands upright, tossing the coin pouch somewhere hidden underneath the countertop. "I expect they’ll get started tomorrow."'

rows.original: When you approach Garth and his eyes meet yours, his brow furrows and he leans forward, crooking one finger at you to approach. Which you were going to do anyway, but now, it almost looks like he’s about to scold you for something. "So, that recent job that you had me get my contacts for," he says, crossing his arms and leaning on the countertop with his elbows. "I’m told it went through without a hitch." You confirm; the house is much better now than you last saw it. A bit small for a conventional house, but at least now you’re not embarrassed to look at it. "Yeah, yeah," he says, trying to hurry the conversation along. "You told me that was a ‘cottage.’ And I’m told it’s currently being squatted in." That’s... correct, too, yes. "You’re aware that that building, out in the grove, was a barracks? And that clearing that it’s in – it was a militant training camp at one point. You knew that, right?" You tell him that, no, you didn’t. A barracks for what army? "Not an army – a mercenary group. I should know. Back in...." He pauses, looking in both directions to make sure that nobody is trying to listen in, and when he continues, it’s with a lowered voice anyway. "Back in my youth, it was an outpost that me and my running used for hideouts. Anyone in the know knew that it was the first place to hide if you were deep in the shit, as it were, and needed to lie low for a while. But even then, it was a run-down and dirty place – good for a stay to let the heat cool off, but not a place worth living." He turns to one side and lowers his gaze. "Now, those days are behind me. I ain’t heard anything about anyone nefarious takin’ up room and board in that rotten little hut. But I also ain’t in the business of helping anyone below-board enough to cause any trouble with me or the locals. This isn’t going to be something I need to worry about, is it?" You reply that you have no idea what he’s talking about. All you know is what you told him: [zo.vaiExists |you and Zo are expecting to start a family and you didn’t want to do it in a house that looked like it was going to collapse if the wind blew in the wrong direction |you knew the squatter staying in the shack and you didn’t want them to live in a house that was infested with termites and looked like it could blow over with a particularly strong gust of wind ]. Garth pauses, searching your eyes for any sign of weakness – signs that you might be lying. "Right," he snorts as he stands back upright. "Well, in any case, my hands are washed clean of it. Whatever happens next doesn’t involve me." And it’s not like Zo can give you her life’s story. ... Can she?
rows.translation: 当你走近加斯时，他的目光与你相遇，他的眉头紧锁，然后他向前倾了倾身子，用一根手部指示意你靠近。其实你本来也是打算这么做的，但此刻，这动作看起来几乎像是在责备你什么。 “那么，你让我去弄那些联系人的那份任务……”他说道，双臂交叉，肘部撑在柜台上，“听说进展得很顺利，没有遇到任何问题。 你确认了一下；这房子现在确实比你上次看到的时候好多了。虽然对于传统意义上的房子来说有点小，但至少现在你看它的时候不会再觉得难看了。 “是啊，是啊，”他说着，试图让谈话快点结束。“你之前说那是一间‘小屋’，而且我听说现在有人在那里面非法居住。 你应该知道，那座位于树林中的建筑曾经是军营吧？而它所处的那片空地，也曾是一个激进分子的训练营地。你应该是知道的，对吧？” 但你却告诉他，你并不知道。那是哪支军队的军营呢？ 不是军队，而是一支雇佣兵组织。我应该知道的……回想当初……”他停顿了一下，四处张望，确保没有人在偷听，然后继续用低声说道：“在我年轻的时候，那是一个我和我的伙伴们经常用来藏身的据点。 任何了解内情的人都知道，如果真的陷入了麻烦，需要暂时躲藏起来，这里就是最好的去处。但即便如此，这个地方也破败不堪、肮脏污秽——虽然适合暂时躲藏以避开麻烦，但根本不适合居住。" 他转向一侧，低下了头。“现在，那些日子已经过去了。我再也没有听说过有什么坏人住在那间破旧的小屋里。但是…… 此外 我可没兴趣以那种偷偷摸摸的方式帮助别人，以免因此给自己或当地人带来麻烦。这种事情根本不需要我担心，对吧？” 你回答说，你完全不明白他在说什么。你只记得自己告诉过他那些事情而已。 [zo.vaiExists |你和佐打算组建家庭，而你们并不想在一个一遇到风吹就会倒塌的房子里开始新生活。 |你明明知道那个住在简陋小屋里的擅自占用他人房屋的人，却不想让他们住在那种被白蚁侵蚀、看起来连一阵大风都能把它吹倒的房子里。 ]加思停顿了一下，注视着你的眼睛，试图从中找出任何软弱的迹象——那些可能表明你在撒谎的信号。“好吧，”他冷哼着，重新站直身体，“无论如何，我已经与这件事毫无关系了。接下来发生的一切都与我无关。” 而且，佐也不可能把她自己的人生故事告诉你吧…… ……真的吗？

rows.original:
When you enter Zo’s grove, the woman herself isn’t difficult to spot: she’s standing on the pathway that intersects her house to her farm to the field in the back of the clearing. She’s facing her newly-repaired house with her hands at her sides and her jaw slightly agape, as if she’s having a hard time believing what she’s seeing.

    You don’t say anything when you enter the grove: you just take your spot beside her, facing the house, admiring the work that you had hired the professionals to do. A part of you is remiss that you didn’t repair the house with her – in retrospect, that sounds like a good way to bond with [zo.vaiExists
        |the mother of your kid
        |your teacher in a way that didn’t involve lessons
    ] – but, honestly, neither of you are carpenters. Even if you had the tools, you’ve never built a house before, even one as small as hers.
    
    But, in the end, Zo’s shack is repaired. The exterior walls are a deep, rich brown, cut from logs that couldn’t have been felled more than two weeks ago. The roof is properly thatched with neat and orderly hay lying atop slanted wooden shingles. And the door on the front is upright and held in place with a pair of large, sturdy hinges – and it even locks properly.
    
    You feel Zo’s right hand reach for your left, her fingers playing along the edge of your wrist. You twist your hand to meet hers, and her fingers intertwine with yours before giving you a squeeze.
    
    You two stand there for a moment, admiring the new look of her house. It’s difficult to believe that, [var0
        |not so long ago
        |even just yesterday
    ], she was living in a derelict shack, the walls infested with termites, the whole thing listing to one side, and the building without a proper door. You get that she lives a monastic life without much in the way of material needs, but she really knew how to take it maybe a little too far.
    
    She leans into you, her head resting on your shoulder. You think to ask her if she’s already seen the inside, but, on second thought, that’s a [pc.isDK
        |stupid
        |silly
    ] question – of course she has. Instead, after another moment of enjoying each other’s company in front of her new house, you ask her if she’ll give you a tour of the inside. It’s a small, one-room cabin, so it shouldn’t take too long.
    
    In response, she steps forward, eagerly pulling on your hand, still tightly held in hers, towards her new home. When she places her hand on the door’s knob, it’s with all the excited energy of a child showing their parent something new that they learned: she twists it both ways, with the bolt audibly clicking out of place both times, before pulling on it and swinging it open. When she lets go of the door, she marvels at how it stays held in place by its hinges, and how she doesn’t have to set it down.
    
    The inside of the cabin is – well, it was never an especially complicated building. It’s the exact same layout: her bed is to the left, east-facing wall. There’s a fire pit with a stone chimney in the southwest corner, just as it was before. And underneath the northern wall’s window is where she keeps her cooking and cleaning tools – a washboard, a tub, and some needle and thread for fixing the rips on her gi.
    
    But the interior of the building is so new that the floorboards don’t creak when you step on them. The interior walls are cut oak, their golden-bronze planks illuminating the interior with a warm glow as natural light bounces off them. The roof isn’t unnaturally slanted, and not a single ray of light makes it through the thatches and the shingles. And... while her bed is still made of hay and grass clippings, she has a real bedframe now.
    
    Despite all the improvements to her home, Zo can’t help but be entranced by the door. The inside of the door has a deadbolt for when she wants some privacy; the door itself closes with a deep, satisfying ‘chunk’ as it slips into place. While you were busy admiring the craftsmanship of her house, she’s spent the whole time playing with the deadbolt, sliding it in and out of place.
    
    In the end, what’s important is that she likes her new house.
rows.translation:
当你走进佐的树林时，那个女人很容易就被发现：她站在那条连接她的房子、农场以及空地后方田野的小路上。她面朝自己刚刚修好的房子，双手部叉腰，下巴微微张开，似乎很难相信自己眼前所看到的一切。

    当你走进那片树林时，你什么也没说，只是站在她身旁，面朝那栋房子，欣赏着那些你聘请专业人士来完成的工作。内心有一部分在责备自己——为什么没有和她一起修缮那栋房子呢？现在想来，那本来是增进彼此感情的好机会啊。 [zo.vaiExists
        |你孩子的母亲
        |以一种并不涉及传统课堂教学的方式来指导你。
    ] – 但说实话，你们俩都不是木匠。即使有工具，你们也从未建造过房子，哪怕是像她那样的小房子。

不过最终，佐的小屋还是被修好了。外墙被涂成了深沉的棕色，那些木材都是在不到两周前砍伐的。 屋顶上覆盖着整齐的干草，这些干草被铺在倾斜的木瓦之上。前门也安装得非常牢固，用一对结实的铰链将其固定住——而且门还能正常锁上。

你感觉到佐的右手部伸向你的左手部，她的手部指轻轻触碰着你手部腕的边缘。 你伸出手部与她的手部相握，她的手部指与你的手部指交织在一起，随后她轻轻捏了捏你的手部。

你们俩站在那里，欣赏着她房子焕然一新的样子。真的很难相信，这一切都是真的…… [var0
        |就在不久前
        |就在昨天
    ]她住在一间破旧的棚屋里，墙壁上布满了白蚁，整个房子都歪向了一边，而且根本没有门。你可以看出，她过着一种近乎苦行僧般的生活，几乎不需要任何物质享受，但她确实把这种生活方式发挥到了极致。

她靠在你的身上，头靠在你的肩膀上。你本来想问她是否已经看过了里面的情况，但转念一想，这个问题或许不太合适…… [pc.isDK
        |愚蠢的
        |愚蠢的
    ] 当然她知道。在她的新房子前又享受了一阵彼此的陪伴之后，你便问她是否愿意带你参观一下房子的内部。那只是一间小单间木屋，所以参观应该不会花太长时间。
    
    作为回应，她向前迈出一步，迫不及待地拉着你的手部，紧紧地握住它，带着无比兴奋的心情，将你引向她的新家。当她把手部放在门把手部上时，那种兴奋劲儿就像一个孩子正在向父母展示自己新学会的东西一样：她来回转动门把手部，每次都能听到锁舌明显地移位，然后她用力一拉，门便打开了。 当她松开门把手部时，她不禁惊叹于门是如何通过合页固定在原位的，也惊讶于自己根本不需要将门放下来。
    
    小屋的内部结构其实并不复杂。布局依然和以前一样：她的床位于左侧，紧靠朝东的墙壁。西南角有一个带石制烟囱的火坑，一切都没有改变。而北墙窗户下方，是她存放烹饪和清洁工具的地方——有一块洗板、一个水盆，还有一些针线，用来修补她战斗服上的破洞。
    
    但这栋建筑的内部装饰极为新潮，以至于你踩在地板上时，地板板条都不会发出嘎吱声。内墙采用的是切割过的橡木材料，那些呈金铜色的木板在自然轻型的照射下，会散发出温暖的轻型芒。屋顶的倾斜角度也非常自然，没有一丝轻型线能够穿透茅草和瓦片。而且……虽然她的床仍然是由干草和草屑铺成的，但她现在终于有一张真正的床架了。
    
    尽管她的家已经进行了种种改造，但佐还是无法抗拒那扇门的魅力。门的内侧装有一个插销，这样在她需要隐私的时候就可以使用；而门本身在关闭时也会发出那种沉闷而令人满意的“咔嗒”声。当你们都在欣赏她家精湛的工艺时，她却一直在摆弄那个插销，不断地把它插进去又拔出来。
    
    最重要的是，她喜欢她的新房子。

But she has so little to her name: even her bed is little more than some hay and grass clippings stuffed together on a pile. |Vai is your bouncing baby boy, full of life and energy – but the crib that Zo whipped together to put him in when he’s tired is barely a higher quality than what she sleeps in, and she sleeps on a pile of cut grass. That’s no way for a child to sleep. ] As soon as you start explaining to Zo that [zo.isPregnant |your baby |Vai ] needs [zo.isPregnant |it’s own |a better ] crib to sleep in, she’s already nodding vigorously enough that her massive hair is bobbing and swinging behind her with the momentum. She agrees wholeheartedly: her decision to sleep on something just barely more than nothing is a conscious one that she made, but [zo.isPregnant |the baby |her son ] both needs and deserves something better than [zo.isPregnant |that |what paltry craftsmanship she’s capable of ]. If you have any ideas or suggestions, she’s already all for it. Well... you’re not much of a craftsman yourself. You’re not much of a builder at all. rows.original: It’s probably not a stretch to suggest to Gwyneth that she knows a thing or two about raising kids. Doing her best to keep a smile from spreading across her face, she scans her eyes across the nursery, looking over everything she’s done to baby-proof the place while still keeping the babies engaged and happy. There are rolls of spare towels off in a distance cupboard; there are changes of baby clothes wrapped up nearby; there are enough toys going around that a kid could go through one toy a day and not have gone through the whole library in a month. "Maybe a thing or two, sure," she says with a light giggle. This might be an unusual request for her, but: what does she know about building cribs? The materials; the instructions; how difficult it is. "I happen to know something about it, certainly," she answers. "Although, it is unusual that you’d ask. Most people aren’t curious enough to learn enough about something like children’s bedding; they usually just ask me to do all the lifting for them, so to speak." Well... you’re looking to start a family, but you and the [silly |missus |mother ] discussed it, and you two decided that you’d rather try raising the kid on your own terms, rather than just moving [zo.isPregnant |it |him ] to Hawkethorne’s nursery. And that includes assembling [zo.isPregnant |its |his ] own bed. "[zo.isPregnant |I take it, from your lack of pronouns, the baby isn’t born yet," she hums. "Which is good! It’s better to be ready for the baby before the baby is ready for you, if you understand me. |I take it, from your specific choice in pronouns, the baby’s already been born," she hums. "Which means you’re lagging behind a little. The crib was something you should have planned ahead for by now. ]" She drums her index finger against her chin as she thinks. "I have the materials to build your own crib from scratch, although it’s only for the frame – you’ll have to find the bedding elsewhere. And I’ve pre-written instructions to be so simple that even the village fool could follow them... provided they’re literate." She just has the instructions to build a crib handy? "They were very useful for when I was just getting used to building them myself," she laughs. "The instructions are free, but I’m afraid the materials aren’t. I don’t skimp on the quality – we’re talking about our baby’s comfort and safety, after all. It’ll cost [gwyn.hasKids |100 electrum... and I should note that that’s at cost. |150 electrum, and I’m afraid I can’t go any cheaper without cutting into my own wallet. ]" If you want to build a crib with Zo, it’ll cost you [gwyn.hasKids |100 |150 ] electrum. A small price to pay, considering this is your baby’s bed that you’re buying.

rows.original:
You tell Gwyneth that she has a deal. You’ll buy her crib and you’ll take her instructions.

        "Excellent. Wait here a moment," she says as a smile spreads across her muzzle. Her tail flicks excitedly behind herself as she walks deeper into the nursery – and only a few seconds later, she comes back with a box with handles punched into its top side. It’s a tall and thin box, and with every step she takes, you can hear the rattle of objects shifting about inside it.
        
        "The instructions are already packaged in there for you," she says as she sets it down and she takes the money from your hands. "Like I said, I’ve written them to be as clear as can be, but if you have any issues, don’t be afraid to come back and ask for help."
        
        You thank Gwyneth for her help as you heft the box in your hands. It’s lighter than you expected it to be.
rows.translation:
你告诉格温妮丝，她有个交易达成啦。你会买她的婴儿床，也会按照她的要求来行事。

“太好了。请在这里稍等片刻，”她笑着说，脸上洋溢着笑容。她兴奋地摇着尾巴，走进婴儿房里去了——几秒钟后，她拿着一个顶部装有提手部的箱子走了出来。 那是一个又高又细的盒子，每当她走动时，都能听到里面物品相互碰撞发出的声响。

“使用说明已经放在里面了，”她一边说，一边把盒子放下来，同时从你手部中接过了钱。 就像我之前说的，我已经把这些说明写得尽可能清晰了，但如果你有任何疑问，随时都可以回来寻求帮助。”

你手部里拿着那个盒子，感谢格温妮丝的帮助。这个盒子比你想象的要轻得多。

As much as it pains you to say, you’ll have to back out of buying the crib for now. You’ll come back to her as soon as you’re ready to spend that kind of money.
 
        "Do hurry," Gwyneth insists. "Something like proper bedding for your child isn’t something that you should tarry on. You wouldn’t spend less on a proper bed for yourself, would you?"
 
        Your first thought was that Zo normally sleeps on a pile of grass, but... you keep that little detail to yourself. You doubt Gwyneth would appreciate that kind of news about the baby’s mom.

You tell Zo that you had gone to the one woman you trusted the most on the topic of baby health, comfort, and security, and she sold you this box: supposedly, a kit containing all the ‘quality’ materials necessary to construct a good crib. And the instructions necessary to put it together. Zo runs her hand along the wooden frame of the box; her mouth curls into a warm smile, knowing that [zo.isPregnant |her baby’s |Vai’s proper ] crib is just one do-it-yourself project away. As her hand feels along the smooth-and-thin frame of the box, her fingers eventually come to yours, leading her hand to rest on top of your own. With a smile and a nod towards the house, you know exactly what she would suggest, if she could: that you get started on it right away. Like they say: there’s no time like the present.

rows.original: The box isn’t very heavy, and you haul it into the house easily[pc.strengthRange 0 5 |, even with someone as... physically diminutive as yourself ]. Cracking it open it a little harder: although the frame is thin and light, it’s sealed tightly and there’s no obvious method to opening it. It takes you and Zo some time and effort, but, eventually, you manage to pry one of the looser ends of the box open and reach for its contents. Inside are a number of oaken frame pieces, all stacked one on top of the other to take up as little space as possible. There are four legs; two sides, comprising of rows of spools connecting two, longer, thinner pieces of wood; a baseboard for the bottom of the crib; and two end pieces, with one of them clearly designated as a headboard. The wood their made of is thick and sturdy, sanded and lightly polished all around to be as aesthetically pleasing as possible, while also so smooth that any baby inside the crib couldn’t possibly get a splinter from it. Also inside the box were a written set of instructions, as Gwyneth had promised – but no pictures. Given the painstaking cursive of the handwriting, it was probably written by Gwyneth herself: the handwriting is beautiful and elegant, but also a bit hard to read. Instruction one was to take the four legs of the crib and slide them onto the corners of the baseboard by following along the grooves carved into the legs. Simple enough. You take one end of the baseboard and two legs, and Zo takes the other. You two make the mistake of working on the same side at the same time, and when you both slide on one leg, the baseboard is several feet off the ground, but all of its weight is shifted to the opposite side, causing it to instantly lose balance and rest diagonally on its baseboard when you let it go. Zo has to hold the whole thing upright for you to slip the third leg on – by then, at least, it’s sturdy enough for her to get the fourth leg on without much trouble. And it’s then that you learn that you were only meant to put on two legs to start with. And they’re both supposed to be on one of the thinner sides of the baseboard, meaning even if you two had stopped at one leg each, you would have put the wrong ones in. Removing the two incorrect legs isn’t hard, but that shows you for not reading ahead. The next step is to slide the endpiece onto the end of the baseboard with the legs; it has a thin groove where the wood of the board can slide into the endpiece, and the piece is specifically and meticulously carved and sanded to fit in between two of the legs. It takes a bit of effort to hold the endpiece in place, since the baseboard is off the ground and one of you needs to hold it at a specific height, and level; once you get the endpiece lined up, Zo pushes and shoves into the baseboard with all her weight to slide it into place. You had expected the other legs to be next, or perhaps the headboard, but the next step is actually to work in the two wall pieces: the pieces with spokes connecting two thinner bits of wood. The principle is the same: there’s a long, thin groove that’s meant to line up with the broad sides of the baseboard, but you’re meant to slot it in from one side all the way down to the other until it fits in snugly against the legs, as opposed to lining them up and forcing them in. And – as you learn too late – the two wall pieces aren’t symmetrical: one piece is specifically meant to slide against one leg. It gives the crib a lopsided look, but the function is meant to be so one side would be easier to look over while the other would prevent the baby from trying to climb it. Once you get the two wall pieces slotted in, then it’s time for the final two legs: again, not such a simple task, since the baseboard only has two legs to stand on and was therefore constantly tipping along its broad side, so you had to lean it upright while Zo hammered in the other two legs herself. And after that, the final piece is the headboard: an expertly-crafted, although not very ornate, piece that slides onto the baseboard the same way the endpiece did – by you holding the crib in place and Zo throwing her weight into it until it’s good and nestled. With that, the crib is completed. It has no decorations and no bedding, but those are things that you handle separately. What you have is a crib made of fine, freshly-cut and specifically-crafted wood, ready to support the weight of a bouncing baby. You wipe the back of your hand along your brow as you take your spot beside Zo, both of you taking a step back to admire your work. You didn’t chop and process the wood or anything, but you still had to assemble it all yourself, and even something as basic as that can be deeply rewarding in its own way – there’s nothing quite like admiring your handiwork after putting in the work to realize it. Your hand wraps around Zo’s waist, your fingers gripping onto her hip, and you feel hers slide along your back and gently tugging on your waist, bringing you closer to her. Zo isn’t typically one for wagging her tail... but she doesn’t try to keep the motion of her hips a secret.
rows.translation: 这个箱子并不重，你很容易就能把它搬进屋里。[pc.strengthRange 0 5 |即使面对像你这样身材如此娇小的人…… ]再用力把它打开一点：虽然这个盒子的框架很薄很轻，但它密封得非常严密，看起来并没有什么明显的打开方法。你和佐花花了一些时间和精力，最终还是设法把盒子的一个边缘撬开了，然后才得以看到里面的东西。 里面装着一些橡木框架部件，它们都被一层层堆放起来，以尽可能节省空间。这个框架共有四条腿：两侧由一排排线轴组成，这些线轴将两块较长且较薄的木头连接在一起；下装则装有底板；另外还有两块端部部件，其中一块被明确标示为床头板。 他们使用的木材质地厚实且坚固，经过打磨和轻微抛轻型处理，既美观大方，表面也十分轻型滑，因此婴儿在婴儿床里绝对不会被木刺扎到。 盒子里还有一份书面说明书，正如格温妮丝所承诺的那样——不过并没有附上任何图片。从那字迹工整、笔迹优美的风格来看，这份说明书很可能是格温妮丝亲自撰写的：字迹确实漂亮优雅，但读起来也有些费劲。 第一个步骤是取婴儿床的四条腿，然后沿着腿上刻好的凹槽，将它们滑到床足部板的四个角上。这个步骤非常简单。 你负责拿床足部板的一端和两条腿，而Zo则负责另外一端和两条腿。 你们两个犯了同一个错误，就是同时从同一侧进行操作。当你们俩都向同一方向移动时，那个底座会离开地面几英尺的高度，但它的所有重量都会转移到另一侧，从而导致它瞬间失去平衡，当你们松开手时，它就会以对角线的姿势落在底座上。 Zo必须先把整个装置撑稳，这样才能帮你安装第三条腿——至少在那个时候，这个装置已经足够稳固了，她可以毫不费力地安装第四条腿。 就在那时，你才会意识到，自己原本只是被安排来扮演这个角色的而已。 两个 首先，你需要准备两根腿。而且这两根腿都应该安装在踢足部线的较窄一侧，也就是说，即使你们每人只拿了一根腿来安装，也会装错位置。拆除这两根装错的腿并不难，但这件事恰恰说明了你们没有事先仔细阅读说明书。 下一步是将末端部件滑到带有腿部的踢足部板的末端；该末端部件上有一条细槽，踢足部板的木头可以滑入这条槽中，而且这个末端部件也是经过精心雕刻和打磨，以便能够恰好卡在两条腿部之间。 要将末端部件固定到位，需要花费一些力气，因为底板是悬空的，所以必须有人将其保持在特定的高度并且确保其处于水平状态；一旦末端部件的位置调整正确，Zo就会用她全部的体重去推挤底板，使其顺利滑入到位。 你原本以为接下来会处理另外那两条腿，或者可能是床头板，但实际上下一步应该先处理那两块墙板——也就是那些带有辐条、用于连接两块较薄木板的部件。制作原理是一样的：这两块墙板上都有一条长而窄的凹槽，这些凹槽应该与床足部板的宽边对齐，但你需要将它们从一侧一直插入到另一侧，直到它们能够紧密地贴合在床腿上，而不是仅仅将它们对齐后再强行插入。 而且——你会在后来才意识到——这两块墙板其实并不对称：其中一块是专门设计用来抵在床架的一条腿上的。这样虽然会让婴儿床看起来有些歪斜，但这种设计的目的其实是让父母可以更轻松地查看婴儿的情况，而另一块墙板则能防止婴儿试图爬出婴儿床。 一旦你将那两块墙板安装到位， 然后 现在是最后两个步骤了：同样，这也不是一个简单的任务。因为床架只有两条腿作为支撑，所以它总是会沿着宽边倾斜，因此你必须把它扶直，而Zo则会负责安装另外两条腿。完成这些步骤后，最后剩下的就是床头板了——这个床头板制作精良，虽然并不十分华丽，但它也是通过同样的方式安装到床架上的：你需要固定住婴儿床的位置，然后Zo再用力将其推到位，直到它稳固地固定在床架上。 就这样，婴儿床就制作完成了。它没有任何装饰，也没有铺好的被褥，但这些都可以另外添加。你现在拥有的是一张由优质木材制成、经过精心切割和加工的婴儿床，它已经准备好承受一个活泼好动的婴儿的体重了。 你用手背擦了擦额头，然后站在佐的身边，两人一起后退几步，欣赏自己的劳动成果。虽然你并没有亲自砍伐或加工木材，但所有的工作还是得你自己来完成。即便只是这样简单的事情，也会带来难以言喻的成就感——当自己付出努力后，能够欣赏到自己的劳动成果，这种感觉确实无与伦比。 你的手环绕在佐的腰间，手指紧握着她的臀部，而你感觉到她的手沿着你的背部轻轻滑动，然后轻轻拉扯着你的腰，将你拉得更靠近她。佐通常并不喜欢这样主动表现……但她也没有试图隐藏自己这种动作。
rows.raw: " The box isn’t very heavy, and you haul it into the house easily[pc.strengthRange 0 5 |, even with someone as... physically diminutive as yourself ]. Cracking it open it a little harder: although the frame is thin and light, it’s sealed tightly and there’s no obvious method to opening it. It takes you and Zo some time and effort, but, eventually, you manage to pry one of the looser ends of the box open and reach for its contents. Inside are a number of oaken frame pieces, all stacked one on top of the other to take up as little space as possible. There are four legs; two sides, comprising of rows of spools connecting two, longer, thinner pieces of wood; a baseboard for the bottom of the crib; and two end pieces, with one of them clearly designated as a headboard. The wood their made of is thick and sturdy, sanded and lightly polished all around to be as aesthetically pleasing as possible, while also so smooth that any baby inside the crib couldn’t possibly get a splinter from it. Also inside the box were a written set of instructions, as Gwyneth had promised – but no pictures. Given the painstaking cursive of the handwriting, it was probably written by Gwyneth herself: the handwriting is beautiful and elegant, but also a bit hard to read. Instruction one was to take the four legs of the crib and slide them onto the corners of the baseboard by following along the grooves carved into the legs. Simple enough. You take one end of the baseboard and two legs, and Zo takes the other. You two make the mistake of working on the same side at the same time, and when you both slide on one leg, the baseboard is several feet off the ground, but all of its weight is shifted to the opposite side, causing it to instantly lose balance and rest diagonally on its baseboard when you let it go. Zo has to hold the whole thing upright for you to slip the third leg on – by then, at least, it’s sturdy enough for her to get the fourth leg on without much trouble. And it’s then that you learn that you were only meant to put on two legs to start with. And they’re both supposed to be on one of the thinner sides of the baseboard, meaning even if you two had stopped at one leg each, you would have put the wrong ones in. Removing the two incorrect legs isn’t hard, but that shows you for not reading ahead. The next step is to slide the endpiece onto the end of the baseboard with the legs; it has a thin groove where the wood of the board can slide into the endpiece, and the piece is specifically and meticulously carved and sanded to fit in between two of the legs. It takes a bit of effort to hold the endpiece in place, since the baseboard is off the ground and one of you needs to hold it at a specific height, and level; once you get the endpiece lined up, Zo pushes and shoves into the baseboard with all her weight to slide it into place. You had expected the other legs to be next, or perhaps the headboard, but the next step is actually to work in the two wall pieces: the pieces with spokes connecting two thinner bits of wood. The principle is the same: there’s a long, thin groove that’s meant to line up with the broad sides of the baseboard, but you’re meant to slot it in from one side all the way down to the other until it fits in snugly against the legs, as opposed to lining them up and forcing them in. And – as you learn too late – the two wall pieces aren’t symmetrical: one piece is specifically meant to slide against one leg. It gives the crib a lopsided look, but the function is meant to be so one side would be easier to look over while the other would prevent the baby from trying to climb it. Once you get the two wall pieces slotted in, then it’s time for the final two legs: again, not such a simple task, since the baseboard only has two legs to stand on and was therefore constantly tipping along its broad side, so you had to lean it upright while Zo hammered in the other two legs herself. And after that, the final piece is the headboard: an expertly-crafted, although not very ornate, piece that slides onto the baseboard the same way the endpiece did – by you holding the crib in place and Zo throwing her weight into it until it’s good and nestled. With that, the crib is completed. It has no decorations and no bedding, but those are things that you handle separately. What you have is a crib made of fine, freshly-cut and specifically-crafted wood, ready to support the weight of a bouncing baby. You wipe the back of your hand along your brow as you take your spot beside Zo, both of you taking a step back to admire your work. You didn’t chop and process the wood or anything, but you still had to assemble it all yourself, and even something as basic as that can be deeply rewarding in its own way – there’s nothing quite like admiring your handiwork after putting in the work to realize it. Your hand wraps around Zo’s waist, your fingers gripping onto her hip, and you feel hers slide along your back and gently tugging on your waist, bringing you closer to her. Zo isn’t typically one for wagging her tail... but she doesn’t try to keep the motion of her hips a secret."

rows.original:
Without the threat of imminent violence the farm actually looks like the calming, pastoral getaway it’s meant to be. There’s a large barn with a small house attached to it, and out in the front is a wooden pen full of sheep — not sheep-girls, as some might expect — beside a series of large tightly-bound preserve barrels. On the pathway leading up to these two buildings is a neatly-polished sign of waxed wood labelled 'Pupperidge Farm' in big, bold letters.

        Off to the side is a container for grains of various kinds, and a well-worn pathway leading back the way you’ve come. All in all, Pupperidge Farm looks like the perfect little enclosed farm for a couple of wolfy shemales and their duo of busty amoozons.
rows.translation:
在没有迫在眉睫的暴力威胁之下，这个农场确实看起来像是一个宁静、田园诗般的度假胜地。那里有一座大谷仓，旁边还建有一间小房子；在谷仓的前面，有一个木制的围栏，里面养着许多羊——当然，这些并不是“羊姑娘”，否则有些人可能会产生这样的误解——而在围栏旁边，还有一排密封良好的腌制品储存桶。 在这两栋建筑通往的道路旁，有一块用蜡擦拭得光亮的木制标志，上面用粗大的字体写着“帕珀里奇农场”。

在标志的旁边，有一个用来存放各种谷物的容器，还有一条磨损严重的小路，可以让你沿着它原路返回。 总而言之，帕珀里奇农场简直就是为那对狼女和她们那对胸部丰满的伙伴们量身打造的理想场所。

rows.original: The smell of fresh cut grass, turned-over soil, and farm animals drifts up to your nose; a little expanse of peaceful nothingness out in the fields. You've wandered up to the edge of an idyllic little farmstead, just off the beaten path. It seems quiet and peaceful, a nice place to take a load off and enjoy a moment's peace in the fertile valley. That moment looks like it’s going to be interrupted, though: you glance out of the corner of your eye as a group of thugs brandishing weapons encroach on it through the fields. These guys' black robes and lurid tattoos are awfully familiar... more of Tollus's goons! A wolf-eared girl with a pitchfork is standing at the farm's gates, ready to hold the vile minions of evil at bay. She sees you on the path and shouts. She's too far for her words to reach you, but the goons all spin around to see the new threat approaching, with readied bows and long knives drawn. It looks like this fight's been chosen for you. [party.som|Sighing, you stand up straight and prepare your own [pc.weapon].|[companion.Name] groans and hefts [companion.hisHer] weapon "Well? Looks like we’ve got to save that farm, [pc.name]."|Your companions ready their own weapons, sharing looks with you. That farm’s hardly going to save itself.] [pc.dcb|"It’s a good day to die!" You shout, watching them charge.|"I’m giving you one chance to run!" You shout, but they seem intent on charging you.|"Oh my gosh! You are all so cute! We’re gonna have fun!"]
rows.translation: 新鲜割下的草、翻动的泥土以及农场动物散发出的气味扑鼻而来；田野里有一片宁静而空旷的区域。你不知不觉地走到了这个远离人迹的宁静小农庄的边缘。 这里看起来宁静而祥和，是这样一个理想的地方，可以让人放松身心，在这片肥沃的山谷中享受片刻的宁静。 然而，这个宁静的时刻似乎就要被打破了：你瞥了一眼，发现一群手持武器的暴徒正从田野中逼近过来。 这些家伙穿着黑色长袍，身上还有那些醒目的纹身，看起来实在太熟悉了……他们肯定是托卢斯的打手！ 一个长着狼耳、手里拿着干草叉的女孩站在农场的门口，准备阻挡那些邪恶的走狗们前进的脚步。 她在小路上看到了你，便大声呼喊起来。由于距离太远，她的声音无法传达到你那里，但那些恶棍们立刻转过身来，警惕地注视着这个新出现的威胁——他们早已拔出了弓和长刀，准备迎战。看来这场战斗是专门为你准备的啊。 [party.som|你叹了口气，站直身体，开始准备自己该做的事情。 [pc.weapon].|[companion.Name] 呻吟着，费力地移动着 [companion.hisHer] 武器：“嗯？看来我们得去拯救那个农场了…… [pc.name]."|你的同伴也拿出了自己的武器，与你对视着。那个农场，恐怕是自保无望了。] [pc.dcb|今天正是赴死的好日子！”你大喊着，看着他们冲了过来。|我给你一次逃跑的机会！”你大声喊道，但他们似乎决心要冲向你。|天啊！你们所有人都太可爱了！我们一定会…… 有趣!"]

rows.original:
The last of the cultists still standing stumbles back, dropping his weapon. "Fuck it... retreat. Back to the camp!" He and his fellows go running to the west, kicking up dust in their wake that lets them escape in safety.

    Now that the cultists are all chased off you can get a proper look at the place... and your damsel in distress. 
    
    For all intents and purposes you’re looking at a farm. There’s a great big pen full of fluffy sheep, a large barn with a building glued to the back of it, and a homely-looking farmhouse. Your damsel however looks a decent amount less innocent, thanks to the way she’s eyeing you up-and-down after a demonstration of your martial prowess. That expression changes into an innocent eyelash-fluttering when she notices your attention however.
    
    She has long pointed wolf-like ears; brown and highlighted with orange fluff. They sprout from the top of neatly-braided brown hair tied up into a bun at the back. A human face smiles at you with bright blue eyes, and a cute button nose rests above soft kissable lips. The only evidence of a blemish on her is a smattering of freckles, and even they seem to be adding to the adorable facial-structure. There’s little of her left to the imagination, thanks to the fact that the girl’s in nothing but a pair of overalls; the straps just barely manage to obscure the broad cherry-like nipples adorning the pale flesh of DD-cup breasts. A great big bushy tail of brown fur with yet more orange highlights wags from behind her hard enough to set her massive hips to swaying... and a large tent in her clothing reveals the pup’s packing something a little extra. She was evidently some kind of human, judging by the way her legs are plantigrade and her bare feet are fleshy... perhaps the works of alchemy.
    
    "Hey hero, you sure came by at a perfect time. Wouldn’t want one of those brutes to go running off with my girls."
    
    "Your girls? I can’t believe they’d hunt your daughters..."
    
    She scoffs, waving her hand. "Daughters? No, no. Unless I squeeze out cow-girls from m’butt! No, this here’s a cow-girl farm. Y’know — big, tall, squishy girls with big boobs and a penchant to moo and wear togas?"
    
    Ah, the minotaur variety of cow-girl as opposed to a rancher. That makes about as much sense as anything else around here you guess. A quick peep down into the nearby pen is enough to blessedly reassure you they’ve not got sheeple curled up down there at least. She doesn’t seem to notice, bouncing over to you and grabbing an arm. "The name’s Anna by the way. Thanks for the help. Do ya... want to come say hi to my sisters and see the farm? I’m sure everyone’d be stoked something fierce after hearing how you saved their soft little butts while they were busy."
    
    Alright, you’ll bite. No doubt the activities on a 'cow-girl farm' are going to be more than a little lurid... hopefully you won’t need some form of wet-weather clothing. "Come on! I can show you where the magic happens!" she insists, orangey-red tail wagging up a furious storm. Even as you both approach the barn there’s the soft sound of 'Moo' on the wind. Pheromones dump their lusty payload into the air the moment the wolf-girl before you tugs open the sliding door...
    
    And it’s not entirely what you expected. Aside from the cylindrical amphora resting flush with the barn’s eastern wall, there’s nothing remotely farm-like or milky about this room. The center of the building is occupied by a large table with a cups of tea and plates of food, and up against the opposite walls are a series of broad, comfy-looking beds. Your guide — sensing your confusion — claps a fluffy paw on your shoulder. "Hey, this really is where the magic happens, hero. Milking’s done by hand, but everyone knows a good pup dines a lady first!"
    
    It’s almost unsettling just how comfortable and cozy the room is considering it’s a giant barn, although the pup seems nonplussed. She waves towards the back of the barn and at the adjacent door. "They all live in a bunk-room back there... judging by the fact that my sister is absent at the moment it probably means they’re otherwise occup—"
    
    She’s cut off by an abnormally loud cross between a howl and a moo, deep and lusty enough to start stealing precious blood away from your brain. "Occupied," she finishes. "But hey, who am I to judge? Oh! If I call in a girl who’s not been milked, perhaps you’d like to help? It’s the least we could do."
    
    Anywhere else, being offered the chance to work hardly seems like ample reward for fighting off invaders... but here, that's probably anything but the case. With all the heat in your body making its way crotchward (not to mention the thought of a free meal if that table’s available) it sounds nearly too good to be true.
    
    What’ll it be?
rows.translation:
最后一名还站着的邪教徒踉跄着后退，手中的武器也掉在了地上。“去他的……撤退吧，回营地！”他和他的同伴们向西跑去，他们身后扬起的尘土帮助他们安全地逃走了。

现在那些邪教徒都被赶走了，你可以仔细看看这个地方了……还有你那位处于危险中的少女。 
    
    从任何角度来看，这里都像是一个农场。有一大片围栏，里面养着许多毛茸茸的羊；还有一个大谷仓，后面还建着一栋小房子；此外，还有一座看起来很朴实的农舍。不过，那位小姐在见识了你的武艺之后，那副天真无邪的表情已经荡然无存了——她正用充满好奇的目光打量着你呢。不过，当她注意到你在看她时，她的表情又立刻变回了那种天真无邪、睫毛轻轻颤动的样子。
    
    她长着一对像狼一样的耳朵，棕色耳朵上点缀着橙色的绒毛。这些耳朵从她背后扎成发髻的棕色头发顶端伸出来。一张人类的脸庞正对着你微笑，那双明亮的蓝眼睛，以及那个可爱的小鼻子，都位于那柔软、令人想要亲吻的嘴唇上方。 她身上唯一的“瑕疵”就是那几颗雀斑，而它们似乎反而为她那迷人的五官增添了几分特色。由于这个女孩只穿着一套工装裤，几乎没有什么地方可以让人发挥想象力了——那些几乎被背带完全遮住的、呈樱桃状的乳头，清晰地显现在她那淡粉色的肌肤上。 她身后摇摆着一条又大又浓密的棕色尾巴，尾巴上还带着一些橙色的斑纹，这种晃动幅度之大，甚至让她那宽大的臀部也开始随之摆动……而她衣服上的一个大口袋则暴露出，这只小狗还带着一些额外的东西。 从她用足部掌行走的方式以及她那没有指甲、肉色裸露的足部来看，她显然属于人类……或许这是炼金术的成果吧。
    
    嘿，英雄，你来得真是恰到好处。我可不想让那些野蛮人把我的女儿们抢走。”

“你的女儿们？我简直不敢相信他们会去追捕你的女儿们……”

她嗤之以鼻，挥了挥手说：“女儿们？才不是呢！除非我屁股里能长出女牛仔来……不，这里其实是一个女牛仔农场。你知道的——那些高大、丰满的女孩，胸部很大，还喜欢哞哞叫，还总是穿着长袍……
    
    啊，这种牛女角色其实更像是弥诺陶洛斯之类的生物，而不是真正的牧场主。不过，说实话，这种设定在这里也挺合理的吧。只要快速瞥一眼附近的围栏，你就会放心了——至少那里并没有羊群蜷缩着休息。 她似乎没有注意到这一点，蹦蹦跳跳地走到你跟前，抓住了你的手臂。“顺便说一下，我叫安娜。谢谢你的帮助。你……愿意来跟我姐姐们打个招呼，看看农场吗？我相信，听到你在他们忙得不可开交的时候保护了她们，大家一定会非常高兴的。"
    
    好吧，你肯定会感兴趣的。在这样一个“牧女农场”里进行的各种活动，肯定会相当有趣……不过希望你不会需要什么防雨衣物吧。“来吧！我带你去看看那些神奇的事情发生的地方！”她坚持说道，那橙红色的尾巴在狂风中欢快地摇动着。当你们俩走向谷仓的时候，风中传来了“哞哞”的牛叫声。当那个狼人女孩拉开滑动门的一刹那，各种信息素立刻散发到空气中……
    
    不过，实际情况并不完全如你所料。除了那个与谷仓东墙平齐放置的圆柱形双耳瓶之外，这个房间里没有任何与农场或牛奶相关的元素。建筑物的中央摆放着一张大桌子，上面摆着茶杯和食物；而在对面的墙壁上，则排列着一系列宽大、看起来非常舒适的床铺。 你的向导察觉到了你的困惑，便用它那毛茸茸的爪子轻拍了一下你的肩膀：“嘿，英雄，真正的魔法就在这里发生的。挤奶是手工完成的，但大家都知道，一只乖巧的小狗总会先喂饱它的女主人！
    
    考虑到这其实是一个巨大的谷仓，这个房间竟然如此舒适惬意，简直让人觉得有些不可思议。不过那只小狗似乎对此并不在意。她朝谷仓的后部以及旁边那扇门指了指：“他们全都住在那里的集体宿舍里……看我姐姐现在不在，大概意味着他们现在都在别的地方吧……
    
    她的声音被一种介于嚎叫与哞声之间的、异常刺耳的声音打断了——那种声音如此低沉、如此激昂，简直会抢走你大脑中的宝贵精力。“正在忙呢，”她终于说道，“不过嘛，我有什么资格评判别人呢？哦！如果我叫来一个还没被挤过奶的女孩，也许你会愿意帮忙吧？这也是我们最起码能做的吧。
    
    在其他地方，能够获得工作机会似乎远远不足以作为击退入侵者的回报……但在这里，情况很可能完全不同。当你全身的热量都往下半身聚集时（更不用说如果那张桌子还有空位，还能免费吃到一顿饭的念头），这种机会听起来简直好得令人难以置信。
    
    你想点什么？
rows.raw:
'
    The last of the cultists still standing stumbles back, dropping his weapon. "Fuck it... retreat. Back to the camp!" He and his fellows go running to the west, kicking up dust in their wake that lets them escape in safety.

    Now that the cultists are all chased off you can get a proper look at the place... and your damsel in distress. 
    
    For all intents and purposes you’re looking at a farm. There’s a great big pen full of fluffy sheep, a large barn with a building glued to the back of it, and a homely-looking farmhouse. Your damsel however looks a decent amount less innocent, thanks to the way she’s eyeing you up-and-down after a demonstration of your martial prowess. That expression changes into an innocent eyelash-fluttering when she notices your attention however.
    
    She has long pointed wolf-like ears; brown and highlighted with orange fluff. They sprout from the top of neatly-braided brown hair tied up into a bun at the back. A human face smiles at you with bright blue eyes, and a cute button nose rests above soft kissable lips. The only evidence of a blemish on her is a smattering of freckles, and even they seem to be adding to the adorable facial-structure. There’s little of her left to the imagination, thanks to the fact that the girl’s in nothing but a pair of overalls; the straps just barely manage to obscure the broad cherry-like nipples adorning the pale flesh of DD-cup breasts. A great big bushy tail of brown fur with yet more orange highlights wags from behind her hard enough to set her massive hips to swaying... and a large tent in her clothing reveals the pup’s packing something a little extra. She was evidently some kind of human, judging by the way her legs are plantigrade and her bare feet are fleshy... perhaps the works of alchemy.
    
    "Hey hero, you sure came by at a perfect time. Wouldn’t want one of those brutes to go running off with my girls."
    
    "Your girls? I can’t believe they’d hunt your daughters..."
    
    She scoffs, waving her hand. "Daughters? No, no. Unless I squeeze out cow-girls from m’butt! No, this here’s a cow-girl farm. Y’know — big, tall, squishy girls with big boobs and a penchant to moo and wear togas?"
    
    Ah, the minotaur variety of cow-girl as opposed to a rancher. That makes about as much sense as anything else around here you guess. A quick peep down into the nearby pen is enough to blessedly reassure you they’ve not got sheeple curled up down there at least. She doesn’t seem to notice, bouncing over to you and grabbing an arm. "The name’s Anna by the way. Thanks for the help. Do ya... want to come say hi to my sisters and see the farm? I’m sure everyone’d be stoked something fierce after hearing how you saved their soft little butts while they were busy."
    
    Alright, you’ll bite. No doubt the activities on a 'cow-girl farm' are going to be more than a little lurid... hopefully you won’t need some form of wet-weather clothing. "Come on! I can show you where the magic happens!" she insists, orangey-red tail wagging up a furious storm. Even as you both approach the barn there’s the soft sound of 'Moo' on the wind. Pheromones dump their lusty payload into the air the moment the wolf-girl before you tugs open the sliding door...
    
    And it’s not entirely what you expected. Aside from the cylindrical amphora resting flush with the barn’s eastern wall, there’s nothing remotely farm-like or milky about this room. The center of the building is occupied by a large table with a cups of tea and plates of food, and up against the opposite walls are a series of broad, comfy-looking beds. Your guide — sensing your confusion — claps a fluffy paw on your shoulder. "Hey, this really is where the magic happens, hero. Milking’s done by hand, but everyone knows a good pup dines a lady first!"
    
    It’s almost unsettling just how comfortable and cozy the room is considering it’s a giant barn, although the pup seems nonplussed. She waves towards the back of the barn and at the adjacent door. "They all live in a bunk-room back there... judging by the fact that my sister is absent at the moment it probably means they’re otherwise occup—"
    
    She’s cut off by an abnormally loud cross between a howl and a moo, deep and lusty enough to start stealing precious blood away from your brain. "Occupied," she finishes. "But hey, who am I to judge? Oh! If I call in a girl who’s not been milked, perhaps you’d like to help? It’s the least we could do."
    
    Anywhere else, being offered the chance to work hardly seems like ample reward for fighting off invaders... but here, that's probably anything but the case. With all the heat in your body making its way crotchward (not to mention the thought of a free meal if that table’s available) it sounds nearly too good to be true.
    
    What’ll it be?
    
    '

rows.original:
Anna’s ears droop a little and she pouts at you. "Aww. Are y’sure, hero?" 

        With a nod, you insist it’s okay. You’re glad she and hers are okay, but for now you’d rather hit the road before it gets too late for you. After a moment’s consideration the pup nods a few times before pulling you into a hug, squishing herself against your [pc.chest]. "Well okay. But come on back y’hear? We make the best food and drink in the Marches, and I'll give ya friend's pricing on anything ya want!"
        
        After assuring her that you’ll definitely be back, she lets you go with a small smile and a slow tail-wag.

安娜的耳朵微微耷拉下来，她撅着嘴看着你：“哎呀，你确定吗，英雄？” 

你点了点头，表示没有问题。你很高兴她和她的家人都平安无事，但眼下你还是想尽快上路，以免耽误时间。过了一会儿，小狗也点了点头，然后紧紧地抱住了你，把身体紧紧贴在你的身上。 [pc.chest]好吧，那行。不过你一定要回来哦？我们在这个地区做的食物和饮料是最棒的，你想买什么，我都会给你朋友同样的价格！”

在向你保证一定会回来之后，她微笑着，还慢悠悠地摇着尾巴，让你离开了。

rows.original: With an offer like that, how could you possibly say no? "Excellent!" Anna announces, pushing you to the center of the room to grab a seat before making her way to the back door. Shrugging, you plant yourself down at the table and discover the very middle of it has been hollowed out... Is that a grill? No way... You’re not given a chance to investigate properly before Anna’s bounding over and diving underneath the table. "They’re just coming! Hold up a sec!" The only part of Anna you can see is her great bushy tail wagging, but there’s a little grope at your nethers and a giggle. "Ooooh, they’re gonna love you." She doesn’t elaborate any further, instead there’s some rustling and the sound of flint striking before the table’s core is lit with a warm orange glow and a woodsmoke scent that has your stomach grumbling in anticipation. Anna pops back out into view again "Our table is a fucking grill, how sweet is that shit?!" It is really fucking sweet, but you play it cool. "Really nice, how does it work?" "Not a damn clue! It came with Gloria and Lucia! Ah— the cow girls. They said they got it from a gargoyle in a magic wagon. Which sounds like total bullshit but the table's too cool to question!" She doesn’t really seem to be stopping to take a breath, but she’s blessedly interrupted by the back door opening. Okay, wow. You’re immediately reminded of the massive muscular minotaurs you’ve heard about. They must each be seven foot tall, with abdomens you could grind meat on... in more than one sense. The first has dark sun-kissed skin, and blonde hair in plaits all the way down one of her shoulders. She’s also completely naked, revealing tits that must be H-cups or some other questionably hard-to-measure size, capped with shining dusky nipples. Whatever isn’t rock-hard muscle is a broad fuckable curve that begs to be held onto, and her cunt is a tight-looking slit with a neatly-trimmed bush. A tiny golden ring adorns her hood, bouncing gently with each heavy, tit-quaking step. It’s also just about possible to make out a swinging tail from above a muscular rear, capped with an adorable blonde paintbrush-poof. "Greetings!" she smiles, "I am Gloria. You must be our 'hero'?" "Yeah, [pc.heShe] kicked some bandit ass!" Anna barks, tail wagging again. You’re suddenly not so sure they needed the help, but she sketches a deep bow all the same and thumps a fist to her squishy chest in salute. "Our deepest thanks! You are most welcome here at any time." Coming from her, the permission seems more... official, than your bouncy, fluffy friend’s own offer. The other cow-girl steps into view after, with equally incomprehensible tracts of land and muscle. As opposed to her companion though, her hair is a mess of deeply ginger ringlets, as is the poof at the tip of her tail, and every inch of flesh is paler and adorned with freckles reminiscent of the ones smattering Anna’s nose and cheekbones. "And I am Lucia! Thank you oh-so-much!" Her voice is a little lighter and more bubbly, but she offers a similar bow and salute to her sister, before hefting out a sack that even from here smells smokey and meaty against the natural fuck-funk of the air... Speaking of, now that they’re out in the open you’re fairly certain they give off something special. [pc.hasCock|If you were any harder you’d be lifting their special table with raw dick-strength alone.|That heated itching sensation building up in your core seems to redouble with its insistence.] They take seats at the table too, and Gloria tenderly pours cups of tea while Lucia begins pulling out actual slabs of steak... holy fuck it smells good. She grabs a dagger, slices off neat hunks and drops them onto the now-hot central grill, wriggling happily at the immediate sizzle and scent of cooking meat. "It is good to have company," Lucia adds, bringing her hands together in a way that only serves to squish her impossibly huge tits ever further. You’re pretty sure you can actually see milk beading on her cute pink nips. "Oh, and Morwen will be out soon! We... were distracted." Anna giggles, reaching over to flip the meat on the grill to deliver another satisfying hiss and sizzle. "Sure, distracted balls-deep perhaps. I hope she wasn’t milking you back there." "N-no! Of course not, we would not waste our bounty so!" "Pffft, I know how you get," Anna teases, handing out tiny plates while you sip from the teacup offered by the other muscular moo-cow. It’s a rich and sweet flavor compared to the smokey meats grilling. They move in a strange synchronicity, plucking up little sweet slices of grilled meat and serving them onto each other’s plates. It takes you a moment to catch up, but the bright smile you get from Anna is reward enough when you dish out a slice of grilled goodness for her. The fluffy pup leans against one of your arms with a cheerful little noise as she settles into eating. There’s never really a chance for a proper 'family-meal' vibe to settle in thanks to another form staggering her way out of the back door before you even get a chance to start eating. "Hey, I made it, don’t eat without me!" she whines, scampering over. Again you’re kept from taking a bite by your hand being claimed by the newcomer. Where Anna’s own fur is dark brown with highlights of orange, this girl’s own — Morwen, you’re pretty sure they said — reminds you of the husky colors of Gwyn back in town. Her attributes are similarly curvaceous and wolfy, and a bulge belies the presence of prick behind her overalls, but her fur is the combination of dark on the inner-layers and frosted with grays and whites throughout. Her skin is similarly pale but where Anna’s eyes are a midnight blue, Morwen’s are the pale blue-white of a frozen pond. She also looks somewhat exhausted, glistening with a sheen of post-coital effort. You slide her your plate before there’s a chance for the food to grow cold, earning a thankful little whine. Anna serves you another dishload with a wink, and finally you can dig in. It’s heaven, utter heaven. The grilled beef melts and breaks apart, filling you with a comforting warmth that could see you sleeping through the coldest nights. Morwen at least waits for you to wolf down a few slices before speaking up, through a mouthful of her own food, "Thanks for doing us a real solid, we had no idea bandits turned up! Otherwise I totally would’ve come and kicked some ass!" You humor her with a smile before more food is laid out on the grill. For perhaps a delightful half hour, time passes without threat or worry. Just a peaceful meal where the only sounds are that of you and your new friends chewing and making happy noises at particularly perfect slices. It feels all-too-sadly-soon when the last of the prepared food is cooked and eaten, but you’re finally sated. A glance around the table shows similarly pleased wagging dog-tails and wriggling cow-poofs. Anna is the first to speak up, having returned to leaning on your shoulder and giving you a dosage of diabetes-inducing sweet-eyes. "You’re good company, hero, but I think I offered you the chance to help out around the farm! Our cows are fed, and it’s time for a milking!" Smiling, you haul yourself up and away from the table. Anna yelps as her head-rest is suddenly absent, catching herself while the other girls giggle. Morwen looks amongst the lot of you, adjusting the bulge in her pants. "In that case, unless you need me I'm going to take this opportunity to score a nap. Otherwise I guess I'll send some of the other sisters down." They have more sisters? This place is swiftly becoming your favorite anything that ever was something. Alas, Anna turns the offer down, directing you to a bed while she fetches a number of pails. It looks like the tanned blonde moo Gloria is the first to thread an arm through your own... [pc.heightRange 0 72 |albeit she has to crouch a little, and the effort has a heaving milky teat smashed into your face. It’s hard to say if she even notices it’s her fault.|and pulling your face straight into her massive bosom.] "Oh? Getting a little frisky already are we? And how is it that you would like to have me?" You weren’t aware there were options.

rows.raw: ' With an offer like that, how could you possibly say no? "Excellent!" Anna announces, pushing you to the center of the room to grab a seat before making her way to the back door. Shrugging, you plant yourself down at the table and discover the very middle of it has been hollowed out... Is that a grill? No way... You’re not given a chance to investigate properly before Anna’s bounding over and diving underneath the table. "They’re just coming! Hold up a sec!" The only part of Anna you can see is her great bushy tail wagging, but there’s a little grope at your nethers and a giggle. "Ooooh, they’re gonna love you." She doesn’t elaborate any further, instead there’s some rustling and the sound of flint striking before the table’s core is lit with a warm orange glow and a woodsmoke scent that has your stomach grumbling in anticipation. Anna pops back out into view again "Our table is a fucking grill, how sweet is that shit?!" It is really fucking sweet, but you play it cool. "Really nice, how does it work?" "Not a damn clue! It came with Gloria and Lucia! Ah— the cow girls. They said they got it from a gargoyle in a magic wagon. Which sounds like total bullshit but the table's too cool to question!" She doesn’t really seem to be stopping to take a breath, but she’s blessedly interrupted by the back door opening. Okay, wow. You’re immediately reminded of the massive muscular minotaurs you’ve heard about. They must each be seven foot tall, with abdomens you could grind meat on... in more than one sense. The first has dark sun-kissed skin, and blonde hair in plaits all the way down one of her shoulders. It’s also just about possible to make out a swinging tail from above a muscular rear, capped with an adorable blonde paintbrush-poof. "Greetings!" she smiles, "I am Gloria. You must be our 'hero'?" "Yeah, [pc.heShe] kicked some bandit ass!" Anna barks, tail wagging again. You’re suddenly not so sure they needed the help, but she sketches a deep bow all the same and thumps a fist to her squishy chest in salute. "Our deepest thanks! You are most welcome here at any time." Coming from her, the permission seems more... official, than your bouncy, fluffy friend’s own offer. The other cow-girl steps into view after, with equally incomprehensible tracts of land and muscle. As opposed to her companion though, her hair is a mess of deeply ginger ringlets, as is the poof at the tip of her tail, and every inch of flesh is paler and adorned with freckles reminiscent of the ones smattering Anna’s nose and cheekbones. "And I am Lucia! Thank you oh-so-much!" Her voice is a little lighter and more bubbly, but she offers a similar bow and salute to her sister, before hefting out a sack that even from here smells smokey and meaty against the natural fuck-funk of the air... Speaking of, now that they’re out in the open you’re fairly certain they give off something special. [pc.hasCock|If you were any harder you’d be lifting their special table with raw dick-strength alone.|That heated itching sensation building up in your core seems to redouble with its insistence.] They take seats at the table too, and Gloria tenderly pours cups of tea while Lucia begins pulling out actual slabs of steak... holy fuck it smells good. She grabs a dagger, slices off neat hunks and drops them onto the now-hot central grill, wriggling happily at the immediate sizzle and scent of cooking meat. "It is good to have company," Lucia adds, bringing her hands together in a way that only serves to squish her impossibly huge tits ever further. You’re pretty sure you can actually see milk beading on her cute pink nips. "Oh, and Morwen will be out soon! We... were distracted." Anna giggles, reaching over to flip the meat on the grill to deliver another satisfying hiss and sizzle. "Sure, distracted balls-deep perhaps. I hope she wasn’t milking you back there." "N-no! Of course not, we would not waste our bounty so!" "Pffft, I know how you get," Anna teases, handing out tiny plates while you sip from the teacup offered by the other muscular moo-cow. It’s a rich and sweet flavor compared to the smokey meats grilling. They move in a strange synchronicity, plucking up little sweet slices of grilled meat and serving them onto each other’s plates. It takes you a moment to catch up, but the bright smile you get from Anna is reward enough when you dish out a slice of grilled goodness for her. The fluffy pup leans against one of your arms with a cheerful little noise as she settles into eating. There’s never really a chance for a proper 'family-meal' vibe to settle in thanks to another form staggering her way out of the back door before you even get a chance to start eating. "Hey, I made it, don’t eat without me!" she whines, scampering over. Again you’re kept from taking a bite by your hand being claimed by the newcomer. Where Anna’s own fur is dark brown with highlights of orange, this girl’s own — Morwen, you’re pretty sure they said — reminds you of the husky colors of Gwyn back in town. Her attributes are similarly curvaceous and wolfy, and a bulge belies the presence of prick behind her overalls, but her fur is the combination of dark on the inner-layers and frosted with grays and whites throughout. Just a peaceful meal where the only sounds are that of you and your new friends chewing and making happy noises at particularly perfect slices. It feels all-too-sadly-soon when the last of the prepared food is cooked and eaten, but you’re finally sated. A glance around the table shows similarly pleased wagging dog-tails and wriggling cow-poofs. Anna is the first to speak up, having returned to leaning on your shoulder and giving you a dosage of diabetes-inducing sweet-eyes. [pc.heightRange 0 72 |albeit she has to crouch a little, and the effort has a heaving milky teat smashed into your face. Anna smiles and bounces on her heels, leading you outside and towards the barn. After a few moments she returns with a big thick brush and some strong metal clippers. "Want to shear the sheepies? Because the weather is super inconsistent around here we don’t do one big yearly shear, instead we brush them and clip them down to a half-coat."

            Her tail wags and she places the tools in your hands. "Come on, I’ll teach you how it’s done. It’s super easy, and the sheep love it since they get brushies." Anna plucks up a wooden stool and places it down in the middle of the sheep pen, grinning at the crowd that immediately forms around you both. You give one baa’ing member of the flock a pet on the head and it takes position between your knees with a surprising amount of patience. "It helps that it’s been getting warmer recently, they’re eager." 

            She shows you how to shear the first few sheep, and they’re delightfully placid except for the odd one that tries to nibble your [pc.hasTail|tail|bum]. Once she’s sure that you know what you’re doing, Anna sets around the farm feeding the various animals. The rusty red pup stops by every now and again to scoop up the wool that you shear — and sneaks a quick smooch off of you too each time — until at last the sheep have left in their half-shorn state to go and eat.

            After that you make sure each sheep is neatly brushed so that their coat grows in without being overly tangled, and then Morwen turns up. "Brushies? I do love brushies!"

            You yelp in surprise when the husky-toned wolf girl nudges you back into your shearing seat and sits on your knee, wagging her tail at you. "Come on! I got all messy while sweeping up the barn and pathways!" With a snort you roll your eyes and brush her tail down, although it requires you to pin the wagging appendage in place every time it tries to escape.

            When Anna arrives she huffs and plants her hands on her broad hips, looking you both over. "I take it you’ve finished your work?" 

            Morwen bashfully wriggles in your lap before giving you a squeeze and running away. "Basically!"

            The red-headed wolf girl rolls her eyes and helps you to your feet again, eyeing your sheeply handiwork and inspecting you closely before returning her attention to you.

            "Not bad at all!" Anna announces, helping you scrub wool off of yourself. The sweat and grime of working has you feeling definitively itchy, but you’re hoping it will pass soon. No wonder the girls wear cute overalls all day. "Say Hero. Woould... you fancy joining me for a bath?"
